articles.title: Kapunan: Impeachment issues repetitive because ‘truth is never new’
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The issues raised in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial — like the youth summits used to justify the use of confidential funds (CF) — only appear to be repetitive…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The issues raised in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial — like the youth summits used to justify the use of confidential funds (CF) — only appear to be repetitive because the truth doesn’t change, lawyer Lorna Kapunan said on Tuesday.

Kapunan, a member of the prosecution panel, was asked about observations from netizens that the testimony of Philippine Army (PA) Col. Manaros Boransing II regarding the Department of Education (DepEd) use of Army-funded programs to justify its CF was not new.

Boransing reiterated before the Senate Impeachment Court that both the Youth Leadership Summit (YLS) and the Information Education Campaign (IEC) used allocations under the PA and not CF or regular funds of DepEd under Duterte or the Office of the Vice President (OVP). This, however, was already revealed in a 2024 congressional inquiry before the House of Representatives.
“Well, there is nothing new because the truth is never new, the truth is always the truth,” Kapunan said in an ambush interview while the impeachment court took a break.
“The truth being the testimony in the House showed that the confidential funds were not used for this, and that was just affirmed,” she added.
Kapunan also stressed that even if the matter was already covered in the House, it should be brought up before the Senate Impeachment Court because the House proceedings were not the trial proper.

“No, because this is the court, this is the Senate Impeachment Court. The House was not a Senate impeachment (court), the House was not a mini-trial. The (proceedings in the) House were a house committee (investigation)… in aid of legislation,” she explained.
“Ito naman ang (This one is the) impeachment court, this is the proper venue for presenting documents,” she added.

During the trial on Tuesday, Boransing said that PA did not receive any CF or regular funds from DepEd under Duterte, OVP, or even the Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group (VPSPG) for the implementation of the YLS and the IEC — two anti-communist recruitment initiatives of the Army.

Boransing’s answer was prompted by the question of counsel for the prosecution Reynaldo Robles, as the DepEd under Duterte cited the YLS and the IEC as activities that would justify the use of their CFs in 2023.

But Robles’ inquiry was similar to the questions thrown at Boransing and other PA officials who attended an October 17, 2024, House committee on good government and public accountability hearing. It was a congressional inquiry on the alleged anomalous use of CFs within Duterte’s offices.

During that hearing, Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro — who eventually became the lead public prosecutor for the impeachment — observed that DepEd under Duterte made it seem that they used P15.54 million of its CF in 2023 for the two programs when it was the Army and local government units who shouldered the expenses.

When Boransing said that they used their own funds, Luistro asked retired Education Undersecretary and Maj. Gen. Nolasco Mempin if it was true that DepEd did not allocate funds for the YLS since it is an AFP program.
Mempin replied in the affirmative.

Also, Luistro was able to solicit a confirmation from the Commission on Audit (COA) that the acknowledgement receipts used by DepEd to show how the P15.54 million CF was spent pointed towards the YLS.
However, DepEd labeled this disbursement as rewards to informers.

Boransing and other PA officials told the House panel that they would have not given DepEd certifications for the YLS if they knew that DepEd would use it to justify confidential expenses for reward of informants.
Boransing is the eighth witness presented by the prosecution for Article I of the Articles of Impeachment, or the allegations that the CFs for Duterte’s offices were misused.

Prior to Boransing, the prosecution panel presented two Land Bank of the Philippines officials from which OVP and DepEd withdrew their CFs; COA auditors who checked on the offices’ confidential expenditures; and OVP staffers like former special disbursing officer Gina Acosta.

Last August 24, Acosta testified before the impeachment court that she released OVP’s CFs Col. Raymund Dante Lachica of the Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group (VPSPG) even if she knew that Lachica was not a bonded officer.

Like Boransing, Acosta also appeared before the House committee on good government and public accountability. During a November 2024 hearing of the panel, Acosta also admitted that it was Duterte who ordered the release of the CFs to Lachica. /mr

articles.title: NIA seeks funding increase in proposed 2027 budget
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The National Irrigation Administration (NIA) on Tuesday asked lawmakers from the House of Representatives to increase the agency’s funding for next year, noting that budget cuts…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Irrigation Administration (NIA) on Tuesday asked lawmakers from the House of Representatives to increase the agency’s funding for next year, noting that budget cuts under the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP) may hinder the implementation of proposed irrigation projects.

During the House committee on appropriations’ briefing on the budget proposal of NIA, NIA Administrator Engr. Eduardo Guillen said the agency proposed funding by program expenditure classification worth P232,778,193,000, which is significantly less than the P46,355,900,000 allocated for the agency under the NEP.
Guillen noted that his agency’s proposal for next year is a 268-percent increase from its 2026 budget of P63,246,735,000.
“The reduction is mainly attributed to the significantly lower allocation for capital outlay, which comprises the bulk of NIA’s irrigation investment requirements,” Guillen said.

Guillen also cited significant budget cuts in improvement of service roads in national and communal irrigation systems. The NIA proposed P17,705,462,000 and P2,389,865,000 fundings for national and communal irrigation systems, respectively, but he said that only P250,000,000 were allotted for each project.

He added that the agency proposed the budgets for the repair of the following: national irrigation systems (P38,261,911,000); communal irrigation systems (P20,515,660,000); and pump irrigation systems (P10,415,188,000) while he said that these projects were allotted P2,021,555,000, P920,000,000, and P3,000,000,000 under the NEP, respectively.

Meanwhile, restoration of national and communal irrigation systems had a proposal of P7,260,567,000 and P13,245,386,000, respectively while they were allotted P1,000,000,000, and P250,000,000 under the NEP, respectively.

The administration also said that the new national irrigation and small reservoir irrigation projects were allotted by the agency of P34,939,697,000 and P11,083,425,000, respectively while they were allocated of P7,561,321,000 and P4,579,000,000, respectively under the NEP.
Guillen shared that as of December 31, 2025, only 2.20 million hectares have been developed out of the country’s total potential irrigable area of 3.13 million hectares. /jpv

articles.title: Man who reportedly killed 3-year-old son in Ilocos Sur may be using drugs
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The 29-year-old man who allegedly killed his three-year-old son in Tagudin, Ilocos Sur is suspected of using illegal drugs, police said Tuesday. The father, who reportedly…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The 29-year-old man who allegedly killed his three-year-old son in Tagudin, Ilocos Sur is suspected of using illegal drugs, police said Tuesday.
The father, who reportedly stabbed his son to death inside their home in Barangay Lacong on Friday, August 28, is currently at large.
During a press briefing, Philippine National Police (PNP) public information chief Col. Allen Rae Co said people who knew the suspect told investigators that he had been using illegal drugs.
“This father could’ve been using illegal drugs,” Co said, adding that they are already looking into the matter.
Police are also checking whether the suspect had a previous criminal record.

When asked if the PNP would also examine whether the suspect might have been experiencing mental health problems, the PNP official said, “Yes, that will come after. Hopefully, if we will be able to track him.”
Meanwhile, authorities are determining the whereabouts of the victim’s mother.
“There were no mentions in the report yet as to where the mother is,” Co explained.
Co said the investigation remains ongoing as authorities continue to track down the suspect and determine the circumstances surrounding the victim’s death.
— Rendell Ivan Manuel, INQUIRER.net trainee

articles.title: Public urged to take precautions amid Metro Manila haze
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Metro Manila residents were urged to take precautions as haze believed to be linked to fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, affected air quality in several cities. Based on data as…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Metro Manila residents were urged to take precautions as haze believed to be linked to fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, affected air quality in several cities.

Based on data as of 6 a.m. from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources-Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB) in the National Capital Region, several areas recorded high levels of PM2.5, or particulate matter less than 2.5 micrometers in diameter.

Eleven cities recorded acutely unhealthy levels, with Parañaque having the highest reading at 296; Quezon City (Ateneo), 241; Las Piñas, 237; Manila, 231; Malabon, 229; Taguig and Valenzuela, 224; Marikina, 217; Muntinlupa, 216; San Juan, 213; and Mandaluyong, 207.

Very unhealthy levels were recorded in Pateros and Navotas at 172 and 153, respectively, while Makati’s reading of 111 was considered unhealthy for sensitive groups. Air quality was fair in Quezon City (Commonwealth Avenue), with a reading of 98.
With unhealthy air conditions, residents can take the following steps to reduce their exposure:

items: Wear a mask when going outside

blocks.text: If going outdoors is necessary, wear respiratory protection such as an N95 mask, which can help reduce exposure to fine particles.

items: Stay indoors as much as possible

blocks.text: When air quality reaches unhealthy levels, limit unnecessary outdoor activities and prolonged exposure.

Under the EMB’s PM2.5 guidelines, people are advised to limit outdoor exertion when conditions become acutely unhealthy, while those with heart or respiratory diseases are advised to stay indoors and rest as much as possible.

items: Protect vulnerable people

blocks.text: Children, older adults, pregnant women and people with respiratory or heart conditions may be more vulnerable to the effects of air pollution.

items: Monitor the air quality in your area

blocks.text: Air quality can vary from one part of Metro Manila to another. Residents should therefore check the Air Quality Index (AQI) before deciding whether to spend time outdoors.
The EMB-NCR provides real-time air quality monitoring data, including PM2.5 measurements, through its monitoring stations across the region.
The DENR-EMB reminded the public to rely on official advisories from the agency or their respective local government units during episodes of haze or deteriorating air quality.
Health hazards
The World Health Organization said PM2.5 can penetrate the lungs and enter the body through the bloodstream, affecting all major organs.
It said exposure to PM2.5 can harm the cardiovascular and respiratory systems and can cause conditions such as stroke, lung cancer and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

New research has also shown an association between prenatal exposure to high levels of air pollution and developmental delays at age 3, as well as psychological and behavioral problems later in life, including symptoms of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, anxiety and depression.

The Indoor Air Hygiene Institute said studies also suggest that long-term exposure to fine particulate matter may be associated with increased rates of chronic bronchitis, reduced lung function and increased mortality from lung cancer and heart disease.
“People with breathing and heart problems, children and the elderly may be particularly sensitive to PM2.5,” the institute said.
Exposure to fine particles can also affect lung function and worsen medical conditions such as asthma and heart disease.

“Scientific studies have linked increases in daily PM2.5 exposure with increased respiratory and cardiovascular hospital admissions, emergency department visits and deaths,” the institute’s study said.

IQAir said PM2.5 can be produced by a variety of sources, resulting in different chemical compositions and physical characteristics. Sulfates, nitrates, black carbon and ammonium are among the most common particles that make up PM2.5.

The anthropogenic generation of PM2.5 can largely be attributed to combustion engines, power generation, industrial processes, agricultural processes, wood and coal burning and construction. The most prevalent natural sources of PM2.5 include dust storms, wildfires and sandstorms.

It said “small particles pose the greatest risk to human health” and that “while the nose can filter most coarse particles, fine and ultrafine particles are inhaled deeper into the lungs where they can be deposited or even pass into the bloodstream.” /dm

articles.title: 1 of 4 missing in Tarlac bridge collapse found dead in Pangasinan
articles.summary: TARLAC CITY– One of the four missing passengers of the vehicle that fell in the Aug.29 Agana bridge collapse was found dead in Barangay Carael at Dagupan City in Pangasinan on Monday. Fishermen…

blocks.text: TARLAC CITY– One of the four missing passengers of the vehicle that fell in the Aug.29 Agana bridge collapse was found dead in Barangay Carael at Dagupan City in Pangasinan on Monday.
Fishermen helped retrieve the body of James Patrick Taborlupa, 30, who was a former staff nurse at the Jecsons Medical Center in Tarlac City.

Still missing are Paul Harvey Collado, nurse supervisor at the Jecsons Medical Center, Shanen Tuhao, and Shiela Mae Taborlupa, who were occupants of the SUV that plunged into the raging Tarlac River when the bridge was torn apart during very heavy rains.

The SUV’s lone survivor was Nataniel Dizon, 20, who shared a post about his uncle Taborlupa’s last advice: “Pagraduate ka na pala Not, papayamanin mo na si Ate Bel (Mama mo) nyan ha, kasi deserve nya, ka swerte nyo ni NatNat sa Mama nyo, sobrang bait, sya lang yung palaging naaasahan, at pinaka napalapit na pinsan namin na palaging nandyan.”
(You are about to graduate, Not, [Dizon’s nickname]. Make your mother rich. You are lucky to have her as your dependable mother and a cousin with whom we have grown close)
Agana Bridge, which was constructed in the 1980s, links Tarlac City to the towns of Sta. Ignacia, Mayantoc, Camiling and San Clemente, and is often used to reach the Pangasinan town of Mangatarem.
Dizon complained that the rescue efforts took a long time and he was not immediately brought to the hospital. Instead, bystanders kept taking videos and uploaded them as social media content.
“Niligtas ko talaga ang sarili ko doon, ako lang, walang nag-rescue sa akin o sa amin. Mas inuna niyo pang mag-video,” he posted on Facebook. INQ
(I saved myself; no one rescued me or us. They prioritized recording videos.)

articles.title: Putin proposes permanent Russia-China visa-free scheme in talks with Xi
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday expressed readiness to make the visa-free scheme with China permanent if Beijing considers it useful, as he held talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping in…

blocks.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday expressed readiness to make the visa-free scheme with China permanent if Beijing considers it useful, as he held talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Kyrgyzstan, Tass news agency reported.
The two countries have introduced an arrangement allowing each other’s nationals to stay for 30 days without a visa, with the measure effective until the end of 2027.

In the meeting held on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek, Putin noted that the visa-free travel had helped increase tourist flows between the two countries by 43 percent in the first half of 2026, according to Tass.

Putin also expressed his condolences to the families of the victims of catastrophic flash floods and mudslides along the Nepal-China border and wished for a “speedy recovery to all those affected,” the news agency said.

The two leaders, who last met in person in Beijing in May, briefly touched upon the Ukraine crisis, but it was not the main issue at their meeting, Tass quoted Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov as saying.
China and Russia have been strengthening their ties in recent years, with Beijing opposing Western sanctions on Moscow over its war against Ukraine. /dl

articles.title: Cebu stuns Abra; Quezon, Biñan triumphs
articles.summary: The Cebu Greats shook the SportsPlus MPBL (Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League) 2026 Season with a 74-70 stunner over the Abra Solid North Weavers on Monday, Aug. 31, at the Ynares Center Montalban…

blocks.text: The Cebu Greats shook the SportsPlus MPBL (Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League) 2026 Season with a 74-70 stunner over the Abra Solid North Weavers on Monday, Aug. 31, at the Ynares Center Montalban in Rizal Province.

Kint Akiar delivered in the homestretch to complete what Mark Meneses set up, lifting Cebu to its fourth straight win and a 19-5 record in the round-robin elimination phase of the two-division, 26-team tournament.

Ariar, a 6-foot-3 find from the Cebu Institute of Technology University and Letran, drilled in a jumper and two free throws in the last 42 seconds as Cebu snapped Abra's hot run at 19 and pulled the Weavers down to 21-2.
Ron Dennison also delivered at clutch time, making two charities with 20.3 seconds left, compensating for the two free throws of Abra's Alfred Ryan Batino, only 12.3 seconds to go.
Overall, Meneses carried the Greats past the defending champion Weavers with 26 points, 14 rebounds, 4 assists, 2 steals and 2 blocks in 35 minutes and 29 seconds of play.
Meneses was named the SportsPlus best player over Dhon Reverente, with 16 points, 12 in the third quarter, and 4 rebounds; and Ariar, who notched 8 points and 2 rebounds.
Abra drew 20 points, 11 rebounds and 2 assists from Dave Ildefonso; 18 points, 6 rebounds, 3 assists and 2 steals from DJ Fenner; and 8 points and 9 rebounds from John Uduba.

With Ildefonso pouring in 12 points and Uduba adding 6, Abra took the half, 38-34, negating Meneses' 16-point effort for Cebu, which is ranked fourth in the South division behind first game winner Quezon Province (16-3), Biñan (19-4) and Batangas City (16-4).
Defending champion Abra still paces the North division, towing San Juan and Caloocan, both 18-3, and Ilagan Isabela (13-9).
Quezon trounces Manila
The Quezon Huskers battered Manila Batang Quiapo, 107-65, to signify their bid for a third straight South division title.

Manila led briefly, 17-16, as Joe Gomez De Liano knocked in his first three triple attempts. Quezon, however, clustered 28 straight points bridging the first and second quarters to regain control, 44-17, and never let go.
All 15 Huskers, with Cedric Manzano piling 16 and John Abate adding 14, scored as they led by as far as 107-61 with 50.4 seconds left.
Biñan thwarts Rizal
Biñan quelled Rizal XentroMall's repeated rallies and prevailed, 65-61, in the nightcap.

Nic Cabanero shone again for Biñan with 14 points, 14 rebounds and 2 assists; followed by Kenny Rocacurva, with 12 points, 8 rebounds and 4 steals; Carlo Lastimosa, with 11 points and 2 rebounds; Mochael Mabulac, with 10 points, 9 rebounds and 3 assists; and Pamboy Raymundo, with 10 points and 4 assists.
Rizal, which saw its five-win streak broken, drew 10 points and 10 rebounds from veteran Mark Yee.
Also-ran Manila fell to a league-worst 1-23 card despite Mark Doligon's 20 points and De Liano's 18.
The MPBL returns to the Batangas City Coliseum on Tuesday, featuring games between Marikina and Pasig at 3 p.m., San Juan and Mindoro at 5 p.m., and Bataan and Batangas at 7 p.m.

articles.title: Japan’s House Foods weighs sale of Curry House CoCo Ichibanya operator
articles.summary: TOKYO —Japan’s House Foods Group Inc. is considering selling listed subsidiary Ichibanya Co., the operator of the Curry House CoCo Ichibanya, or CoCo Ichi, restaurant chain, it was learned on Monday,…

blocks.text: TOKYO —Japan’s House Foods Group Inc. is considering selling listed subsidiary Ichibanya Co., the operator of the Curry House CoCo Ichibanya, or CoCo Ichi, restaurant chain, it was learned on Monday, Aug. 31.
The major food maker is apparently looking to streamline its group business structure, according to sources familiar with the matter.
In a statement, House Foods said the company is “considering all available options,” including the delisting of Ichibanya, “with a view to enhancing corporate value and shareholder value.”
House Foods acquired Ichibanya in 2015 through a tender offer. Ichibanya has remained a publicly listed company since then.
Ichibanya, listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange’s top-tier Prime section, was about 51 percent owned by House Foods as of February this year.
For the business year that ended in February 2026, Ichibanya reported consolidated sales of ¥65.5 billion, up 7.4 percent from the previous year, and a net profit of ¥2.5 billion, down 19.2 percent.
It runs about 1,200 CoCo Ichi restaurants in Japan and some 200 overseas, including the Philippines.

articles.title: PNP, BPI, BFP, and BIR advance to Final Four of Conrado Estrella III Cup
articles.summary: The race for the championship intensified as four powerhouse teams punched their tickets to the semifinals of the 1st Inter-Agency LISEA Pickleball Tournament “Conrado Estrella III Cup” following…

blocks.text: The race for the championship intensified as four powerhouse teams punched their tickets to the semifinals of the 1st Inter-Agency LISEA Pickleball Tournament “Conrado Estrella III Cup” following thrilling quarterfinal encounters held Thursday at the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) Gymnasium along Elliptical Road, Quezon City.

Showcasing skill, teamwork, and determination, government agencies battled for a coveted spot in the tournament’s Final Four, delighting spectators with fast-paced rallies and competitive action on the pickleball courts.

The Philippine National Police (PNP) tandem of Pialyn Fabros and Namnama Cajefe emerged victorious in the opening quarterfinal match, overcoming the challenge posed by the Social Security System (SSS) pair of Erika Ravago and Claire Tañada to secure their place in the semifinals.

In the second quarterfinal showdown, the Bureau of Plant Industry (BPI) duo of Pearl Anisco and Gabriela Frias displayed poise and consistency to defeat Philippine Heart Center (PHC) representatives Sheryl Dela Cruz and Maan Mendoza, booking a Final Four berth.

The Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) also stamped its authority as Maylyn France Bautista and Nina Sorronda outplayed the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) pair of Hazel Ubag and Jacqueline Quilit to advance.

Meanwhile, an all-BIR affair capped the quarterfinal round as Jolina Dayoc and Leilanie Claridad prevailed over fellow Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) teammates Juvie May Novio and Rica Banares, ensuring the agency’s continued presence in the title hunt.

With the quarterfinal dust settled, the semifinal stage is now set for a pair of highly anticipated clashes. BIR’s Jolina Dayoc and Leilanie Claridad will take on BPI’s Pearl Anisco and Gabriela Frias, while PNP’s Pialyn Fabros and Namnama Cajefe will square off against BFP’s Maylyn France Bautista and Nina Sorronda.

As the tournament enters its decisive phase, fans can expect even fiercer competition as the remaining teams battle for a place in the championship match and the honor of becoming the inaugural champions of the Conrado Estrella III Cup.
“The intensity continues to rise as only four teams remain standing in what has become one of the most exciting inter-agency pickleball events of the year.”

articles.title: US Settlement requires Meta to check young users’ ages. How will that work?
articles.summary: Here is a look at what Meta said it will do to ensure that users are as old as they say they are, and some of the legal issues that could complicate age checks

blocks.text: META. People are seen behind a logo of Meta Platforms, during a conference in Mumbai, India, September 20, 2023
Francis Mascarenhas/Reuters
Here is a look at what Meta said it will do to ensure that users are as old as they say they are, and some of the legal issues that could complicate age checks

items: Meta has agreed to improve age verification for users on its platforms as part of an $18-billion legal settlement aimed at reducing children's access to social media.
The settlement requires Meta to implement daily usage limits and stronger age checks, particularly for users under 13, while allowing for some data use to train AI for future age detection.

Legal challenges remain due to the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA), which restricts companies from collecting personal data from children under 13, complicating effective age verification.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Meta has agreed to improve how it verifies the age of users of its platforms such as Facebook and Instagram as part of an $18 billion legal settlement with US states that is aimed at curbing children’s use of social media.
Here is a look at what Meta said it will do to ensure that users are as old as they say they are, and some of the legal issues that could complicate age checks.

Meta policy bars children under 13 from using Facebook or Instagram and permits teenagers to use the platforms with some limits on content. Meta has acknowledged that younger users sometimes lie about their ages when creating accounts, and the company has faced increasing pressure from countries around the world to limit children’s access to social media.

Meta has not historically asked users for proof of age such as a photo ID. Instead the company said it looks at contextual clues, like birthday posts or celebrations of school grades, to identify accounts that are being used by children.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg testified in February that age verification would be more effective if it was handled by makers of mobile devices, an approach taken by a Texas state law that requires people under 18 to get parental consent before downloading an age-restricted app onto their device.
Meta agreed to the multi-state settlement, announced on August 26, to resolve legal claims that it designed social media platforms to addict children.

The settlement requires Meta to make broad changes related to users under 18, such as setting daily usage limits and disabling push notifications at night. It also calls for stronger age checks for young users, but it does not require Meta to take strict verification steps such as checking the photo IDs of users or asking them to upload a video selfie.

The settlement focuses particular attention on age checks for children below age 13, requiring Meta to take extra steps such as searching the friend networks of the accounts of the youngest users in an effort to identify and eliminate them. The company must also make it easier for social media users to report suspected children’s accounts, and it allows an independent auditor to review Meta’s efforts to check ages.

The settlement allows Meta to temporarily use some data generated by children it identifies in order to train an AI model to detect under-13 users in the future, similar to its current approach for identifying the accounts of suspected teenagers.

Meta has previously described both legal and practical roadblocks to stricter age assurance, including a 1998 federal law called the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act, or COPPA. This statute holds companies liable for damages if they collect personal data from children under age 13 without parental consent.

Meta and other social media companies have argued that this law puts them in a bind because it restricts them from collecting from children the kind of data that would reliably verify a person’s age, such as IDs, biometric information or detailed records of their online activity.

Experts who advocate for better protections for children online have argued that social media companies have tried to use COPPA as a distraction to avoid taking responsibility for allowing children onto their platforms.

The $18-billion settlement, as well as a $942-million judgment in a New Mexico court case on August 6, have attempted to thread the needle, requiring more proactive age-verification measures without triggering potential violations of COPPA.

In New Mexico, the judge concluded that the online-privacy law restricted him from ordering Meta to ask children to submit personal data or be passively tracked online, and said that strict age-verification requirements could put Meta at an unfair disadvantage to social media competitors. So the judge ordered changes intended to improve age assurances “within the limits of COPPA.” The settlement uses a similar approach.

The Federal Trade Commission, which enforces COPPA for the US government, issued a policy statement in February that it would not take action against any company that collects personal information for the sole purpose of determining a user’s age via age-verification technologies.
Legal experts said that the FTC policy provides only a partial shield for companies because US states have their own authority to enforce COPPA violations even when the FTC declines to do so.
Several states had sued Meta, alleging online-privacy violations, but dropped those claims as part of the settlement. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Antipolo bishop urges Pinoys to scrutinize leaders ahead of elections amid flooding
articles.summary: Antipolo Bishop Ruperto Santos on Tuesday called on Filipinos to be discerning in choosing leaders ahead of the upcoming elections, as multiple areas in the country continue to reel from flooding and…

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 2:15pm

Antipolo Bishop Ruperto Santos on Tuesday called on Filipinos to be discerning in choosing leaders ahead of the upcoming elections, as multiple areas in the country continue to reel from flooding and heavy rains due to the southwest monsoon or Habagat.
In a social media post, Santos urged voters to avoid reelecting candidates who failed to deliver on their promises in previous elections and to examine their track records carefully.
"Kung ang binoto natin noon ay hindi naghatid ng pagbabago, kung ang pangako ay hindi natupad, kung ang bayan ay lalo pang napahamak, huwag na nating ulitin," Santos said.
(If those we voted for in the past failed to bring about change, keep their promises, or caused further harm to the country, we should not make the same mistake again.)
"Suriin ang track record. Kilalanin ang gawa, hindi lamang salita. Kung puro pangako at walang patunay, huwag nang piliin, bagkus talikuran na," he added.
(Scrutinize their track record. Know not only their promises but also their work. If they only make promises without any results, let us not choose them.)
Voters should also not be swayed by temporary gains or bribes when choosing government officials, the prelate said.

"Sa darating na halalan, maging mapanuri. Huwag magpadala sa panandaliang biyaya o lagay. Ang kapalit ng ilang libong pisong lagay ay taon-taong pagdurusa, pagkasira ng kabuhayan, at kawalan ng pag-asa," Santos said.

(This coming elections, be discerning. Do not be swayed by temporary benefits or bribes. The price of accepting a bribe worth a few thousand pesos is years of suffering, loss of livelihood, and hopelessness.)
The National and Local Elections in the country is scheduled for May 2028, as mandated by the Constitution.
The first parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao will be held on September 14, 2026.

Meanwhile, Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE) is set on November 2, but several proposed measures have been filed seeking to reset the polls and fix the terms of the concerned elective officials to five years.
A 'sin' to God, Filipinos
The bishop described widespread flooding as not merely a failure, but a sin against God and all Filipinos.
"Mga kapatid, hindi kasalanan ng mamamayan ang katiwalian. Hindi kasalanan ng mamamayan ang ghost projects. Ang lahat ng ito ay kasamaan, kasakiman, at kapabayaan ng mga namumuno," Santos said.

(Brothers and sisters, corruption is not the fault of the people. Ghost projects are not the fault of the people. All of these are the result of the wrongdoing, greed, and negligence of those in power.)
Several areas in Luzon, including Metro Manila, Pampanga, Rizal and Bulacan were flooded following the continuous torrential rains brought by the Habagat.
Many residents in Rodriguez, Rizal are already accustomed to flooding. Many of them simply survive, clean up the damage left behind by the flood, and then prepare for the next possible inundation.

According to Rodriguez Mayor Ronnie Evangelista, flooding in their area is partially due to topography, as the town acts like a funnel for major river systems that may overflow with runoff water coming from nearby mountains.
Around 17,300 residents in Pampanga have been moved to 270 evacuation centers as severe, prolonged flooding continues to affect the province. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: P1.9-M smuggled cigarettes from Cebu intercepted in Negros port
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY - A van loaded with P1.980 million worth of suspected illicit cigarettes from Cebu was intercepted by authorities before midnight in a seaport in Barangay 6, San Carlos City, Negros…

blocks.text: Authorities intercept P1.980 million worth of suspected illicit cigarettes from Cebu in a seaport in Barangay 6, San Carlos City, Negros Occidental on Monday, Aug. 31. (Negros Occidental Police Provincial Office)

BACOLOD CITY - A van loaded with P1.980 million worth of suspected illicit cigarettes from Cebu was intercepted by authorities before midnight in a seaport in Barangay 6, San Carlos City, Negros Occidental on Monday, Aug. 31.
Police Lt. Col. Nazer Canja, San Carlos police chief, said they were able to track down the vehicle, following a report on the alleged cigarette smuggling operation.
Canja said that a 30-year-old driver and 24-year-old helper from Toledo, Cebu voluntarily surrendered 33 master cases of cigarettes with 60 reams per cases.
He said that the vehicle was only rented in Cebu, and the two individuals were only tasked to pick-up the items.
Canja said these individuals did not reveal any information regarding the person who ordered the items.

This follows the series of seizure of P26.6 million worth of the same contraband in Escalante City, Negros Occidental on Aug. 25, P21 million in a seaborne patrol in Sipalay City, Negros Occidental, and P14.6 million in Bago City, Negros Occidental last month.

articles.title: Meralco advances nuclear plans with $2.8-million US-backed study
articles.summary: Manuel V. Pangilinan-led Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) and its power generation arm, Meralco PowerGen Corp. (MGEN), have tapped United States (US)-based engineering firm Sargent & Lundy and local…

blocks.text: Manuel V. Pangilinan-led Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) and its power generation arm, Meralco PowerGen Corp. (MGEN), have tapped United States (US)-based engineering firm Sargent & Lundy and local partner AMH Philippines Inc. (AMH) to assess the viability of deploying small modular reactors (SMRs) in the country as nuclear energy enters its pre-development phase.

In a statement on Tuesday, Sept. 1, MGEN said the partnership is part of the $2.8-million technical assistance (TA) program funded by the US Trade and Development Agency (USTDA), which was formally announced in February 2026.

The study aims to provide One Meralco with a data-driven basis to determine the feasibility, timing, and integration strategy for incorporating SMRs into the nation’s future energy mix. A dedicated SMR working group has been established within One Meralco to lead the initiative alongside Sargent & Lundy and AMH, with target completion set for the fourth quarter of 2027.

Under the engagement, Sargent & Lundy will execute a vendor-neutral assessment aligned with International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) standards and global best practices. The scope covers technology assessment, site selection, grid integration, financial planning, and decision-making frameworks.

MGEN President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Emmanuel Rubio said the collaboration would allow the company’s nuclear roadmap to move into a more actionable, data-driven assessment under its nuclear energy strategic transition (NEST) program.

“As we advance this USTDA-funded study, MGEN remains committed to exploring safe, reliable, and low-carbon technologies such as SMRs as we work to secure the Philippines’ long-term energy future and support the country’s economic growth,” Rubio added.

Beyond technical evaluations, the study features a series of dedicated workshops designed to build technical capacity among key energy stakeholders, including MGEN, the Department of Energy (DOE), and the Philippine Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (PhilATOM).
MGEN Head of Strategic Energy Transition Felino M. Bernardo emphasized that the initiative addresses both operational and regulatory realities.

“By bringing together a dedicated internal working group, alongside global and local experts, we are undertaking a comprehensive assessment that considers the technical, financial, and regulatory realities of the Philippine setting,” Bernardo said.

“The study goes beyond identifying suitable technologies and potential sites. It will also build the technical capacity and decision-making frameworks that can support MGEN and our national stakeholders well beyond the completion of the study,” he added. - Gabriell Christel Galang

articles.title: AFP deploys troops, trucks, water assets for Habagat, Pilandok response
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) has deployed troops, military vehicles, and water assets to flood-hit areas in Luzon as the country continues to deal with the effects of the Southwest…

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 2:09pm

The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) has deployed troops, military vehicles, and water assets to flood-hit areas in Luzon as the country continues to deal with the effects of the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat and Tropical Cyclone Pilandok.
At a press briefing, AFP spokesperson Colonel Francel Margareth Padilla said the disaster response teams were sent to Tarlac, Pampanga, and Bataan.

“For humanitarian assistance and disaster response, noong August 29, the AFP deployed personnel, vehicles, and other HADR assets to Tarlac, Pampanga, and Bataan to support local government units and disaster response agencies,” she said.
This is to assist local government units and disaster response agencies in rescue operations and the transport and distribution of relief supplies.
The Philippine Army deployed 269 personnel and 15 military trucks for humanitarian assistance and disaster response operations in communities affected by widespread flooding in Luzon.
Another 2,406 soldiers, reservists, and other personnel, along with 277 military trucks and 15 water assets, were placed on alert for immediate deployment if needed.
The Army's responders conducted rescue, evacuation, and sandbagging operations while coordinating with government agencies and local authorities to assist communities affected by the monsoon rains.

Meanwhile, the Philippine Air Force (PAF) also sent disaster response teams to Pampanga and Tarlac from August 28 to 31 to support rescue, evacuation, search-and-rescue, relief and sandbagging operations.
In Pampanga, PAF teams assisted in rescue operations in Floridablanca and Lubao, while search-and-rescue teams were deployed to Bacolor and San Fernando.
In Tarlac, the PAF supported search operations following the collapse of a portion of Agana Bridge on August 29 and helped evacuate residents in Barangay Aduas in Paniqui. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Why leptospirosis remains a serious threat long after people wade through contaminated water
articles.summary: During the rainy season, especially when there is widespread flooding, doctors brace for the inevitable deluge of leptospirosis cases. Infectious diseases doctors like me, along with kidney doctors…

blocks.text: During the rainy season, especially when there is widespread flooding, doctors brace for the inevitable deluge of leptospirosis cases. Infectious diseases doctors like me, along with kidney doctors (nephrologists) and lung doctors (pulmonologists), are usually called upon to see the sickest patients. While most people infected with leptospirosis only develop mild symptoms, severe leptospirosis can manifest without much warning, progress quickly, and can be fatal.

Leptospirosis is caused by a spiral-shaped bacteria that is usually found in rodent urine. Other animals such as dogs and cats can harbor Leptospira species, but it is not as common in these animals. Leptospirosis is usually acquired when wading through flood waters contaminated by rat urine. Other less common ways to get leptospirosis are by ingesting food contaminated with rodent urine and feces, as well as eating poorly cooked meat that is infected with Leptospira.

The usual incubation period (time from exposure to symptoms) for leptospirosis is five to 14 days, but in rare cases can be as little as two days or as long as 30 days. Common symptoms of leptospirosis include fever, muscle pain (especially in the calf muscles), fatigue, and headache. Some people develop conjunctival suffusion, which manifests as redness and swelling in the whites of the eyes that can look like sore eyes. Not all these symptoms may be present, and a lot of people only develop milder manifestations, which can get better on their own even without proper treatment.

However, a significant number of patients who are not properly treated with antibiotics progress to severe leptospirosis, which is a life-threatening condition. Signs and symptoms of severe leptospirosis include jaundice (yellowing of the skin), decreased urine output, dark color of the urine, abdominal pain, and shortness of breath. This can lead to coughing up blood, bleeding in the mouth, gums, or stool, and low blood pressure.

People who have been exposed to flood water, even if they have intact skin with no wounds, should seek medical attention as soon as possible. A doctor or healthcare worker can determine the degree of exposure and prescribe antibiotic prophylaxis with doxycycline or an alternative agent.

Prophylaxis works best when given as close to the time of exposure as possible and becomes less effective the longer the delay. When there are large numbers of people exposed, local government units try to make doxycycline available through the barangay health centers following proper medical assessment by barangay healthcare personnel. This medical evaluation is important because the dosing and duration of antibiotics are different for people with intact skin versus those with open wounds or those who inadvertently swallow contaminated water. Continuing exposure to flood water may need periodic administration of prophylaxis. Moreover, antibiotics like doxycycline are prescription-only drugs that can have side effects.

Doxycycline can cause heartburn, photosensitivity, rashes, and (in women) vaginal yeast infections. Doxycycline should not be given concurrently with dairy products since milk can inactivate it. Doxycycline should not be given to pregnant women or women who might be pregnant. There are alternatives to doxycycline which a properly qualified obstetrician can prescribe. Children, especially those below 12 years old, should also not be given doxycycline without proper evaluation by a pediatrician. Never take an antibiotic without proper medical evaluation. Aside from potential side effects, unnecessary antibiotic intake can lead to the development of bacterial drug resistance, and the antibiotic may no longer work when we actually need it.

If a person develops any of the symptoms of leptospirosis within the two- to 30-day incubation period, they should immediately seek medical care. This should be done even if that person took doxycycline for prophylaxis after exposure. Doxycycline prophylaxis is not a guarantee that one won't get leptospirosis, especially if it is taken more than 72 hours after the exposure. While antibiotic prophylaxis isn't 100 percent effective at preventing infection, it can help decrease the risk of developing severe leptospirosis.

Mild to moderate leptospirosis can usually be treated with oral antibiotics and careful monitoring. These patients may not need to be admitted to the hospital if the laboratory results are normal or near normal. Close follow-up is essential since some of these patients can progress to severe leptospirosis even with proper treatment.

Patients with severe leptospirosis need to be admitted to the hospital immediately and given intravenous antibiotics such as penicillin or ceftriaxone. Severe leptospirosis can adversely affect the kidneys, the liver, and/or the lungs. Patients with kidney failure from leptospirosis may need urgent dialysis. Early dialysis can help the kidneys recover. If the kidney failure isn't treated promptly, the patient may end up on permanent dialysis, if he or she survives the illness.

Patients with liver failure from severe leptospirosis (also known as Weil's disease) have a high chance of dying. They need good supportive care and may need blood products to prevent bleeding since the liver makes the clotting factors for the body.

Perhaps the most dreaded complication of leptospirosis is pulmonary hemorrhage. Patients who bleed into their lungs are at a very high risk of dying. They usually need to be hooked up to the ventilator and may need strong medicines like high-dose corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide (an immunosuppressant medication) to modulate the extreme inflammatory response from severe leptospirosis. Even with the best care, we lose a lot of these patients.

As I write this, I am the supervising infectious diseases consultant for adult charity patients at the emergency room at our government hospital, and we are seeing a large surge of severe leptospirosis cases. Some patients have already died. These cases were likely infected two weeks prior, and since we’ve had non-stop rains and floods since then, this is just the beginning.

Leptospirosis can kill you. Avoid wading in flood waters, use protective gear if you can, and get doxycycline prophylaxis from a healthcare provider or the barangay health center if you are exposed. If you develop symptoms, see your doctor for proper care before it gets worse.

articles.title: Boransing says Army youth summits predated VP Duterte's DepEd confidential funds use by nearly 20 years
articles.summary: The Philippine Army had been conducting Youth Leadership Summit (YLS) for almost two decades before impeachment trial respondent Vice President Sara Duterte became Department of Education (DepEd)…

blocks.text: The Philippine Army had been conducting Youth Leadership Summit (YLS) for almost two decades before impeachment trial respondent Vice President Sara Duterte became Department of Education (DepEd) secretary, Col. Manaros Boransing II testified before senator-judges on Tuesday, Sept. 1.

Boransing's revelation belied claims that the 2023 summits were created by DepEd or were dependent on the agency’s confidential funds--the alleged misuse of which was the subject matter of the Senate impeachment court.
At any rate, Boransing acknowledged that DepEd joined the interagency planning when schools and students began to be involved.
He described the program during direct examination by private prosecutor, layweecReynaldo Robles on day 20 of respondent Duterte’s impeachment trial.
“The [YLS] is a long-time Philippine Army program or Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) program,” Boransing said.
He described YLS as a response to the recruitment of students and out-of-school youth by violent extremist groups in areas affected by insurgency or terrorism.
“The first official, according to the Army’s historical records, the first record was 2002 in Southern Tagalog,” he testified.

Boransing recalled that the 1st Infantry “Tabak” Division had conducted a summit in Jolo, Sulu as early as 2005. The number of activities varied with the threat level, but the program continued regularly.
“It’s definitely annually...It is part of the regular program of the Philippine Army if it is requested by our subordinate unit,” added the military official.
Duterte was DepEd secretary from 2022 to 2024.
Boransing issued certification on Jan. 1, 2024, covering eight YLS activities with 531 participants and 53 Information Education Campaign (IEC) activities with 9,428 participants in 2023.

The Army led the YLS while bringing in local governments, schools, police and other stakeholders. “Well, sir, it’s the Army, and we try to have the local government unit involved as much as possible,” he said.
The program’s long history did not mean the Army acted alone; an interagency technical working group selected particular venues after assessing local conditions.

“There were some inputs from DepEd, sir, because some of the areas are schools, and many of the participants are students. So definitely, they were involved in the planning and the choosing of the areas,” the witness testified.
He described those inputs as school locations, academic schedules and permission to speak with students. He could not say whether they were products of confidential operations.
He said the Army budgeted for its own role in YLS, local governments supported youth delegates and participating agencies paid their respective expenses.
“It’s part of the regular budget, sir,” Boransing said of the Army’s participation.
Boransing's testimony showed that the YLS predated Duterte’s DepEd tenure, operated as a regular Army program and could proceed without receiving confidential funds from DepEd.

While the Interagency coordination can explain why DepEd officials or students were present, it cannot be established that confidential informers were paid, that they supplied intelligence or that their information caused the activities certified by Boransing.

DepEd later attached Boransing’s certifications to its April 17, 2024 response to COA Audit Observation Memorandum No. 2024-015. The AOM sought proof about the reported rewards totaling ₱15.54 million given to informants for the successful information-gathering or surveillance.
Certifications for attendance only
Boransing testified that he issued the document as a routine certification of activities and participation—not as his verification of DepEd’s confidential fund transactions.

The Jan. 1, 2024 certification recorded eight YLS activities with 531 participants and 53 Information Education Campaign (IEC) activities with 9,428 participants in schools within the 1st Infantry “Tabak” Division’s area of operations.

Robles then replayed in court Boransing’s Oct. 17, 2024 testimony at the House of Representatives to establish why the Army issued such documents. The latter affirmed that account under oath before the impeachment court.
It did not name a DepEd informer, describe intelligence, record a reward payment or trace the ₱15.54 million later associated with DepEd’s confidential fund response to state auditors.
Boransing said Army programs regularly brought together national agencies, local governments, schools and community groups. Participants commonly requested proof of attendance or involvement.
“When we participate in activities of one or many agencies, many agencies ask for certifications of attendance,” Boransing said.
“We assumed that the certification was also for that purpose...A lot of other national government agencies and local government units ask for certifications in that manner also,” he added.
Boransing said then-DepEd Undersecretary Nolasco Mempin sought the document through the Army chain of command.
The document’s text remained narrow--it listed activities, participants and locations, but it did not state that DepEd funded the Army programs.

It also did not certify that information supplied by a paid informer caused an activity to occur. Likewise, it contained no acknowledgment from a reward recipient and no description of an intelligence product.

articles.title: Wushu Arena PH triumphant in int'l tourney
articles.summary: Wushu Arena Philippines, a traditional martial arts school based at Fisher Mall, Quezon City, concluded its campaign at the 2026 International Traditional Wushu Championship hosted by the…

blocks.text: Wushu Arena Philippines, a traditional martial arts school based at Fisher Mall, Quezon City, concluded its campaign at the 2026 International Traditional Wushu Championship hosted by the International Kung Fu Union Federation, securing 2 gold, 16 silver, and 18 bronze medals across traditional internal and external wushu styles.

The 15-athlete delegation — Luyi Corpuz, Anton Sesdoyro, Armando Soriano Jr., Diane Basa, Faith Dapon, Ishy Tantiangco, Jhune Beatriz, John T Duran, Juana Marcelino, Phoebe Ragos-Ty, Reena Cabugao, Sha Liwanag, Sia Villarosa, Sunshine Reyes, and Laurice Ricamara — competed in Children A, Children B, Youth Group, Junior Group A, and Junior Group B divisions in disciplines ranging from Shaolin Barehand and DitangQuan to Emei Sword, Kinarra Staff, and Taichi Duilian. Faith Dapon and Luyi Corpuz brought home the team's two gold medals in Shuang Shanzi and Lian Ren Bu Quan respectively.

The team entered the tournament as IKUF's officially designated Kung Fu team for the July–August 2026 championship cycle. Head Coach Arra Jeuneze Corpuz, a certified IKUF international judge for internal arts and Taichi, also served as an External and Internal Kung Fu Judge for western countries during the same competition.

The result builds on the school's existing international track record of well over a hundred medals accumulated across the Hong Kong International Wushu Championships and the Emei Cup International Wushu Championships in Chengdu, China.
Recognition beyond the mat

Alongside the team's competitive results, Arena Fitness Dojo and Wushu Arena Philippines have been named a finalist for the Ten Outstanding UN SDG Awards (TOUSA) People Award and a shortlistee for the Zero Project 2027 Awards under the #ZeroCall27 cycle, run by Austria's Essl Foundation — two international recognitions tied to the program's "Movement Is for Every Body" advocacy rather than to competition results.

"This result belongs to every athlete who showed up to train even on the days it was hard," said Corpuz. "We built this program on the idea that traditional wushu, done right, can compete anywhere in the world — and our athletes just proved that."
An inclusive model that is getting global attention

Unlike many competitive wushu programs, Wushu Arena Philippines operates under an open-door policy — welcoming children, adults, seniors, and students with special needs regardless of prior experience or athletic background. This philosophy previously earned the school recognition as an official member of the Martial Arts Coalition for Sustainable Development (MCS), a UN ECOSOC-linked coalition advancing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, making it one of the only Philippine organizations on the coalition's international map.
About the team

Head Coach Arra Jeuneze Corpuz is a 2nd Degree Black Belt (Nidan) in Aikido under Aikido Philippines and Aikikai Hombu Dojo Japan, a two-time Excellent Coach Awardee from the Hong Kong and Chengdu international competitions, and an Overseas Wushu Ambassador Awardee.

Supporters can stay updated on the team's ongoing achievements and future endeavors by following their journey on Facebook: fb.com/wushuartsacademy or their website: https://sites.google.com/view/teacherarra/wushu-kung-fu

articles.title: ‘Alarm bells were going off’: parents tell of ordeal at Send school closed down after abuse allegations
articles.summary:
Annette and Kevin Maxwell say children with special needs have become moneymaking tool for private companies

Annette and Kevin Maxwell were nervous about sending their son Jonah to a…

blocks.text: Annette and Kevin Maxwell were nervous about sending their son Jonah to a residential home for children with special educational needs and disabilities (Send). Jonah has severe autism – he is non-verbal, has epilepsy and behavioural problems and needs round-the-clock care.

“It was a huge decision, but we almost had no choice because with Jonah at home, you can’t work and we had two other children to think about. He’s beautiful, but he is very, very complicated,” said Annette. “Outsourcing parenting is just foreign to us and it’s horrible, but we didn’t have another option.”

When he first arrived at St Christopher’s in Bristol, Jonah was thriving, receiving different therapies and doing activities such as horse riding. Then, in 2016, the charity that ran the home collapsed and the centre was acquired by the Aurora Group, which runs more than 30 Send schools and is owned by Octopus, an investment management and real estate company.

The Maxwells, who live in Bath, noticed a change almost immediately. They said the food quality went downhill, an overnight nursing position was cut and they began to have concerns about Jonah’s wellbeing. Whenever he came home to visit he seemed very tired.
“Alarm bells were going off. But every time we spoke to management and staff, they would always reassure us that everything was OK,” said Annette.

blocks.caption: Jonah Maxwell allegedly suffered physical abuse from staff at St Christopher’s in Bristol. Photograph: Adrian Sherratt/The Guardian

blocks.text: At this point, the Aurora Group was being paid £292,000 a year by their local authority to care for Jonah. The company was expanding rapidly by acquiring several established providers to become one of the UK’s largest specialist education and care operators.

Then, in 2019, it was announced that St Christopher’s was being closed down by Ofsted after serious allegations of child cruelty came to light. Vulnerable children had to move out at short notice, their belongings hastily packed into black bin bags. They were sent across the country to new placements.
The police began an investigation into alleged child cruelty and safeguarding concerns and this concluded after two years without any criminal charges being brought.

The Maxwells were told by police there had been allegations involving Jonah. In one incident, he was said to have been roughly grabbed and shoved into his room by a staff member. They also found out a carer had allegedly been waking him up every two hours through the night to go to the toilet to avoid having to clean soiled sheets, which police said could be classified as child cruelty.
“I just wish I’d been more pushy at the time and tried harder to get to the bottom of things. I really, really regret that I didn’t do more,” said Annette.

blocks.caption: Annette and Kevin Maxwell are pushing for stricter laws to ensure private Send providers are subject to the same levels of accountability as other schools. Photograph: Adrian Sherratt/The Guardian

blocks.text: Police later confirmed they were unable to interview the directors of the Aurora Group, who parents believed had questions to answer over cost-cutting that may have contributed to alleged abuse. Child cruelty legislation applies only to those who directly commit an alleged offence.
St Christopher’s was classified as a school, not a care provider, meaning it could not be investigated under legislation that might implicate both a corporation and individuals.
Kevin said: “Our kids have become a moneymaking tool for these companies, and they squeeze it, because they know that, ultimately, they can walk away. There has to be better accountability.”
The couple pursued civil action against Aurora, alleging a breach of Jonah’s human rights. The company agreed to pay £18,600 without admission of any guilt.
The Maxwells are pushing for stricter laws to ensure private Send providers face the same levels of accountability and transparency as other schools.
As part of sweeping Send reforms announced earlier this year, the government promised to “crack down” on private companies running schools, imposing fee caps and minimum standards.

blocks.caption: Jonah playing with his mother at St Christopher’s in 2015. The school was shut down suddenly in 2019. Photograph: SWNS.com

blocks.text: Those in the sector said they had been raising the alarm for years and urged the government to create more state schools in the Send sector to wrest back control from private companies, which charge significantly more.

Darren Northcott, the national officer for education at the NASUWT teaching union, said: “There is a big problem where public money which should be being spent on children, young people and the staff working with them is leaking out of the system in the form of profits and surpluses. That’s not acceptable.”

He said many Send schools, in the state and private sector, had become incredibly challenging places to work because of a lack of staffing or resources to deal with children with complex needs. He said staff were increasingly expected to accept violence from children as “part of the job” and in some cases “the level of care and investment in staff falls short of would reasonably be expected”.

Hayley Harding of the Let Us Learn Too campaign said many parents were frustrated by the lack of Send places in state schools, leaving private providers as the only option for many. “There’s a huge issue with local authority capacity and lack of planning – for so many years they have been firefighting, rather than actually planning for how many children need this,” she said.
“Nobody wants people making profit out of our children. But we want them to be educated, and that’s often the only option available.”

A spokesperson for the Aurora Group said it was the only B Corp accredited provider in the sector. B Corp certification is a private credential for for-profit companies that prove high social and environmental standards through independent evaluation. Aurora also said 96% of its services were rated by Ofsted as good or outstanding.

The spokesperson added: “St Christopher’s was in serious difficulties under different ownership and under close Ofsted scrutiny when we responded to a campaign to keep the school open. We invested substantially in improving staffing, facilities and overall provision.

“We regret that we were ultimately unable to overcome the school’s challenges, and we remain saddened by the circumstances surrounding its eventual closure in 2019. We did all that we could at the time to support the Maxwell family and wish them well.
“The police thoroughly investigated the allegations and agree that we did all we could to support their inquiries. Police took no further action.”

The spokesperson said all the Aurora Group’s profits were reinvested in establishing new schools in partnership with local authorities, bringing “relief to families and making it far easier for children to go to school nearer to home”.
