articles.title: Iconic Burnham Lake in Baguio City is opened to public after P150-M rehab
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY – Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority (TIEZA) Operating Officer Mark Lapid led the opening of the P150-million worth of rehabilitation of the famous Burnham Lake, which…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY – Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority (TIEZA) Operating Officer Mark Lapid led the opening of the P150-million worth of rehabilitation of the famous Burnham Lake, which is the first highlight of the 117th Baguio Day celebration, this morning, September 1.

“Finally, it’s finished although there was a delay due to weather, but now it’s okay and we can start the rehabilitation of the children’s park and Rose Garden, so we can see the total rehabilitation of the entire Burnham Park. Apart from this, we also have a rehab on Session Road, which we will start after the Panagbenga celebration next year,” Lapid said.

blocks.caption: TIEZA Operating Officer Mark Lapid, along with Mayor Benjamin Magalong, Congressman Mauricio Domogan and city officials, led the opening of the new rehabilitation of Burnham Lake during the 117th Baguio Day celebration, this morning, September 1. (Photo By Zaldy Comanda)

blocks.text: TIEZA Operating Officer Mark Lapid, along with Mayor Benjamin Magalong, Congressman Mauricio Domogan and city officials, led the opening of the new rehabilitation of Burnham Lake during the 117th Baguio Day celebration, this morning, September 1. (Photo By Zaldy Comanda)

“Burnham Park is the heart of Baguio, when I was a kid, I used to go here for sightseeing, boating, biking, so it is an honor that we were given a position in the government and we were able to help beautify it”

Mayor Benjamin Magalong said Burnham Lake and its surroundings have changed a lot. “The water is now clean because the lake was filled with rain, there is a walkway and there are new boats that will be placed here and coil and carp fish, to help with pollution.”

He said that boat riders will no longer have difficulty boarding the boat because there is a deck for safety and they will have insurance from P350 to pay and will be required to use a safety vest, because the lake is deeper now
He also said that the beauty of the lake now is that there is a pathway where you can jog in addition to the pathway that will be placed around Burnham Lake.

“The big issue in this project is funding, fortunately TIEZA is there to help us beautify the entire Burnham Park. Hopefully before the end of this year, the Children Park and Rose Garden will also be finished,” Magalong said.
According to Magalong, the beautification of our iconic Burnham Park, which is the main attraction in the Summer Capital, is a huge help for the city of Baguio.
Magalong also announced that there are other projects in the pipeline, the initial P500-million water sewer system of Burnham Park and the rehabilitation of Session Road from TIEZA funds.
Lapid was the guest honor and speaker at the Baguio Day celebration in recognition of his great contribution to the city’s tourism projects.

articles.title: Who could succeed Gesmundo? JBC invites 5 senior justices
articles.summary: Leonen and four senior SC justices were invited to apply.

blocks.text: September 1, 2026 | 1:40pm
A hall at the Supreme Court building in Manila in an undated image.
SC PIO

MANILA, Philippines — The Judicial and Bar Council has invited five senior Supreme Court associate justices to apply for chief justice ahead of Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo's retirement in November.

Supreme Court spokesperson Camille Ting told Philstar.com Tuesday, Septemeber 1, that the JBC invited Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen and Associate Justices Alfredo Benjamin Caguioa, Ramon Paul Hernando, Henri Jean Paul Inting and Rodil Zalameda.
Ting said the JBC has followed the practice since the early 2000s of inviting five senior associate justices to apply as a matter of courtesy and recognition of their seniority.
"What began as an informal practice has since become a standing JBC policy," Ting said.
The invitation does not guarantee inclusion in the JBC shortlist that will be submitted to the president for appointment.
Gesmundo is set to retire on Nov. 6. Applications for chief justice will be accepted until 4:30 p.m. on Oct. 13.
His retirement will give President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. his first opportunity to appoint a chief justice.
Marcos made his first Supreme Court appointment in June 2025 when he named Associate Justice Raul Villanueva to replace retired Associate Justice Mario Lopez.

articles.title: P200-M flood control infrastructure to protect thousands living in riverside communities in Agusan del Sur
articles.summary: BUTUAN CITY – Thousands of riverside community folks may now have some measure of security whenever heavy rains come after two of Gibong River Bank flood control infrastructure worth almost P200…

blocks.text: BUTUAN CITY – Thousands of riverside community folks may now have some measure of security whenever heavy rains come after two of Gibong River Bank flood control infrastructure worth almost P200 million in Las Navas and La Suerte, both in Prosperidad town, Agusan del Sur province, recently became operational.

These two flood control protection infrastructure are eagerly anticipated projects for the thousands of community folks, especially farmers who frequently experience anxiety and worry during bad weather conditions that causes flood.

The construction of Gibong River Bank slope protection structure along Barangay Las Navas is already 96.68 percent complete, and only the remaining works of parapet and concrete slabs are being undertaken by the Agusan del Sur 1st District Engineering Office (DEO) of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH-1st District DEO).

“This 186.0m length Las Navas project is hitting its timeline of completion by the end of this month of September,” said DPWH 13 Assistant Regional Director (ARD) Engr. Vincent Roderick “Bong” M. Acebes, in an interview with The Manila Bulletin on Tuesday, Sept. 1.
He said round-the-clock ground works are being undertaken by the engineers and personnel of the 1st District DEO and assigned contractor to hit their target timeline of completion.
“The completion of Las Navas project is tentatively by the end of this month (September),” ARD Acebes pointed out.
On the other hand, the 182.4m length construction of flood control structure in La Suerte area, also along Gibong River is already 100% complete, only on Thursday, Aug. 27, this year.

These two flood control structures that started in the middle of 2025 was built by the DPWH to ensure the safety of residents and their properties from flooding, particularly farm lands in these areas, also said DPWH 13 Regional Director Sabeniano D. Caliao, Jr.
He said the instruction of our DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon was to finish these projects to ensure the safety of our community folks and land properties of farmers, the DPWH 13 top official added.

“It is a long-awaited project as raging flood waters forced our locals living along this giant Gibong River to leave and reside in a safer place. With the total completion of these flood control structures, they are now better protected and their safety is ensured,” also said Agusan del Sur solon Rep. Adolph Edward “Eddiebong” Plaza.
Plaza expressed heartfelt gratitude to the DPWH for the completion of these projects in Sabang Gibong River Bank.

articles.title: LTFRB warns PUV drivers vs road bullying, summons bus operator
articles.summary: The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) warned operators and drivers of passenger buses and other big motor vehicles to refrain from bullying smaller ones following a viral…

blocks.text: The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) warned operators and drivers of passenger buses and other big motor vehicles to refrain from bullying smaller ones following a viral counterflow video which the agency described as dangerous and disrespectful.
Acting LTFRB chairman Greg G. Pua, Jr. was referring to the overtaking incident involving a bus of the Victory Liner that forced a motorcycle rider to stop and pull over alongside the road.

“Roads are not the place of bullying of big motor vehicles to smaller ones, we will not allow that and those who would dare do that in the public transportation sector will suffer consequences,” said Pua.
What made it dangerous is that the overtaking and counterflowing happened on the blind or curved side of the road, which forced a rider to pull over alongside the road.
Pua said the entire incident was captured on the video which served as the basis for the show cause order (SCO) issuance when the LTFRB monitored it on social media.

In the SCO, the LTFRB asked the bus operator to explain in writing why its Certificate of Public Convenience (CPC) should not be suspended or cancelled over the dangerous driving behavior of one of its drivers.
The same document stated that the passenger bus endangered road users and the act committed by the driver falls under failure to provide safe and convenient public transportation service.
The bus firm is also facing an administrative case of employing a reckless driver, according to Pua.
The hearing of the case is on September 10.
Pua reminded public utility vehicle (PUV) drivers to behave and always observe road courtesy and discipline in the interest of the safety of all road users.

“Road crashes are preventable and one of the key factors is discipline and respect to all fellow road users. On the part of the LTFRB, we will pursue accountability against those who would defy that,” said Pua.

articles.title: Philippine manufacturing surges to near-decade high in August as output, orders accelerate
articles.summary: Philippine manufacturing activity accelerated sharply in August, with factory conditions improving at their strongest pace in nearly a decade as production growth hit its fastest rate since 2016 amid…

blocks.text: Philippine manufacturing activity accelerated sharply in August, with factory conditions improving at their strongest pace in nearly a decade as production growth hit its fastest rate since 2016 amid stronger demand.

In a report on Tuesday, Sept. 1, S&P Global said its Philippines manufacturing purchasing managers’ index (PMI) climbed to 54.9 in August from 51.8 in July, marking the fourth consecutive monthly increase and the strongest improvement in the health of the sector since December 2016.
A PMI reading above 50 indicates an overall improvement in manufacturing conditions compared with the previous month, while a reading below 50 signals a deterioration.

“The Filipino manufacturing sector continued to build momentum in August, moving on from the flat performance seen in the previous quarter, when activity was affected by the conflict in the Middle East. Encouragingly, production rose at its fastest pace since 2016, helped by stronger demand conditions,” S&P Global Market Intelligence economist Maryam Baluch said in a statement.

Manufacturing output rose substantially during the month, with the pace of growth accelerating from July to its fastest since December 2016. Firms attributed the increase to stronger underlying demand and greater production efficiency.

Inflows of new work also rose at the fastest rate in six months, supported by new product and model launches, higher repeat business, and a broader customer base. International demand likewise improved, with new export orders rising for the first time in six months.

The stronger order books prompted manufacturers to step up purchasing activity, which expanded at a six-month high. Stocks of purchases also increased for the first time since February despite a deterioration in supplier performance.

“Firms responded by increasing both purchasing and hiring to keep up with greater production needs. At the same time, cost pressures eased, and confidence about the year ahead improved to a 21-month high,” Baluch said.
Manufacturers also increased staffing levels for the first time in five months. Although the increase was modest, the pace of job creation was the strongest in 21 months.

Cost pressures, meanwhile, eased despite firms continuing to report higher expenses for energy, raw materials, and logistics. Input cost inflation slowed notably from July, while output charges increased at the weakest pace in the current six-month period of inflation.

Business confidence also strengthened to its highest level since November 2024, as manufacturers expecting higher output over the next 12 months cited expansion plans, new product lines, stronger order inflows, and expectations of attracting new customers.

S&P Global’s Philippines manufacturing PMI is compiled from responses to questionnaires sent to purchasing managers at a panel of around 400 manufacturers. Data for the August survey were collected from Aug. 12 to 24. - Danielle T. Bayani

articles.title: Japan, Belgium defense chiefs agree to deepen security ties
articles.summary: TOKYO, Aug. 31 (Jiji Press) -- Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and his Belgian counterpart, Theo Francken, at a meeting in Tokyo on Monday agreed to deepen security cooperation between…

blocks.text: Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi (right) and his Belgian counterpart, Theo Francken, shake hands at a meeting in Tokyo on Monday.

TOKYO, Aug. 31 (Jiji Press) -- Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and his Belgian counterpart, Theo Francken, at a meeting in Tokyo on Monday agreed to deepen security cooperation between their countries.

Koizumi welcomed Belgium's first assignment of a defense attache to its embassy in Tokyo, saying this is highly significant as the security in the Euro-Atlantic region and that in the Indo-Pacific region are becoming increasingly inseparable.
The two ministers exchanged views on regional developments and confirmed cooperation to maintain a free and open international order based on the rule of law.
Francken, who also serves as Belgium's trade minister, expressed his eagerness to strengthen defense industry cooperation with Japan.

articles.title: China warns of ‘consequences’ over Taiwan presence at Pacific Islands Forum
articles.summary:
Beijing-Taipei tensions a feature at meeting in Palau, with Australia and New Zealand saying the forum – not another country – will determine who attends

China ⁠said it had serious concerns…

blocks.text: China ⁠said it had serious concerns ⁠about Taiwan’s presence at ​the annual Pacific Islands Forum in Palau, warning of “consequences” after the democratically ruled island attended the group’s opening ceremony on Monday.
China views Taiwan as its own territory, and China-Taiwan tensions have ⁠featured prominently at the meeting, which is intended to demonstrate regional unity.

“There will always be consequences,” Qian Bo, China’s special envoy for Pacific island affairs, said of Taiwan attending the event. “It’s not a ⁠threat,” he said, without specifying what the consequences would be.

“This is objected to by all, so this should not have happened. We ​think it’s very inappropriate to do so,” he ‌told reporters on Monday after an opening ‌ceremony in Palau, an archipelago of more than 500 islands that has maintained diplomatic ties with Taiwan.
Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese, said when asked by reporters about the Chinese envoy’s remarks: “The ‌Pacific Islands Forum determines what happens here, not any other country.
“This is primarily a gathering of the Pacific family … and I look forward to the engagement.”
New Zealand’s foreign minister, Winston Peters, echoed that sentiment, saying the group did not take instructions from countries outside it.

Taiwan’s foreign minister, Lin Chia-lung, said on Monday: “Taiwan is honoured to serve as a partner in the Pacific, continuing to stand with everyone and work together to make the Pacific ‌more prosperous and peaceful.”

Lin Chia-lung was invited for meetings and side events held alongside the forum. Taiwan is not a formal dialogue partner of the forum like ​China, but a development partner. The US, EU, Britain, Canada, India and Japan are also among the 21 dialogue partners of the forum.
China has gradually whittled away the number of Pacific Island countries with formal ties to Taipei, with only three remaining: Palau, Tuvalu and the Marshall Islands.

The leaders of Fiji, Vanuatu, Samoa, Solomon Islands and Kiribati did not attend the gathering of the 18-member group that ⁠counts Australia, New Zealand and Pacific island nations as members. Ministers are attending in their ​place.

China is Australia’s largest trading ​partner but Canberra remains wary of Beijing’s expanding influence ​in the Pacific and has stepped up security and development ties with island nations to deter any ​permanent Chinese military presence in ‌the region.

Australia, New Zealand ​and the US have ​long considered the South Pacific to fall within their sphere of influence. In the latest sign of that effort, New Zealand and the US said in a joint statement released on Tuesday during the summit that they would jointly fund a major upgrade of a second world war port on a Cook Islands atoll.

articles.title: Japan FY 2027 budget requests likely to top 143 trillion Yen
articles.summary: TOKYO, Aug. 31 (Jiji Press) -- General-account budget requests from Japanese government agencies and ministries for fiscal 2027 are expected to exceed 143 trillion yen, hitting a record high for the…

blocks.text: A Japanese Finance Ministry official checks budget requests for fiscal 2027 on Monday. (Courtesy of the Finance Ministry)

TOKYO, Aug. 31 (Jiji Press) -- General-account budget requests from Japanese government agencies and ministries for fiscal 2027 are expected to exceed 143 trillion yen, hitting a record high for the fourth consecutive year.
The figure will be much higher than the 122,445.4 billion yen sought under the government's fiscal 2026 general-account budget.
On Monday, the Finance Ministry finished accepting budget requests for the fiscal year starting in April 2027.

The anticipated increase in the total requested amount reflects the government's decision to include funds for measures that have been earmarked under supplementary budgets in the initial budget and create a new investment quota with no caps set on the amounts to be sought. The new quota will be for investments in the crisis management and growth fields to create a strong and prosperous Japan.
Also, ministries and agencies were allowed to make fund requests without setting specific amounts for certain measures.
Fund requests for the new investment quota topped 10 trillion yen, the level assumed by the government in its estimates. The industry ministry made the largest request of 4,525 billion yen.

Debt-servicing costs will likely balloon due to an increase in coupon payments reflecting rising interest rates. As a result, the overall budget request for fiscal 2027 is expected to go up by over 2 pct from 140,612.6 billion yen, the combined amount of the fiscal 2026 initial budget and the fiscal 2025 supplementary budget.
The health ministry made a record budget request totaling 36,580.3 billion yen.

While the size of the Defense Ministry's latest budget request is almost the same as that for the previous year, many of its requests did not show specific amounts as the government is set to update the country's three major national security documents later this year.

The Finance Ministry plans to secure a record 36,638.6 billion yen to cover debt-servicing costs in fiscal 2027, up by 5,362.8 billion yen from fiscal 2026. The growth reflects a hike in the assumed long-term interest rate to 3.8 pct from 3.0 pct.

Voicing plans to strictly scrutinize the submitted requests, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said at a press conference Tuesday last week that the requested funds "should naturally contribute to growth or induce private investments."
"We hope to build a strong economy and realize fiscal sustainability at the same time in an integrated way under our responsible and proactive fiscal policy," she said.

articles.title: JBC invites 5 SC senior justices to apply for Chief Justice post to be vacated by Gesmundo on Nov. 6
articles.summary: The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) has invited the five senior associate justices of the Supreme Court (SC) to apply for the Chief Justice post that would be vacated on November 6 with the compulsory…

blocks.text: The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) has invited the five senior associate justices of the Supreme Court (SC) to apply for the Chief Justice post that would be vacated on November 6 with the compulsory retirement of Chief Justice Alexander G. Gesmundo.

In a message to journalists, SC Spokesperson Atty. Camille Sue Mae L. Ting said that those invited by the JBC were Senior Associate Justice Marvic M.V.F. Leonen and Associate Justices Alfredo Benjamin S. Caguioa, Ramon Paul L. Hernando, Henri Jean Paul B. Inting, and Rodil V. Zalameda.

It was presumed that since Associate Justice Amy C. Lazaro-Javier – who is currently the fourth senior associate justice -- is compulsory retiring at age 70 on November 16, she was no longer invited to apply and her place was given to Associate Justice Zalameda.
The five associate justices may apply or may be nominated. However, they have the option to decline the nomination.

Ting said that “since the early 2000s, the JBC has followed the practice of inviting the five most senior associate justices to apply for the Chief Justice post as a matter of courtesy and in recognition of their seniority.”
“What has begun as an informal practice has since become a standing JBC policy,” he also said.
The deadline for the submission of the application or nomination for the Chief Justice post will be at 4:30 p.m. on October 13.
Applicants or those who will submit nominations must visit the JBC website – www.jbc.judiciary.gov.ph – for the complete details and guidelines.

Under Section 7, Article VII of the Constitution, a member of the SC – including the Chief Justice – must be a natural-born citizen, at least 40 years of age, and has served as a lower court judge or practiced law in the Philippines for 15 years or more. He or she must be a person of proven competence, integrity, probity, and independence.

The JBC -- the constitutional office that accepts, screens, and nominates appointments to the judiciary, the Office of the Ombudsman and its deputies, and members of the Legal Education Board – is mandated to submit at least three nominees to President Marcos for appointment.
Whoever is appointed by the President would be his second appointment to the SC. His first appointee is Associate Justice Raul B. Villanueva.
If the President has not appointed Gesmundo’s replacement after the submission of the JBC’s nominees, Senior Associate Justice Leonen will be acting Chief Justice starting November 6.

articles.title: Piercing, not earpiece: Chiz debunks image of Ortonio as AI-generated
articles.summary: Viral photo falsely showed the Office of the Vice President witness wearing an earpiece.

blocks.text: September 1, 2026 | 1:34pm

MANILA, Philippines — A viral image supposedly showing Office of the Vice President official Lemuel Ortonio wearing an earpiece while testifying last week was AI-generated and false, impeachment court presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero said Tuesday, September 1.
The image circulated on social media alongside claims that Ortonio was being coached during his testimony in Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial.

"After Mr. Ortonio testified before this court, an image of him allegedly wearing an earpiece was widely circulated on the internet. We take this opportunity after verification that it was an AI-generated image and simply false," Escudero said.
Escudero said what could be seen on Ortonio's ear was a piercing on the front fold helix, not an earpiece.
He nevertheless reminded parties that witnesses must testify solely from their own knowledge and without coaching or influence from lawyers or other people.

"No witness, while testifying, shall possess, have access to or use any earpiece, headset, cellphone, smartwatch, smart glasses, or any other similar device capable of transmitting or receiving information or communication," Escudero said.

"Witnesses are also prohibited from receiving or attempting to receive any communication, suggestion, answer, signal, message or prompt for any person whether inside or outside of this court," he added.
Escudero also directed court personnel to secure prohibited communication devices from witnesses before they are sworn in and obtain their confirmation that they understand the rules.
Ortonio, an OVP assistant secretary and assistant chief of staff, was declared a hostile prosecution witness when he testified last week on allegations involving the office's confidential funds.
His testimony forms part of the proceedings on Article I of the impeachment case, which involves allegations over the use of confidential funds by the OVP and the Department of Education.

articles.title: PNP-ACG nabs suspect over illegal online sale of registered SIMs in Bulacan
articles.summary: A 26-year-old man was arrested after allegedly selling registered SIM cards online in an entrapment operation in Obando, Bulacan, the Philippine National Police (PNP) Anti-Cybercrime Group (ACG) said…

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 1:33pm

A 26-year-old man was arrested after allegedly selling registered SIM cards online in an entrapment operation in Obando, Bulacan, the Philippine National Police (PNP) Anti-Cybercrime Group (ACG) said Tuesday.

"Natunton natin ang isang tao na responsable sa pagtitinda ng mga SIM cards. So, 400 SIM cards ang nakumpiska during entrapment operations," ACG chief Police Major General Wilson Asueta said at a press briefing.
(We have traced a person responsible for selling SIM cards. So, 400 SIM cards were confiscated during entrapment operations.)
The operation was conducted on August 24.

According to the ACG, the operation stemmed from the cyber patrolling activities which monitored social media accounts allegedly involved in the illegal sale of fully verified e-wallet accounts and registered SIM cards.
The suspect identified as "Junel" had posted on Facebook offering registered SIM cards for P10 each, according to the police.
Further investigation showed that the suspect was allegedly engaged in the bulk sale of registered SIM cards.

The ACG said the suspect admitted that he personally registered some of the SIM cards using the identities of other individuals. Some of the SIM cards had already been registered when the suspect bought them from an undisclosed seller, according to the ACG.
A total of 400 registered SIM cards were seized during the operation, which will be subjected to a Warrant to Disclose Computer Data (WDCD) and further investigation.

The suspect is currently under ACG custody after undergoing inquest proceedings. He faces charges for violations of the SIM Registration Act of 2022, in relation to the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.
Meanwhile, the ACG seeks amendments to the SIM Registration Act, including the use of the Philippine National ID as the primary means of identity verification.
SIM cards should be activated only after successful registration and identity authentication, the ACG said.
According to the ACG, a requirement should be presented for proper documentation before transferring a registered SIM to another person.
SIM ownership, the ACG said, should also be limited to five per person across telecommunications providers. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Meal deal: meth found hidden inside McMuffin during a police car search in Western Australia
articles.summary:
Police say the drugs were uncovered as part of ongoing investigations into illicit drugs in Broome

A Western Australian man has been charged after police said they found approximately 3.5…

blocks.text: A Western Australian man has been charged after police said they found approximately 3.5 grams of methylamphetamine in a ziplock bag wedged between the bacon and egg of a McMuffin meal during a car search.
The arrest on 20 August was part of ongoing investigations into illicit drugs in Broome, in WA’s Kimberley region.

Police said the 39-year-old man was seen entering and leaving a house of interest under surveillance as part of the drug operation, before getting into his vehicle and driving away. He was stopped a couple of streets away for a car search at about 2.10pm.
During the search of the car, police said a bag containing hot food from the fast-food chain Chicken Treat was found on the rear floor between the driver’s and passenger seats of the vehicle.
In a video captured by police body-worn camera during the search, officers can be seen rummaging through the fast food bag on the bonnet of the car.
Several meal items, including burgers and fries from a number of different fast food outlets, are seen being pulled out of the bag along with the McMuffin.
Speaking on a WA police podcast after the arrest, Sen Const Ben Lucas said the drug-laden food immediately stood out as suspicious.

“That bag was found to contain fresh, hot, warm, lovely-smelling Chicken Treat, but at the bottom was a cold discarded McMuffin burger that had been secreted at the bottom of the bag that obviously drew our attention,” he said.
after newsletter promotion
The Derby man has been charged with one count of possession of prohibited drug with intent to sell or supply. He is next due to appear before the magistrates court on 9 September.
A woman who was also in the car and present during the search was released by police after questioning.

articles.title: Netizens share woes, tips after hours-long traffic jam along NLEX
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Several netizens shared their experiences of being stuck in traffic for hours along the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) amid flooding brought by days of torrential rains. Many…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Several netizens shared their experiences of being stuck in traffic for hours along the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) amid flooding brought by days of torrential rains.
Many towns in Pampanga province, which the NLEX runs through, were flooded as the southwest monsoon (habagat) prevailed over parts of Luzon over the weekend.

In a post shared with the Facebook group “Traffic Updates – NLEX / SCTEX / TPLEX,” a social media user said she had left La Union around 6:30 a.m. on Monday and only arrived in Taguig City at 4:30 a.m. on Tuesday.
SCTEX refers to the Subic-Clark-Tarlac Expressway, while the TPLEX refers to the Tarlac-Pangasinan-La Union Expressway.
The user noted that, due to the heavy traffic along portions of NLEX, they were prompted to take detours through the towns of Pampanga, Nueva Ecija and Bulacan.
“Parang nag-abroad lang e,” she joked.
(It was almost as though we went abroad.)
Jose Mari Chan
“Grabe ka, NLEX! Nakapag-staycation tuloy kami sa iba’t ibang provinces at lugar… Imagine, nakapaglibot kami! Inabutan tuloy kami ni Jose Mari Chan sa daan!” she added.
(You’re something else, NLEX! We managed to take a staycation in many different provinces and places… Imagine, we got around! We were even greeted by Jose Mari Chan on the road!)
Chan is a beloved figure in Philippine music, best known for his Christmas carols often used to usher in the local celebration of the Yuletide season as early as September.
The social media user explained that she was on the way to Metro Manila for her third chemotherapy session.
“This kind of situation really makes you realize how crucial accessible and passable roads are, especially for patients who need to reach hospitals urgently,” she said.
Although she said she was grateful to have returned home, she stressed, “We Filipinos deserve better.”

Another social media user said she and her family had left their flooded home in Apalit town, Pampanga at 9 a.m. on Monday, but they only arrived at a relative’s home in Dau also in the province at 5 a.m. on Tuesday.
The netizen said roads going through Apalit, San Simon and San Fernando had been impassable due to waist-deep floods at the time.
She also said they had gone to Calumpit, Bulacan in hopes of catching a big bus to pass through the flooded areas.
“We travelled back and forth from Apalit to Calumpit, to Apalit again, and back to Calumpit kase sabi meron daw libreng sakay, pero wala naman dumadating after waiting for hours,” she said.
(We travelled back and forth from Apalit to Calumpit, to Apalit again, and back to Calumpit because we were told there were free rides, but none came after waiting for hours.)
`Truck for cows’
However, she managed to get the help of a truck driver who had allowed them on board until reaching NLEX, where the vehicle could no longer bear the weight of the passengers.
“TRUCK NA PARA SA BAKA. Hindi bus, hindi rescue trucks from the government. Pero, thank you kay kuya na hindi naman utos ng gobyerno pero nagmabuting loob na subukang mahatid kami,” she noted.
(IT WAS A TRUCK FOR COWS. Not a bus, not rescue trucks from the government. But, thank you to the driver who was kind enough to try to drive us despite no order from the government.)
“Para kaming mga palaboy naghahanap ng masakayan, buti nalang may big bus na kononsider kunin kami ni lola, lalo na may mga bata,” she added.
(We felt like wanderers who could not find a ride. We were lucky to find a big bus who considered taking us since we were travelling with an elderly person and children.)
“Sana naman may natitira pang awa yung gobyerno,” she stressed.
(I hope the government still has some mercy.)
Meanwhile, another social media user said they had left Dinalupihan, Bataan at 4 p.m. on Monday and arrived in Santa Rosa, Laguna at 8:30 a.m. on Tuesday.
She noted that they had likewise taken detours through several towns in Pampanga, Nueva Ecija and Bulacan before finding their way to their destination.
“Mapapaisip ka na lang ng dito ba napupunta ung taxes ko?” she said.
(You’ll just think: is this where my taxes go?)

She urged fellow motorists to research on social media groups and on map applications to see the conditions of the roads; to fill up their gas tanks, have full meals and bring food before travelling; and to have patience on the road.

For its part, in a statement on Monday, NLEX operator Metro Pacific Tollways Corporation (MPTC) said it understood the public’s frustration, stressing that it was “deeply sorry” for the delays that motorists endured.

MPTC noted that it will be deploying concrete barriers along 300 meters northbound and 300 meters southbound along the Tulaoc Bridge in San Simon, Pampanga to serve as a temporary flood wall as well as siphoning trucks to remove the floodwater.

In a traffic advisory on Tuesday morning, the NLEX Corporation said heavy traffic was still reported in both the northbound and southbound lanes of the expressway segment near San Simon but that all types of vehicles could pass through Lane 1 segment.
Meanwhile, it added, only Class 2 and 3 vehicles, or larger vehicles including buses and trucks, could pass through Lane 2 of the segment. /mr

articles.title: Nepal floods: ‘I managed to survive, but my brother and sister couldn’t’
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — By the time 16-year-old Samir Tamang reached his school in Khalte, Rasuwa, the Bhotekoshi river had already turned into a roaring torrent of debris. Samir, an eighth grader at…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — By the time 16-year-old Samir Tamang reached his school in Khalte, Rasuwa, the Bhotekoshi river had already turned into a roaring torrent of debris. Samir, an eighth grader at Nilakantha Secondary School, scrambled up a nearby hill to save his life. But his two younger sisters—13-year-old Priya and seven-year-old Parbati—were at home. They have been missing ever since the torrent swept through their village on Wednesday.

“My youngest sister had an injury on her hand and could not attend school, so my older sister stayed back to take care of her,” said Samir, his voice breaking as he sat inside a crowded temporary holding centre at Shivalaya Basic School in Laharepauwa, Rasuwa. “I don’t know what to do anymore. My sisters were like my closest friends, and in a single moment, the flood took them away.”
The flood did not spare Samir’s home either. His father, Surya, managed to escape the deluge while his mother, Chhesang, is currently working in Kuwait.
Samir is one of hundreds of children now taking shelter in relief blocks in Rasuwa and Nuwakot following the catastrophic floods of August 26.

According to preliminary data released by the Education Ministry, 250 students and teachers remain missing across the affected districts. Out of 230 students, 213 are out of contact, while 17 have been confirmed swept away. Furthermore, 10 teachers out of 19 missing have been swept away. Severe structural damage has been reported across 23 educational institutions, including eight in Nuwakot, seven in Rasuwa, and remaining others in Dhading.

“This data was gathered through a WhatsApp group named ‘flood-affected education’, disaster management taskforce and direct updates from field officers,” said Bir Bahadur Dhami, information officer at the ministry. “Because search teams are still clearing mud and rubble, the casualty and missing figures are being updated continuously as people slowly re-establish contact.”

For 14-year-old Akash Tamang, also from Khalte, the memory of the flood is a horrifying blur. Akash had arrived early at Uttargaya Public School when he heard a terrifying roar coming from the Trishuli river. Crowds began running in panic as water inundated the compound.

“We ran towards the forest as fast as we could. Otherwise, we wouldn’t have survived,” said Akash. “The flood swallowed my school in seconds. A bus bringing students to school was also caught in the flood.”

Akash had prepared a meal that morning for his younger siblings—eight-year-old Ashwin and 11-year-old Anisha—and sent them off to Ramchandra Basic School across the border in Nuwakot. Neither has been seen since the flood.

“I managed to survive, but my brother and sister couldn’t,” said Akash, wiping away tears. Anisha was in grade three and Ashwin in grade two. Their mother, Karsang, works in Dubai, and the father, Sanukanchha, works in Malaysia.

The children had been renting a small room near Betrawati to attend school. “We had been staying in the rented room in Betrawati with the money sent by our parents. I have no idea where the river carried my siblings.”

Although children have been brought to various shelters, there is still no news regarding the whereabouts of their relatives. Fifteen-year-old Nirajan Tamang is frantically searching for his 12-year-old brother Abiral, a fourth-grader at Nilakantha Secondary School who was caught in the torrent while walking to class.

“I had already reached school,” said Nirajan with a pale face. “My brother was walking to school when he got caught in the flood. I miss him so much,” he lamented. “I don’t think we will ever find him now.” His father, Lawang, and mother, Munchi, were at home in Thiru with his youngest brother, Sachin.

blocks.caption: Flood-displaced children sheltering at the holding centre at Shivalaya Basic School in Laharepauwa, Rasuwa, pictured on Sunday.  Angad Dhakal/TKP

blocks.text: In Kalikastan of Kalika Rural Municipality, 12-year-old Anju Tamang lost her mother, Subhamaya, along with her eldest brother, brother-in-law, aunt, uncle, and a one-year-old cousin when flash floods hit Shanti Bazar. Anju, who had lost her father five years ago, is now homeless and staying with relatives at Shivalaya Basic School.

In a statement issued on Thursday, UNICEF Representative to Nepal Alice Akunga confirmed that an estimated 17,000 children have been directly affected by the catastrophe across the Trishuli and Bhotekoshi river corridors.

UNICEF warned that the children who survived the disaster are now exposed to heightened risks of disease, malnutrition, exploitation, and trauma. The agency stressed the urgent need for temporary learning spaces, instructional materials, and immediate psychosocial counseling for both traumatized children and teachers.

The disaster has also raised grave child protection concerns. On Saturday, the Ministry of Women, Children and Senior Citizens issued an urgent alert warning against the illegal transport or unlawful custody of displaced minors.

Chakra Bahadur Budha, joint secretary and spokesperson for the ministry, urged local administration units in disaster-declared zones—including Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading—to strictly monitor child movement.

“No individual or organisation is permitted to transport or relocate children who have lost their parents or homes without explicit recommendation from the local Child Welfare Officer at the local level and prior authorisation from the National Child Rights Council,” said Budha in the official notice.

The warning comes as humanitarian organizations work against time to deliver targeted aid. While early relief distributions relied heavily on instant foods, aid agencies are shifting towards nutritional security and protection.

“The immediate need is proper nutrition,” said Sher Bahadur Karki, coordinator at the Emergency Operations Centre of the Nepal Red Cross Society. “Children in holding centers are being given junk food like instant noodles, which lack essential nutrients. They urgently require protein-rich, balanced meals to prevent outbreaks of illness.”

Karki added that the Nepal Red Cross Society has deployed field officers across three primary holding centres in Nuwakot, distributing mattresses, blankets, dry rations, and clothing in coordination with local government agencies.

Meanwhile, UNICEF has mobilised specialised mental health and psychosocial support teams to assist children coping with severe loss. Humanitarian workers are also conducting systematic profiling to track down missing children, register unaccompanied minors, and facilitate family reunifications.

For local community representatives, the sheer scale of destruction has proven overwhelming. Karna Ghale, an executive member of Uttargaya Rural Municipality who lost seven relatives in the disaster, said local authorities are struggling to manage the influx of displaced families.

“I can’t think straight because of the grief,” said Ghale at the Shivalaya shelter. “All I can do right now is beg the government and aid agencies to care for these children properly. They have lost their families, their clothes, and their schools.”
Thirteen-year-old Nirmal Ghale, who fled into the woods barefoot after watching his grandparents Mingmar and Lenjom get swept away by the river, remains too terrified to think about the future.

“I was walking to school when the flood hit,” said Nirmal. “The noise was deafening. I thought I was going to die right there. I pulled off my shoes and ran into the forest. So many of my classmates were swept away. Every time I hear the river now, I panic. I don’t want to go back to school. I don’t even have a change of clothes.”

As search and rescue operations continue along the riverbanks, officials at the National Child Rights Council acknowledged that establishing a final count remains challenging. Ram Bahadur Chand, information officer at the council, said that field teams are actively coordinating with local ward offices to verify figures, locate survivors, and ensure every displaced child receives immediate state protection. /dl

articles.title: Palace on NLEx gridlock: ‘Bakit ka pa papasok kung trapik na?’
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Tuesday advised motorists to avoid the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) for now after scores were left stranded along sections of the expressway due to severe…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Tuesday advised motorists to avoid the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) for now after scores were left stranded along sections of the expressway due to severe flooding.
At a briefing, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro dismissed proposals to temporarily suspend toll fees on NLEX, saying that doing so could result in heavier traffic.
“Bakit ka pa papasok kung traffic na? Wag mo na gamitin muna. I mean, diba? For the meantime, huwag na muna kayong dumaan doon kung hindi naman din siya makakalusot,” she said.
(Why would you still go there if there’s already heavy traffic? Don’t use it for now. I mean, right? In the meantime, avoid passing through there if you won’t be able to get through anyway.)

“So anong purpose ng libre? Tanong ko lang. Magandang adhikain ‘yung libre, pero kung ililibre natin, mas maraming sasakyan na papasok. So pag mas maraming papasok na sasakyan mas lalong magkakaroon ng traffic, so dapat nga iwasan muna nila tong NLEX,” the Palace official continued.

(So what’s the point of making it free? I’m just asking. It’s a good initiative to make it free, but if we make it free, more vehicles will enter. And the more vehicles that enter, the worse the traffic will get. So for now, they should.)

Castro said there was no order from President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to sanction NLEX operator Metro Pacific Tollways Corporation, as the President was focused on finding ways to ease the traffic congestion.
The heavy traffic was caused by severe flooding in the Tulaoc and San Simon Interchange sections in Pampanga, triggered by the overflowing Pampanga River due to persistent monsoon rains.
As of 6:15 p.m. on September 1, heavy traffic was still reported in the northbound and southbound lanes of the Tulaoc (San Simon) and San Simon Interchange.
Despite the heavy traffic, the NLEX corporation said all types of vehicles could pass through Lane 1, while Class 2 and 3 vehicles could pass through Lane 2 of Tulaoc (San Simon).

On Monday, Metro Pacific Tollways Corporation said it understood the public’s frustration and apologized for what motorists—especially those traveling with children, elderly passengers, or individuals needing medical attention—had to go through.
Lane 1 of San Simon Interchange is passable by Class 2 and 3 vehicles, except for Class 1 vehicles.

Meanwhile, the corporation said that the Libtong, Sta. Rita Northbound Entry, and Pulilan Northbound Entry are temporarily closed to all vehicles while approximately two-kilometer traffic buildup is observed at the Sta. Rita Northbound Exit. /jpv

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — Four people reported missing after the Bhotekoshi floods were found dead in India, with Indian police handing over their bodies to Nepal Police on Sunday.

The bodies were recovered from a river in India’s Maharajganj district and handed over to Nepal Police, according to Madan Thapa, deputy superintendent of police at the District Police Office in Nawalparasi West.
The bodies have been kept at Prithvi Chandra Hospital in Parasi for identification.
In Nawalparasi West, authorities have so far recovered 54 bodies and 28 human remains along the banks of the Narayani river following the floods.

Authorities are preparing for the DNA tests on the recovered remains and, after identification, will bury those that remain unclaimed in a pit dug at Mulpani Community Forest in Sunwal Municipality. /dl

articles.title: Sotto: No person behind alias? Then, it's a 'fake name'
articles.summary: Senator-judge Vicente "Tito" Sotto III on Tuesday, Sept. 1, clarified that Philippine law allows the use of pseudonyms only for specific literary and entertainment purposes, distinguishing these from…

blocks.text: Senator-judge Vicente "Tito" Sotto III on Tuesday, Sept. 1, clarified that Philippine law allows the use of pseudonyms only for specific literary and entertainment purposes, distinguishing these from fictitious or fake names.
Senator-judge Vicente "Tito" Sotto III (Senate PRIB photo)
Sotto made the clarification during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, citing Republic Act No. 6085, the law regulating the use of aliases.

“The general rule, Mr. President, that she mentioned is Republic Act 6085, regulating the use of aliases. It's only allowed in the Philippines only for pseudonyms, solely for literary, cinema, television and other entertainment purposes,” Sotto said.
Sotto said the existence of a real person behind a name determines whether it is an alias.
“If there is a person behind the alias, then it is an alias,” he said.
“If there is no person behind the name, it is a fictitious name or a fake name,” he added.
Sotto made the manifestation after reviewing the impeachment court's journal concerning the previous trial's questioning of private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia by Senator-judge Robin Padilla.
He said he wanted to clarify the matter after seeing a newspaper report stating that Divinagracia had been prevented from answering and had been cut off several times.
Sotto said the journal showed that Divinagracia was able to answer most of Padilla's questions, although there were one or two instances when she was cut off.
He said Divinagracia was discussing RA 6085 when she was interrupted and that the court allowed her to answer, although she was unable to elaborate further.
Sotto said he was making the clarification “just for the record” and for the information of the public and members of the impeachment court.
Presiding Officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero acknowledged Sotto's manifestation.

articles.title: Japan govt asks eastern city to accept N-waste site survey
articles.summary: HITACHIOMIYA, Ibaraki Pref., Aug. 31 (Jiji Press) -- The industry ministry on Monday asked the city of Hitachiomiya in Ibaraki Prefecture, eastern Japan, to accept a literature survey for selecting a…

blocks.text: Sadayuki Suzuki (left), mayor of Hitachiomiya, Ibaraki Prefecture, eastern Japan, receives from a senior industry ministry official at a meeting in the city Monday a written request for a literature survey on the selection of a final disposal site for high-level radioactive waste from nuclear power plants.

HITACHIOMIYA, Ibaraki Pref., Aug. 31 (Jiji Press) -- The industry ministry on Monday asked the city of Hitachiomiya in Ibaraki Prefecture, eastern Japan, to accept a literature survey for selecting a final disposal site for high-level radioactive waste from nuclear power plants.

If realized, Hitachiomiya would become the fifth site in the country to accept a literature survey, after the town of Suttsu and the village of Kamoenai, both in the northernmost prefecture of Hokkaido, the town of Genkai in the southwestern prefecture of Saga and Minamitorishima, a remote Tokyo island in the Ogasawara chain in the Pacific.
This is the second case of the central government seeking approval for the literature survey without a request from local communities.

Senior ministry officials visited Hitachiomiya and handed a written request to Mayor Sadayuki Suzuki. "I view the request very positively," the mayor said, adding that he wants to make a final decision after hearing from the city assembly.

Industry minister Ryosei Akazawa later told reporters at his ministry in Tokyo that he is grateful to Suzuki for taking the state's request seriously. "The government will take the initiative in approaching other municipalities to expand the areas subject to literature surveys," he added.
Hitachiomiya is located in the northwestern part of Ibaraki and borders Tochigi Prefecture.

The city was included in the scientific features map released by the central government in 2017, which listed sites where the possibility of favorable features to host a final disposal facility, such as no volcanoes or active faults nearby, being found is relatively high. Although Hitachiomiya is landlocked, parts of the city are located some 20 kilometers to the coast, making it favorable from a transportation perspective as well.

The literature survey, the first stage of the three-tier selection process, is aimed at examining the possible effects of volcanoes and faults based on geological maps and scientific papers over a period of about two years.

The consent of the prefectural governor and the heads of relevant municipalities is required to proceed to the second and third stages--preliminary and detailed investigations. The overall selection process is said to take a total of some 20 years.
Ibaraki Governor Kazuhiko Oigawa said he will "closely watch" how the city of Hitachiomiya will respond.

articles.summary: About 600 people remain stuck in several devastated hydropower stations that have become the focus of rescue efforts, while Prime Minister Balendra Shah says over 11,000 people have been rescued…

blocks.text: DISASTER. Members of the Nepal Army head back after collecting the bodies that were washed away by flash floods and a mudslide, in Narayani River, Chitwan, Nepal, August 31, 2026.
Navesh Chitrakar/REUTERS

About 600 people remain stuck in several devastated hydropower stations that have become the focus of rescue efforts, while Prime Minister Balendra Shah says over 11,000 people have been rescued across the affected region

items: Nepali rescuers are working to rescue nearly 300 trapped workers and have restored power and communication lines in some areas after devastating floods caused by a glacier collapse, which have resulted in at least 939 deaths.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah reported that over 11,000 people have been rescued, and efforts are focused on hydropower stations where many remain trapped, with aid contributions exceeding $42 million.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

KATHMANDU, Nepal – Nepali rescuers built temporary bridges to reach remote areas and dug through the ruins of hydropower projects in the Himalayas to rescue close to 300 trapped workers, nearly a week after devastating floods left a trail of destruction across the country’s towns and valleys.

About 600 people remain stuck in several devastated hydropower stations that have become the focus of rescue efforts, while Prime Minister Balendra Shah said over 11,000 people have been rescued across the affected region and power and communication lines had been restored in some areas.
At least 939 people have been killed in the destruction, Shah said in a late-night social media post.
“Thousands of citizens have lost their homes, families, loved ones and property,” he said.
“The government understands the immense pain they are enduring. The path ahead is to support them through this suffering and help them return to normal life through rehabilitation.”
Rescue teams had managed to restore road networks to Nuwakot, one of the worst-affected districts, facilitating rescue operations and distribution of relief material, Shah said.
A glacier collapse triggered a deluge of ice, rock and mud which swept through the impoverished nation’s border region with China, posing a massive challenge for Nepal’s six-month-old government.
Police official Bipin Regmi said a search team recovered 24 bodies from a house in Betrabati village in Nuwakot district.
“We are reaching new areas and recovering bodies,” Regmi told Reuters.
Aid worth more than $42 million had poured into the country after the disaster, Shah said, and the government expected the contributions to increase.
Neighbors India and China, between whom Nepal is wedged, were helping with rescue efforts, including building bailey bridges to reach remote affected areas.
Shah said 279 workers had been rescued from hydropower projects so far where authorities estimated that close to 1,000 people were trapped.

Pictures and videos shared by rescue teams showed earth-moving equipment digging and shovelling mud and rocks under lights in the dark of the night as workers watched. Soldiers used torchlight in a big pit they had created to look for space to get into one tunnel.

There has been a boom in hydropower projects in Nepal since the turn of the century as the mountainous country sought to take advantage of its Himalayan water resources to address chronic domestic power shortages and exploit prospects for selling electricity to southern neighbour India.

Hydropower projects in Nepal’s mountains need tunnels to carry water through the steep terrain, allowing developers to exploit the sharp elevation drop between Himalayan rivers and powerhouses to generate electricity.
Shah said the catastrophic event signaled the growing risks that the Himalayan region faces.

“The region must therefore remain vigilant. The time has come for us to strongly raise before the international community the disasters we are experiencing as a consequence of climate change,” Shah said in his post.
Last week’s flood was “caused by glacier instability under the long-term effects of global warming,” China’s state broadcaster said on Monday. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Several Luzon areas get nearly 3 months’ worth of rain in August, says PAGASA
articles.summary: Several areas in Luzon recorded nearly three times their normal rainfall in August as heavy rains from the southwest monsoon or “habagat” contributed to unusually high monthly rainfall totals, the…

blocks.text: Several areas in Luzon recorded nearly three times their normal rainfall in August as heavy rains from the southwest monsoon or “habagat” contributed to unusually high monthly rainfall totals, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said.

PAGASA weather specialist Benison Estareja said during a press conference on Tuesday, Sept. 1, that La Trinidad, Benguet recorded the highest accumulated rainfall in August at 2,868.7 millimeters from Aug. 1 to 31.
The amount was equivalent to 298 percent of the station’s normal August rainfall of 963.3 millimeters.
“Halos pang tatlong buwan na ulan yung inulan po sa La Trinidad Benguet for the month of August 2026 (La Trinidad, Benguet received nearly three months’ worth of rain in August 2026),” Estareja said.
Iba, Zambales followed with 2,630 millimeters of rainfall from Aug. 1 to 31, equivalent to 284 percent of its normal August rainfall.
Baguio City recorded 2,626.26 millimeters of rainfall for the month, compared with its normal August rainfall of 963.2 millimeters. This was equivalent to 273 percent of normal.
The figures showed that Iba and Baguio City also received nearly three times their normal August rainfall, Estareja said.
Abucay, Bataan recorded 2,210 millimeters of rainfall, placing it among the top five stations with the highest rainfall totals for August.
However, no comparison with its normal August rainfall was available because it is a new PAGASA station.
Olongapo City, meanwhile, logged 2,100 millimeters, or 243 percent of its normal August rainfall.
Although not part of the top five, the PAGASA Science Garden monitoring station in Quezon City also recorded a significant amount of rainfall at 1,510 millimeters for the month.
This was equivalent to 266 percent of its normal August rainfall of 568.5 millimeters.

“Nakakontribute po yung ganito karaming ulan na 1,500 millimeters nung August 8, nung August 17, nung August 29 (The rainfall amounting to 1,500 millimeters was contributed by the rains on Aug. 8, Aug. 17, and Aug. 29),” he said.

Broadcaster Ray Hadley has told a Sydney court that an alleged victim…

blocks.text: Broadcaster Ray Hadley has told a Sydney court that an alleged victim of Alan Jones confided in 2019 he’d been “sexually assaulted” by the fellow 2GB broadcaster on a number of occasions.
“He said [Jones] put his hand on my cock and kissed me,” Hadley told the Downing Centre local court on Tuesday.
Jones is on trial on 20 charges of indecent assault and two counts of sexual touching against six complainants. The 85-year-old has pleaded not guilty.
“I asked him if he was homosexual and whether he was consenting to it,” Hadley told the court when giving evidence.
“He broke down and cried and said ‘No, I hated it. I’m not homosexual.’”

Hadley was questioned by the prosecutor Georgina Wright about the conversation he had with the alleged victim, known as complainant C. He was also questioned about later putting him in contact with a journalist from the Sydney Morning Herald.
Hadley said he promised C he would not reveal his identity and he would keep his disclosure secret. The conversation lasted between 30 and 40 minutes, Hadley told the court.
“At varying stages, he broke down and sobbed,” Hadley said. “I just stopped, let him compose himself, offered my support, and let him continue.”
C earlier told the court he confided in Hadley in 2019 that he had been inappropriately touched by Jones in 2008.
“I broke down and I said ‘He’s a fucking grub, he used to grab me on the cock, he used to kiss me’,” C told the court.
“Ray just listened. I just broke down sobbing. I said ‘He [Jones] is a fucking cunt, he’s just a cunt’.”

Hadley on Tuesday said: “I wanted to go across the other side of the desk and give him a hug, but I just kept telling him it wasn’t his fault. He was a victim, and he didn’t have to explain to me that he should have rejected the advances.”
Hadley told the court that C had also mentioned a luncheon where “Jones brought him to sit next to him, and during the luncheon he was touching his cock under the table”.
Hadley said C told him that two guests at the lunch, including broadcaster Jason Morrison, were “laughing and giggling at what was happening” and C said he felt “embarrassed” and “helpless”.

Jones’s defence barrister Gabrielle Bashir SC said in her opening address last month that the allegations against her client were “trial by media” fuelled by the hatred and jealousy of his 2GB radio rival Hadley.
“You will see evidence in Hadley’s own words of his resolve to destroy Jones and to one by one, tear his supporters apart,” Bashir said.
The court heard part of the defence case is that two SMH journalists, columnist Peter FitzSimons and chief investigative reporter Kate McClymont, were “looking for a story”.
“Unfortunately, rumours and media coverage are at the heart of more than a reasonable possibility of contamination or reconstruction in this case,” Bashir said.
Bashir alleged that Hadley “wanted to destroy” Jones and to “tear him apart”.
“Rivalry, treachery, double-dealing, money, hatred, desperation, opportunism and more” were at the “heart of this case”, Bashir said in the opening of the judge-only trial.
Bashir alleged that Hadley passed on information to the SMH about complainant C who had worked for Jones as a driver.

On Monday, a 2GB staffer told the court there was a fierce rivalry between Jones and Hadley over the coveted breakfast slot in 2019, when Jones was nearing the end of his contract and Hadley wanted to move from the Ray Hadley Morning Show to breakfast.
“My understanding is Mr Hadley had signed a secret contract to replace Mr Jones while Mr Jones was coming off contract,” James Willis told the court.
“And while this was meant to be a secret, it had spread throughout the corridors enough that our team, including Jones, had been aware of it.”
The trial before judge Glenn Walsh continues.

articles.title: LG unveils their evolution of an AI home at IFA 2026
articles.summary: LG is unveiling the next evolution of its AI Home at IFA 2026. Bringing together AI-powered appliances, connected services and contextual intelligence, LG AI Home simplifies daily routines, enhances…

blocks.text: LG is unveiling the next evolution of its AI Home at IFA 2026. Bringing together AI-powered appliances, connected services and contextual intelligence, LG AI Home simplifies daily routines, enhances convenience and delivers a more personalized and intuitive customer experience.
A Home That Understands You

LG AI Home analyzes schedules, routines, the home environment and appliance usage to recommend appropriate actions and optimize coordination between devices and services. By providing personalized suggestions based on real-world context, it proactively supports customers to spend less time managing their appliances and more time enjoying life. To illustrate this vision at IFA 2026, LG invites visitors to explore immersive AI Home spaces—spanning living, kitchen and rest zones—where they can experience firsthand how LG’s AI technologies coordinate devices and services around different everyday routines.
ThinQ Claw: Extending AI Home Through Chat and Contextual Intelligence

At IFA 2026, LG is introducing ThinQ Claw, a new text-chat-based AI agent experience that further enriches and expands the company’s AI Home offering. Built on the concept of OpenClaw and optimized specifically for LG AI Home, ThinQ Claw can understand user intent and context and help complete tasks by connecting and coordinating relevant services and devices.

ThinQ Claw interprets updates shared by the user within the context of their life, rather than as isolated events. This enables it to recommend (or help initiate) appropriate actions aligned with personal preferences and the unique demands of each situation. It can manage cooking appliances to help the user prepare for hosting guests, monitor indoor air quality and temperature before the user arrives home to create a more comfortable environment based on current conditions, or suggest tailored experiences to entertain, empower or relax.

Beyond appliance control, ThinQ Claw works collaboratively with daily services like calendars and other connected services. Instead of requiring complex automation rules, it allows users to share their plans or current status through a natural chat interface. In addition to being able to understand requests and determine the necessary steps, ThinQ Claw can remember customers’ likes and dislikes, leading to increasingly personalized experiences over time. This intelligent and context-aware agent expands how customers engage with AI Home by providing increasingly personalized support both inside and outside the home. ThinQ Claw will be demonstrated at LG’s AI Home Zone throughout IFA 2026.
An Expanded AI Home Ecosystem

The AI Home Zone highlights LG’s open AI Home ecosystem powered by Homey, a smart home platform developed by Athom, which LG acquired in 2024. With its broad interoperability across brands and connected devices, Homey enables a safe and reliable connected home experience.

Homey allows users to manage diverse products from different manufacturers and service providers in one place. Through a comprehensive Home Energy Management System (HEMS) demonstration, IFA visitors can observe how Homey intelligently orchestrates energy generation, storage and consumption in real time by connecting smart meters, solar panels, home batteries and EV chargers with LG appliances. HEMS can help reduce household electricity bills by optimizing when energy is generated, stored and consumed, while taking advantage of dynamic energy pricing where supported.*

IFA 2026 will also mark the European debut of LG ThinQ Pro. Designed for multi-family residential and commercial environments, ThinQ Pro supports the efficient management of devices and facilities while illustrating how LG’s AI Home vision extends beyond the home into shared and professional spaces.
Applied across the entirety of the AI Home ecosystem, the LG Shield security framework helps protect connected appliances, services and customer data, enabling safe and secure AI experiences.

“ThinQ Claw marks the next step in LG AI Home, illustrating how AI can understand customer intent and life context to support a more personalized and streamlined daily experience,” said Baek Seung-tae, president of the LG Home Appliance Solution Company. “LG will continue advancing AI Home through innovations that are increasingly intuitive and responsive to customers’ needs.”

articles.title: Gov’t explores cheaper feedstocks to raise bioethanol blend, cut fuel imports
articles.summary: The government is exploring cheaper feedstock sources as it looks to increase the country’s bioethanol blend and reduce dependence on imported fuel, according to the Department of Agriculture (DA).…

blocks.text: The government is exploring cheaper feedstock sources as it looks to increase the country’s bioethanol blend and reduce dependence on imported fuel, according to the Department of Agriculture (DA).

The DA said the government is studying the prospect of raising the bioethanol blend from 10 percent to 15 percent, or E10 to E15, in line with efforts to temper surging fuel prices in the domestic market.
Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel said the increase would rely on cheaper and more diverse feedstock sources to also protect farmers and industries that depend on these resources.
Tiu Laurel said the DA and the Department of Energy (DOE) are evaluating different feedstock options to support a higher bioethanol blend, including molasses, sugarcane juice, and corn.
“We are studying these options carefully, and there is potential for them to help bring down gasoline prices,” said Tiu Laurel.
Gasoline sold in the country is mandated to contain a locally sourced E10 blend to ensure a stable domestic market for locally produced feedstocks.

A higher E20 blend is currently implemented on a voluntary basis. There are only nine petroleum stations that offer this bioethanol blend, based on estimates from the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).
Raising the current mandatory blend requires cheaper sources, as prices of sugarcane juice and molasses, which serve as the primary feedstocks, are usually double those of imported sources.
The DA said locally sourced corn is the best candidate for an alternative feedstock to molasses and sugarcane, particularly in filling the current gap in local ethanol production.
Domestic output from sugarcane-derived feedstock averages between 325 million and 385 million liters annually, while existing bioethanol plants have a capacity of more than 500 million liters.
“To protect the sugarcane industry, only the unused capacity could be sourced from corn, which would accommodate additional production without displacing existing agricultural output,” the DA said.
The agency said it would study expanded corn production through better seeds, mechanization, and contract farming between producers and ethanol plants to support this initiative.
However, Tiu Laurel pointed out that the problem is not the availability of corn but whether it can be bought at a price that makes bioethanol commercially viable.
The DA chief also said that higher demand for bioethanol could raise corn prices for livestock raisers, who depend on the crop for animal feed.
As such, further diversifying feedstock sources is expected to reduce pressure on any single agricultural commodity and support stronger bioethanol production.
Tiu Laurel said palm oil could become another long-term feedstock for biodiesel, although he noted that plantations take about three years to mature.

Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) Administrator and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Dexter Buted earlier told reporters that the government is also looking at increasing the country’s biodiesel blend by next year.
Buted said this would hinge on whether prices of coco methyl ester (CME), which is used to produce biodiesel, would decline to a level that would not further raise petroleum prices.
He said PCA has recommended hiking the biodiesel mandate from three percent to five percent, or B3 to B5, to the DOE.

articles.title: Japan Defense Ministry eyes record 8.9-T.-Yen budget for FY 2027
articles.summary: TOKYO, Aug. 31 (Jiji Press) -- Japan's Defense Ministry said Monday that it will ask for a record 8,890.8 billion yen under the government's budget for fiscal 2027, which starts next April. The…

blocks.text: Japan's Defense Ministry in Tokyo
TOKYO, Aug. 31 (Jiji Press) -- Japan's Defense Ministry said Monday that it will ask for a record 8,890.8 billion yen under the government's budget for fiscal 2027, which starts next April.
The figure is based on the existing Defense Buildup Program, which sets the country's defense spending at around 43 trillion yen for the five years through fiscal 2027.

As the budget request includes many items for which specific amounts of necessary funds are not fixed yet, the total sum to be sought is likely to increase during the budget compilation process late this year.

With the government planning to revise the country's three key security-related documents within this year to cover fiscal 2027 and later years, spending for many related measures in the budget request was left unspecified due to possible changes based on the document update.

The fiscal 2027 budget request includes spending on measures featuring the use of artificial intelligence and drones in response to new warfare as a major pillar, as well as on organizational revamp plans, such as establishing a new agency to aid retired Self-Defense Forces members and their families.

Specifically, the ministry will introduce AI to the SDF's Joint Operations Command in order to help commanding officers make swift decisions. It will utilize existing foreign AI systems for the time being while promoting the development of domestic systems.
The ministry plans to introduce a high-security sovereign cloud as part of its AI platform.

Utilizing private-sector technologies, the ministry will start developing long-range drones that can be mass-manufactured quickly and cheaply. It will also work on developing underwater-launched hypersonic guided missiles to enhance the country's standoff defense capabilities.

Besides setting up the new agency for retired SDF members, which will have a staff of about 110, the ministry will establish three new bureaus, for international policies, defense infrastructure and facility policies.

In light of Russia's prolonged invasion of Ukraine, the ministry will put efforts into securing sustained combat capabilities. As part of the move, it will begin research on introducing cargo ships equipped with autonomous navigation technology to ensure stable supplies of goods.
Aiming to improve the country's defense equipment production bases, the ministry will newly set up an entity in charge of promoting exports of such equipment.
