articles.title: Show evidence behind ‘wasted’ Lakeshore funds, Cayetano tells Lacson
articles.summary: Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano on Tuesday, September 1, continued to defend Taguig Lakeshore’s continued public use amid claims by Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson that billions in government…

blocks.text: Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano on Tuesday, September 1, continued to defend Taguig Lakeshore’s continued public use amid claims by Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson that billions in government funds were wasted on flood control and infrastructure projects in the area.

In a social media post on National Heroes Day, Cayetano insisted that under the management of Taguig City government, Lakeshore had not been neglected or wasted under pointing to its use for health, education, leisure, businesses, and other public functions.

“Hindi po sinayang at hindi sinasayang ang Lakeshore (Lakeshore was not neglected or wasted). Let’s not let politics rob this generation and future generations of the opportunity to reap its benefits,” Cayetano said.
Cayetano made the post after Lacson said P3.713-billion in completed, ongoing, and suspended DPWH projects within alleged reclamation areas in Taguig, may have been wasted.
Earlier, Lacson also alleged other irregularities and said the findings would be submitted to the Office of the Ombudsman.
Cayetano warned that this kind of partisan politics could derail efforts to address corruption and flood control, stressing the need for evidence-based investigations that lead to accountability.
“The honest search for solutions is overshadowed by partisan politics. Corruption and flood control are perfect examples,” he said.
The senator challenged Lacson that if there is any evidence against him, or the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) or the Taguig City government, he should present it.

“If there is evidence against DPWH, Taguig, or against me, then present it. Stop the theatrics and let the evidence do the talking set in the proper judicial venue where fairness is assured,” he challenged Lacson.
The lawmaker said the focus should remain on solving problems and ensuring that public funds and government efforts are directed toward projects and reforms that benefit Filipinos.

“Every hour the government spends on political warfare instead of solving problems is wasted. Every peso spent on projects that do not serve the people is wasted. Every opportunity to reform a broken system sacrificed for personal or partisan advantage is wasted,” he said.

articles.title: House probe eyed amid SOCOTECO II–Ignite Power controversy
articles.summary: A ranking House member is seeking a congressional inquiry on proposed joint venture between South Cotabato II Electric Cooperative Inc. (SOCOTECO II) and Ignite Power and Energy Corporation (Ignite).…

blocks.text: A ranking House member is seeking a congressional inquiry on proposed joint venture between South Cotabato II Electric Cooperative Inc. (SOCOTECO II) and Ignite Power and Energy Corporation (Ignite).
General Santos City lone district Rep. Shirlyn Bañas-Nograles, vice chairperson of the Committee on Nuclear Energy, introduced House Resolution (HR) No. 1401 for this purpose.

Filed in the House of Representatives last Aug. 27, the measure directs the House Committee on Energy to conduct an investigation, in aid of legislation, into the Conditional Joint Venture Agreement (CJVA) between SOCOTECO II and Ignite.

The resolution, pending first reading, seeks to determine whether the proposed arrangement complies with existing laws, rules and regulations, while examining issues of transparency, accountability and the prudent stewardship of cooperative assets.
It also calls for an assessment of how the agreement could affect the rights and economic interests of the government and SOCOTECO II’s member-consumer-owners (MCOs).

HR No. 1401 comes with "the end in view of determining compliance with existing laws, rules, and regulations; ensuring transparency, accountability, and the prudent stewardship of cooperative assets; protecting the rights and economic interests of the government and the member-consumer-owners; and strengthening the governance and regulation of joint venture arrangements involving electric cooperatives".
Bañas-Nograles' initiative comes as opposition to the proposed partnership continues to grow.

The Social Action Center of the Diocese of Marbel (SAC-Marbel) has raised questions regarding the process by which SOCOTECO II’s Board of Directors reportedly secured authority for the proposed joint venture.

In a statement issued Aug. 20, the group alleged that Resolution No. 104 was declared adopted during the cooperative’s 43rd Annual General Membership Assembly on July 25 without a duly counted vote showing how many MCOs supported or rejected the measure.

SAC-Marbel also questioned the use of a standing vote without an actual count and called for the deferment of the plebiscite, greater transparency and accountability, and an independent investigation into SOCOTECO II’s operations.

The concerns have placed the proposed joint venture under greater public and regulatory attention, particularly on questions involving the management and long-term stewardship of electric cooperative assets.

For businesses, consumers and other stakeholders within SOCOTECO II’s franchise area, the congressional inquiry could provide an avenue for greater clarity regarding the commercial, regulatory and governance implications of the proposed partnership.

The House probe, if pursued, could become a significant step in determining whether the proposed partnership meets applicable legal and regulatory requirements and whether sufficient safeguards are in place to protect the interests of the cooperative and its consumers.

Meanwhile, a peaceful candlelight rally opposing the joint venture was held on August 29 at Plaza Heneral Santos and along Pioneer Avenue. Protesters from municipalities within the Diocese of Marbel carried banners calling for the proposed deal to be stopped and for the protection of the rights, resources and interests of SOCOTECO II’s member-consumer-owners.
The proposed plebiscite on the CJVA is scheduled over four weekends in September 2026.

articles.title: Boransing: No confi funds from Sara Duterte's DepEd in Army youth seminars
articles.summary: Army Colonel Manaros Boransing II said Tuesday his unit did not receive any confidential fund from the Department of Education during the term of Vice President Sara Duterte as Education chief for…

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 12:37pm

Army Colonel Manaros Boransing II said Tuesday his unit did not receive any confidential fund from the Department of Education during the term of Vice President Sara Duterte as Education chief for the conduct of eight leadership seminars in Mindanao provinces in 2023.
Boransing made the testimony during Day 20 of the impeachment trial of the Vice President as a witness for the prosecution.
He said that while they conducted the Youth Leadership Seminar (YLS) with DepEd, he does not know how the agency paid for its expenses in the said seminar.
DepEd provided the military with information on schools and the schedule of the students to determine their availability for the seminar.
“I have no knowledge on [DepEd’s] source of funds. I can only speak for us,” Boransing said.
“There were no DepEd funds downloaded to our unit,” he added.

Boransing was one of the military officials who issued military certifications in January 2024, which was issued on the request of then DepEd Undersecretary Michael Poa who is now one of the defense counsels of the Vice President.

Poa said he asked for military certifications in response to state auditors’ queries seeking documentary evidence on DepEd’s P15.5 million worth of confidential fund spending for rewards to informants.
Boransing said he did not know his certification will be used to justify DepEd’s confidential fund spending.
“I have no knowledge of that. I haven’t even read COA (Commission on Audit) documents,” he said.
The military official, however, did not take offense that his certification was used for justifying DepEd’s confidential fund expenses.
“I did not have any reaction,” Boransing said.
However, he could not say if he will again issue a certification if he knew that DepEd will use it to justify its P15.54 million confidential fund spending.
“It is hard to speculate what I would have done,” Boransing added. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: JBC invites 5 senior justices to apply for Chief Justice post -- SC
articles.summary: The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) has invited five senior justices to apply for the post of Supreme Court (SC) Chief Justice, which will become vacant upon the retirement of Chief Justice Alexander…

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 12:36pm

The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) has invited five senior justices to apply for the post of Supreme Court (SC) Chief Justice, which will become vacant upon the retirement of Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, the court said Tuesday.

SC spokesperson Atty. Camille Ting confirmed that the JBC invited Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen and Associate Justices Alfredo Benjamin Caguioa, Ramon Paul Hernando, Henri Jean Paul Inting and Rodil Zalameda.

“Since the early 2000s, the JBC has followed the practice of inviting the five most senior Associate Justices to apply for the Chief Justice post as a matter of courtesy and in recognition of their seniority,” Ting said in a statement.
“What began as an informal practice has since become a standing JBC policy,” she added.
Gesmundo is set to retire on November 6, 2026.
Over the weekend, the JBC opened the application and nomination process for the post.
The deadline for the submission of online applications is on October 13, 2026, Tuesday, at 4:30 p.m.

Interested applicants must visit the official JBC website for complete details and guidelines on the application requirements. They must also access the JBC Online Registration and Application System through the Philippine Judiciary Platform and complete the necessary steps.

“Applicants who have been found by the Council to have willfully made false statements, misrepresentations, or concealments of any material information as provided for under the 2020 Revised JBC Rules, as amended, shall be considered disqualified from being nominated by the Council or may be subject to perjury,” the JBC said.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: AfD's Ulrich Siegmund has plans for Saxony-Anhalt and beyond
articles.summary: The AfD's lead candidate in the upcoming election aims to turn his small federal state into a blueprint for right-wing extremist politics across Germany.

image.caption: Ulrich Siegmund, leading in the polls, plays the role of a charismatic charmer in his public appearances and visibly enjoys the campaign grindImage: Christian Schroedter/IMAGO

blocks.text: All eyes are on Saxony-Anhalt this week, ahead of a state election on Sunday that could trigger a political earthquake across Germany.

Though the state is small, with a population of just 2 million — and with economic strength and life expectancy the lowest of any of Germany's 16 federal states — a victory for the Alternative for Germany (AfD) could usher in the first far-right government in the history of post-World-War-II Germany.

The AfD's lead candidate is Ulrich Siegmund, and polls show him well in the lead. The only open question seems to be whether the AfD will be able to secure an absolute majority of the seats in Saxony-Anhalt's parliament, which would allow it to govern alone. This would appear to be Siegmund's only path to the state premiership, as the other parties have said they will not enter a coalition with the AfD.
What if Germany's far-right AfD party wins in Saxony-Anhalt?

Things are going well for the 35-year-old Siegmund. As he tours his state on the campaign trail, he draws crowds — even in small towns. He's often surrounded by a swarm of international journalists: from Canadian and Danish television, Swiss broadcasting, the BBC and the British magazine The Economist, alongside dozens of reporters from across Germany. Everyone wants to know: Who is Ulrich Siegmund?

The candidate was born in the small town of Havelberg, Saxony-Anhalt, in 1990. He joined the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU) at age 19, only to leave the party five years later and join the AfD. A former perfume salesman, he cuts a dynamic and athletic figure: slim, handsome and fresh-faced.

Above all, he is cheerful — playing the role of a charismatic charmer in his public appearances. When he steps into town squares to a cheering crowd, he beams back, shaking hands and cracking jokes. Nothing about him seems forced; he visibly enjoys the campaign grind.
"I don't know when there was last such a high approval rating, even among young people," Siegmund told DW. "It's simply enormous." He speaks quickly, articulately and with practiced ease.
AfD, right-wing influencers battle for young voters
AfD campaign pushes policies with 'high-gloss marketing'
Even critical observers in Saxony-Anhalt can't help but admit that the AfD has all the momentum in this election.

"The AfD's campaign events run like clockwork, both logistically and in terms of political strategy," observed David Begrich of Miteinander, an organization based in the state capital of Magdeburg that fights right-wing extremism. "It is high-gloss marketing of their own policies."

But what exactly do the AfD's policies aim to achieve? To judge by Siegmund's campaign speeches, the goal is a return to a bygone era — a time before Germany viewed itself as a country of immigration, when electricity came from nuclear power plants rather than wind turbines, and when LGBTQ+ rights were not yet recognized. Siegmund wants to pursue, as he says in his campaign speeches, politics "from the people, for the people!"

Apparently, that doesn't include all the people living in the state. The AfD's "100-day immediate action plan" contains some radical policies, including a key promise to "deport from minute one" foreign nationals who have no legal right to stay, but whose presence is tolerated for humanitarian reasons, many of whom have found work and established their lives in Germany.
Germany's freedom of art under threat?

The action plan also calls for funding cuts to pro-democracy NGOs, forcing refugees to work and prioritizing a love for the German homeland over social diversity. There are significant legal doubts, however, about whether a state government actually has the authority to implement all these pledges.
Controversial figures behind the scenes

There are also doubts over the "clean" image that Siegmund has cultivated. He has not been able to escape the allegations of cronyism that have dogged the AfD, after it was reported that several of the party's state and federal lawmakers secured well-paid jobs for their friends and relatives in the offices of other AfD officials.
Siegmund himself found a position for his own father. While not illegal, the move was poorly received, even within his own party.

Then there are the people behind Siegmund, those who support him as leader of the AfD's parliamentary group in Saxony-Anhalt. According to the daily newspaper Die Welt, the group employs four former members of a now-banned neo-Nazi organization, the Heimattreue Deutsche Jugend (German Youth Loyal to the Homeland). Before it was outlawed, the group openly admired Adolf Hitler's Nazism and adhered to his racial ideology, one that led to the murder of 6 million Jews and hundreds of thousands of Sinti and Roma in the Holocaust.
German activists target neo-Nazis with trademark law

Siegmund himself appears to have no qualms about associating with supporters who have tattoos or clothes with neo-Nazi symbols. DW observed him appearing arm-in-arm with men wearing neo-Nazi attire and sporting tattoos such as the Black Sun, a recognized symbol among neo-Nazis.
AfD wants to 'turn Saxony-Anhalt into a testing ground'
But what would all this mean if the AfD actually did take power after the September 6 election?

"There are clear indications that if the AfD were to enter government, it would turn Saxony-Anhalt into a testing ground for the whole country," said Begrich. "Just how far can one go in overriding the written — and perhaps even more importantly, the unwritten — rules of democratic culture in a federal state?"
For that reason, many churches, trade unions, civil society organizations and political parties have warned against an AfD victory. Begrich shares their concerns.

blocks.caption: AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund is using social media and merchandise to push his message in Saxony-AnhaltImage: Heiko Rebsch/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: "Naturally, things will become difficult, above all, for those in society who either belong to minorities or do not fit into the AfD's ideological worldview," he said. "The social climate would inevitably shift to an authoritarian regimentation — and that poses a problem for people who need liberal openness in society as they need air to breathe."
Like many critics, Begrich believes that winning Saxony-Anhalt is only the first step for a party that wants to take over the entire country.
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: Tinio questions OP’s secret funds, seeks fair transparency rules
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – ACT Teachers party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio on Tuesday questioned why nearly half of the Office of the President’s (OP) proposed budget next year falls under secret funds, a…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – ACT Teachers party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio on Tuesday questioned why nearly half of the Office of the President’s (OP) proposed budget next year falls under secret funds, a query left unanswered after lawmakers opted to forego questioning.

The House Appropriations Committee voted 37-5 to swiftly end debate on the OP’s P10.1 billion proposed budget, cutting short discussions after the panel deferred questioning over its spending plan due to parliamentary courtesy.
But Tinio pressed his point, urging transparency be applied across all agencies.

“Why is it that almost half of the budget of the Office of the President is confidential and intelligence funds?” he told lawmakers in Filipino, as around P4.56 billion was earmarked for spending beyond traditional scrutiny.

Confidential and intelligence funds are to be spent on surveillance and intelligence information gathering activities, according to a 2015 joint circular between the Commission on Audit (COA) and several agencies.

Tinio said the OP should explain its allotments meant for secret expenses, amid claims that Vice President Sara Duterte misused secret funds that had formed a key plank of impeachment efforts against her.
“If P612.5 million in confidential funds is under scrutiny… why is the Office of the President not explaining why its confidential and intelligence funds are that big?”, he said.
“We need a fair application of the principle of transparency,” he added.
Executive Secretary Ralph Recto said that President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. has the right to hold secret funds as the nation’s chief executive.
He also noted that COA had rendered an unmodified opinion on OP’s finances, which he described as “the highest opinion ever for all government agencies.”

“The president is the chief executive officer. The president is the head of state, so his first job is to ensure law and order and that is where confidential funds are being used,” he told reporters in mixed English and Filipino.
“To the intelligence fund, he is the commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, and that is important for national security,” he added. /gsg

articles.title: More countries join Nepal flood rescue efforts
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — In the aftermath of the August 26 Bhotekoshi disaster, Nepal is turning increasingly to foreign governments for specialized expertise and equipment as the scale of the search,…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — In the aftermath of the August 26 Bhotekoshi disaster, Nepal is turning increasingly to foreign governments for specialized expertise and equipment as the scale of the search, rescue and recovery operation becomes clearer.

What began largely as a domestic rescue effort has evolved into an international response, with countries sending tunnel-rescue teams, forensic specialists, drones and other equipment, while Nepal seeks additional help to identify the dead and reach people who may still be trapped in difficult terrain.

So far, 903 bodies have been recovered from the disaster-hit areas, while around 4,200 people remain unaccounted for. More than 10,000 people have been rescued, including over 323 foreign nationals. About 590 foreign nationals from 32 countries are still missing, according to the Nepal Tourism Board.
After initially limiting overseas involvement, officials said Nepal has since become more proactive in seeking specialised support that is not readily available domestically.
“The Nepal government has become more proactive since Sunday in seeking logistical and technical assistance from foreign governments,” an official at a diplomatic mission in Nepal told the Post.
The immediate need is increasingly about reaching places that conventional rescue operations cannot easily access and identifying victims whose remains have yet to be matched with families.

India and China, Nepal’s two immediate neighbors, have deployed specialized tunnel-rescue teams to work alongside Nepali security personnel at hydropower projects in the disaster-hit areas. An 11-member Indian team is working at Mailung, the site of the Chilime Hydropower Project, while a nine-member Chinese team has been deployed at the Upper Trishuli 3A project site in Syabrubesi, according to the Foreign Ministry.

India’s assistance has also extended from rescue to the identification of the dead. An 18-member team of Indian forensic experts specialising in DNA analysis has arrived in Kathmandu and is working with the Nepal Police Central Forensic Science Laboratory and Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital.

“The team has arrived in Kathmandu and is working with the Nepal Police Central Forensic Science Laboratory and Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital to analyze DNA samples,” Indian ambassador Naveen Srivastava said on X.

blocks.caption: A Nepali Army personnel leads affected women to safety at the No. 1 Military Training Centre in Bidur, Nuwakot, after being rescued by helicopter from flood-affected areas along the Bhotekoshi river in Rasuwa and Nuwakot. RSS

blocks.text: As the authorities struggle with the large number of unidentified bodies, Singapore is preparing to contribute another specialized capability. The Singapore Police Force is deploying officers trained in Disaster Victim Identification (DVI) at Nepal’s request, according to the Singapore Embassy in New Delhi, which is accredited to Nepal.

Singapore will also provide humanitarian supplies from civilian sources and the Singapore Armed Forces. Its assistance is expected to complement the forensic work already being undertaken by Nepal and India, as authorities try to establish the identities of those killed.

The need for such support has become more urgent as the authorities confront not only the number of dead but also the logistical difficulties of recovering and preserving remains. Nepal has already received airtight body bags, with additional supplies being sent by India and China, while it has sought more freezers for storing bodies.

The government is also looking beyond immediate rescue operations to technology that could help search the rugged and inaccessible terrain. It has requested LiDAR equipment from the United States, as well as DNA testing kits and other essential non-food items and services, according to Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Lok Bahadur Poudel Chhetri. LiDAR uses laser pulses to measure distances and can generate detailed three-dimensional maps, potentially helping authorities assess difficult terrain and search areas affected by the disaster.

Nepal has also requested Bailey bridges and high-capacity drones. Some Bailey bridges have already been received, while high-capacity drones are expected from China and Singapore. Japan and the Republic of Korea are also expected to provide specialised equipment soon, the officials say.

South Korea has already deployed a rescue team to the affected areas with drones and other equipment. Australia, meanwhile, has sent 12 response personnel to Kathmandu, including crisis-response and consular officers and members of the Australian Federal Police. The team is supporting the crisis response alongside Australian officials already in Nepal.
The Australian government has raised its humanitarian support for the disaster to $8 million. As many as 42 Australians remain missing in the floods.

Beyond the specialised equipment and personnel, the international response is beginning to address more basic needs arising from the destruction. Relief materials already received from India, China, the United Arab Emirates and other countries include bridge units, generators, solar lamps, emergency rescue equipment, tents, blankets, sleeping bags, food and medicines.

Chhetri said they are expecting more assistance from countries including the UAE, Myanmar, the United States, Qatar, the United Kingdom, Australia, South Korea, Japan, New Zealand, Malaysia, Singapore, Bangladesh and Pakistan, as well as international organisations including the United Nations, World Health Organization, World Food Program and UNICEF. Nepal is also receiving financial assistance from foreign governments and development partners.
The focus remains on finding those still missing, recovering and identifying the dead, and helping communities along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river corridors begin to recover.

The disaster has also required close coordination with China over Nepalis affected or stranded on the Chinese side of the border. The Foreign Ministry and Nepal’s missions in China are in constant contact to collect and share information about Nepali nationals, Chettri said.
“The Chinese side has facilitated the return of Nepali nationals from Tibet through Hilsa and other border points,” he said on Monday.

Nepal and China have also been exchanging information in real time on hydrological and meteorological conditions, including flood risks, avalanches, glacial lakes and other water-induced disasters, Chettri said.

Foreign assistance is likely to become even more important as Nepal moves beyond the immediate rescue phase. The government is conducting a preliminary assessment of its needs, while a detailed post-disaster needs assessment will determine the scale of support required for rehabilitation and reconstruction. The National Planning Commission will lead the preparation of the Post-Disaster Needs Assessment, according to Chettri. /dl

articles.title: Boransing insists: No Duterte offices’ funds in Army youth summits
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Not a single peso — whether regular allocations or confidential funds (CF) — from Vice President Sara Duterte’s offices was received or used for the youth leadership summits…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Not a single peso — whether regular allocations or confidential funds (CF) — from Vice President Sara Duterte’s offices was received or used for the youth leadership summits conducted by the Philippine Army (PA), Col. Manaros Boransing II said on Tuesday.

During the resumption of Duterte’s impeachment trial, Boransing was asked by prosecution lawyer Reynaldo Robles whether the Army’s Youth Leadership Summit (YLS) and the Information Education Communication (IEC) campaign — two anti-communist recruitment initiatives — were funded by the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd).

Robles asked this as the DepEd under Duterte cited the YLS and the IEC as activities that would justify the use of their CFs in 2023. In response, Boransing said they did not receive any CF from Duterte’s offices, and only PA funds were used, and local government unit (LGU) allocations for local partners.
“There was no funding released to the 1st Infantry Division from DepEd, sir, of any source,” Boransing said.

“How about funding, by way of confidential funds, provided by the offices identified with the respondent Vice President Sara Duterte, particularly the OVP, Office of the Vice President, or the Vice President Security and Protection Group or VPSPG, were there funding provided from those offices for your YLS and IEC activities in 2023?” Robles asked.
“For 2023 sir, there were no funds from other government agencies released to 1st Infantry Tabak Division, sir,” Boransing added.
The Army official also clarified that they did not receive even regular funds from OVP, DepEd, or VPSPG.

“I was asking you about confidential funds, now let me ask you about funds in general, confidential or otherwise, how much funding was provided or downloaded to your unit by the DepEd, for your conduct of the YLS and IEC activities for 2023?” Robles asked again.

“As I earlier said, no funds whatsoever or any amount was downloaded to the 1st Infantry Tabak Division for 2023 for the Youth Leadership Summit and Information Education Communication campaign, by any government agency sir,” Boransing answered.

Robles’ inquiry was similar to the questions thrown at Boransing and other PA officials who attended an October 17, 2024, hearing of the House of Representatives’ committee on good government and public accountability — which probed allegations of anomalous CF use within the Vice President’s offices.

During that hearing, Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro — who eventually became chairperson of the committee on justice and lead public prosecutor — observed that DepEd under the Vice President made it seem that they used their CF for the YLS and IEC when it was the PA and LGUs that shouldered most of the expenses.
Luistro made this conclusion after asking Boransing which agencies’ funds were used for the YLS, as the DepEd claimed to have allocated P15 million of its CF.

When Boransing said that they used their own funds, Luistro asked retired former Education Undersecretary and Maj. Gen. Nolasco Mempin if it was true that DepEd did not allocate funds for the YLS since it is an AFP program.
Mempin replied in the affirmative.

However, Luistro was able to solicit a confirmation from the Commission on Audit (COA) that the acknowledgement receipts used by DepEd to show that the P15 million CF was spent for the YLS. However, DepEd labeled this disbursement as reward to informers.

Boransing and other PA officials told the House panel that they would have not given DepEd certifications for the YLS if they knew that DepEd would use these to justify confidential expenses for rewards to informants.
Boransing is the eighth witness presented by the prosecution for Article I of the Articles of Impeachment, or the allegations that the CFs for Duterte’s offices were misused.

Prior to Boransing, the prosecution panel presented two Land Bank of the Philippines officials from which OVP and DepEd withdrew their CFs; COA auditors who checked on the offices’ confidential expenditures; and OVP staffers like former special disbursing officer Gina Acosta.

Last August 24, Acosta testified before the impeachment court that she released OVP’s CFs Col. Raymund Dante Lachica of the Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group (VPSPG) even though she knew that Lachica was not a bonded officer.

Like Boransing, Acosta also appeared before the House committee on good government and public accountability. During a November 2024 hearing of the panel, Acosta also admitted that it was Duterte who ordered the release of CFs to Lachica. /jpv

articles.title: Cops seize P748,000 shabu, arrest 2 in upscale CDO community
articles.summary: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — A late afternoon anti-narcotics operation shattered the quiet of Villa Ernesto Subdivision, one of this city’s established upscale residential enclaves in Barangay Gusa,…

blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — A late afternoon anti-narcotics operation shattered the quiet of Villa Ernesto Subdivision, one of this city’s established upscale residential enclaves in Barangay Gusa, leading to the arrest of a high-value individual and the seizure of approximately P748,000 worth of suspected shabu on Monday,

Operatives from the City Drug Enforcement Unit (CDEU) and the City Mobile Force Company (CMFC), in coordination with the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency Region 10 (PDEA-10), conducted the operation against the suspect at around 5:42 p.m.

The joint operation, supervised by CDEU chief Maj. Aldren Baculio and Cagayan de Oro City Police Office (COCPO) Director Col. Dexter Paje, resulted in the apprehension of the high-value target along with an accomplice.
Law enforcers confiscated roughly 110 grams of suspected shabu during the raid.
The suspects are currently detained and face charges for allegedly violating the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002 (RA 9165)./coa

articles.title: Nepal floods: Families seek answers in relatives’ final phone signals
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — Roshan Kumar Joshi, an environmental expert from Morang who worked on the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project under a Korean company, has been out of contact since last week’s…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — Roshan Kumar Joshi, an environmental expert from Morang who worked on the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project under a Korean company, has been out of contact since last week’s devastating floods in central Nepal. Joshi’s relatives have scoured social media for videos, photographs and maps that might offer a clue to his whereabouts. They have also inquired with other company employees.

“One of the colleagues who reportedly talked to him for the last time said she heard him sending his colleagues outside, shouting, ‘Run, run quickly,’” one of Joshi’s relatives said. “We have no idea what happened after that.”

On Saturday, Joshi’s relatives asked police authorities to trace the last location of his mobile phone. The response was: “Ramche-C, 9:10, 2026/08/26.” This indicated that Joshi’s phone was in the direction of the “C” sector of the Ramche tower in Rasuwa at 9:10 am on August 26.
Based on the location data, his family has now taken to social media, appealing to authorities and others involved in the search to look in that direction.

As Wednesday’s catastrophic floods along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers crippled communications across Rasuwa and Nuwakot, families searching for missing relatives have turned to an unlikely source of hope—the last signal from a mobile phone. Relatives are increasingly asking law enforcement authorities and telecom companies to check when a missing person’s phone was last active and which mobile tower it was connected to.

Telecommunications experts say the data cannot pinpoint a person’s exact location. What it can do is offer important clues about whether the missing person was near the river when the floods struck or was moving towards higher ground.
The family of Chitragupta Bhatta, a resident of Archale, Rasuwa who worked at Trishuli Hydropower Company Limited, is also clinging to a faint hope offered by his mobile phone’s last known location.

On Sunday, Bhatta’s family approached security personnel to check his last location. They received one response: “Neupane Chaur, 9:26, 8/26.” This indicates Bhatta’s phone was on for more than 15 minutes after the flood current hit the area. A telecom expert who knew the area well guessed he probably was inside the tunnel.

“After learning about this location, we began to hope that perhaps he is inside a tunnel,” a family member told Kantipur on Monday. “So many days have passed, and he was already somewhat frail. It is becoming increasingly difficult to hold on.”

A mobile tower typically divides its coverage area into three sectors, usually named A, B, or C, allowing network operators to identify the general direction from which a handset was connected, said Nabin GC, director for delivery and service at Huawei Nepal.
“The three sectors cover different directions,” GC said. “By mapping the direction geographically, we can determine whether the phone was on the river side or the mountain side.”

blocks.caption: Relatives of the missing people at Maharajgunj-based TU Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu. Photo: Nepal Photo Library

blocks.text: If a phone was last connected to a sector facing the river before losing contact, it could indicate that the person was directly exposed to the flood. A final signal from a sector facing higher ground, however, may suggest they were moving towards safety.
The information can help narrow search areas. It, however, cannot establish whether a missing person is alive or dead, experts say.

Individuals cannot directly access that data as privacy laws prevent telecom operators from handing it over to them. But government agencies and security bodies can request network information through authorized channels for search and rescue operations.
GC, who also heads Huawei Nepal’s disaster response ‘war room’, said the government could use real-time network monitoring and tracking systems to support rescue efforts.
“As a technology company, our primary responsibility is to keep the network running,” he said. “But during a disaster, the government should also make effective use of mobile and network data.”

Nepal Telecom spokesperson Kamal Lamichhane said the company has been providing available information to rescue agencies through official and legal channels, including security bodies and the Cyber Bureau.

“Our priority after power supplies were disrupted in affected areas was to keep voice calls running,” Lamichhane said. “To conserve battery power, we initially shut down data and other services and operated only 2G services.”
An Ncell representative said its tracking team responds immediately when requests arrive through government channels.

“A phone can disappear from the network because it was damaged by water or because its battery ran out,” the representative said. “Disconnection does not necessarily mean the person was caught in the disaster. They may have reached safety and simply run out of battery.”
Ncell said it had provided free services to around 300,000 customers in the three affected districts.

Nepal Telecom, Ncell, Huawei, Nepal Police and the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority have all received a growing number of requests from families seeking information about missing relatives through their phone numbers.
Sushil Kumar Shrestha, a senior divisional engineer at the disaster authority, said around 2,300 people have so far reported relatives missing.
“In a situation like this, even a mobile number can offer a faint hope,” he said.

Telecom officials said requests to trace missing people’s phones surged after the floods. Previously, such requests were more commonly linked to stolen phones or suspects fleeing after financial fraud.
Both Nepal Telecom and Ncell said they have been directing families to file requests through police because location data cannot legally be shared directly with the public.
“Because of legal provisions protecting personal privacy, we cannot provide location information directly to individuals,” Lamichhane said.
Huawei, meanwhile, has set up a help desk after receiving repeated requests from families asking the company to check the status of missing relatives’ phone numbers.

Huawei does not provide location data directly to the public, GC said. Instead, authorized agencies including the Home Ministry and Nepal Police have been given access through telecom operators to relevant systems.
“Government agencies can log into the system and check the status of phones reported missing,” he said.
The government and disaster management authority are also analyzing broader network data to estimate how many people may still be missing.

Shrestha said technicians and specialists in information technology and telecommunications are comparing the number of phones active in affected areas before the disaster with those that went offline afterwards and those that have since reconnected.

The analysis, however, cannot establish an exact number of missing people. A phone may be switched off because its battery has died or because it has been damaged, while children and elderly people may not have had phones at all.
An emergency communications restoration team formed by the government is also compiling a list of numbers that lost network connection during the floods and have not returned to the network.
A team member said the data could help produce an estimate, but not a definitive count.

“We have to account for other reasons a phone may be offline, including a drained battery or physical damage,” the official said. “Not everyone, particularly children and elderly people, carries a phone. So the data alone cannot tell us exactly how many people are missing.”

On August 26, when the floods struck that morning, there was a sharp and widespread loss of mobile connectivity between 8:30 am and 9:45 am along the corridor stretching from the Nepal-China border to Betrawati, network monitoring data show.

An elderly couple surnamed Subedi who had travelled to Rasuwa also lost contact that day around that time. Worried family members back in Kathmandu scrambled to find out the couple’s last phone signal.

A day later, the location showed “Gosaikunda-B, 08/27”, around 25-30 kilometers away from the flooded Bhotekoshi river basin. The couple had lost contact after their mobile phone battery died. They returned home the next day. /dl

articles.title: Leviste’s Solar Philippines unloads ₱3-billion SPNEC shares to anonymous investor, cuts stake to 11.5%
articles.summary: Leviste-led Solar Philippines Power Project Holdings Inc. (SPPPHI) has further pared its stake in SP New Energy Corp. (SPNEC), selling ₱3 billion worth of shares to an undisclosed buyer as founder…

blocks.text: Leviste-led Solar Philippines Power Project Holdings Inc. (SPPPHI) has further pared its stake in SP New Energy Corp. (SPNEC), selling ₱3 billion worth of shares to an undisclosed buyer as founder Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste continues his corporate exit.
In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Tuesday, Sept. 1, SPNEC reported that SPPPHI sold approximately 2.4 billion common shares at ₱1.25 per share.
The transaction reduced SPPPHI’s stake in the renewable energy (RE) firm to 11.51 percent from 16.3 percent.
Although the statement blurred out the identity of the buyer, the purchase would allow the new owner to absorb another chunk of Leviste’s remaining holdings in SPNEC.
Prior to this, Leviste had already resigned as a director of Terra Solar Philippines Inc. and SPNEC after the Department of Energy (DOE) sought to purge stalled RE projects earlier this year.

SPNEC’s equity structure is currently led by Manuel V. Pangilinan-led MGEN Renewable Energy Inc. (MGreen) with a 57.33-percent controlling stake, followed by SPPPHI at 11.51 percent, also Pangilinan-led Metro Pacific Investments Corp. (MPIC) at 3.2 percent, and the remaining balance held by a new minority investor.
Meanwhile, Meralco PowerGen Corp. (MGEN) approved a budget for the 280-megawatt (MW) Sta. Rosa solar project, even as financing details have yet to be shared with the public.

“We are waiting for the DOE to allow us to proceed by granting our request to reinstate our service contract after showing that we have been developing it and faced challenges only in meeting the GEA [Green Energy Auction] timeline,” MGEN President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Emmanuel Rubio told Manila Bulletin.

To recall, the Sta. Rosa solar facility was among the numerous projects affected when the DOE canceled thousands of MW worth of RE service contracts linked to Leviste’s firm. MGEN is actively awaiting the DOE’s decision to allow it to pursue the project.

articles.title: Escudero bans phones, earpieces for impeachment trial witnesses
articles.summary: Presiding Officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero on Tuesday, Sept. 1, ordered all witnesses appearing before the Senate impeachment court to refrain from using cellphones, smartwatches, earpieces and other…

blocks.text: Presiding Officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero on Tuesday, Sept. 1, ordered all witnesses appearing before the Senate impeachment court to refrain from using cellphones, smartwatches, earpieces and other communication devices while testifying, citing the need to protect the integrity of the proceedings.
Presiding Officer Senator Francis "Chiz" Escudero (Senate PRIB photo)

Escudero issued the directive after an AI-generated image circulated online purporting to show former Office of the Vice President assistant secretary Lemuel Ortonio wearing an earpiece while testifying before the impeachment court.
Escudero clarified that the image was not part of the official record and did not establish that Ortonio actually wore an earpiece or received outside assistance.
“The Chair therefore makes no finding against him,” Escudero said.
Nevertheless, he said the controversy underscored the need for a uniform safeguard against possible witness coaching, tampering, or outside influence.
“Testimony must be the witness’s own and must remain free from tampering, coaching, or outside influence,” Escudero said.
He cited the fundamental principle that witness testimony should remain free from coercion, coaching, or improper influence to preserve the integrity of judicial proceedings.

Escudero also referred to US cases as persuasive authority, citing a 2003 Philippine Supreme Court ruling that foreign decisions may be considered persuasive when no local authority squarely addresses a particular situation.

He cited the February 2026 US case Villarreal v. Texas, where Justice Samuel Alito, in a concurring opinion, said that when a defendant is testifying, defense counsel cannot pass notes to the witness or communicate with the witness through an earpiece.
According to Escudero, Alito explained that a witness must provide his own account in his own words rather than testimony “scripted or choreographed by counsel.”

Escudero likewise cited Sky Development, Inc. v. Vistaview Development, Inc., a 2010 US case that recognized that real-time coaching could come not only from lawyers but also from other interested persons through electronic messages.
“The Court need not wait for actual coaching to occur,” Escudero said. “Once testimony is compromised, the harm to the truth-seeking process may be impossible to cure.”

Under Escudero’s order, witnesses are prohibited from possessing, wearing, accessing or using any cellphone, smartwatch, earpiece, headset, smart glasses or other device capable of transmitting or receiving communications while testifying.

Witnesses are also prohibited from receiving or attempting to receive any communication, suggestion, answer, signal, message, prompt, or assistance from any person, whether inside or outside the session hall.
The restriction will also apply during recesses until the witness is formally discharged.
Escudero ordered witnesses not to discuss the substance of their testimony with anyone during such recesses.

Any medical, accessibility, interpretation, or evidentiary device deemed necessary, as well as consultations unrelated to the substance of the testimony, will require the prior approval of the presiding officer.

The Clerk of the Impeachment Court was directed to inform every witness of the order, secure prohibited devices before witnesses are sworn in, and obtain their confirmation of compliance on the record.
Any violation will be immediately reported to Escudero and may be dealt with under the impeachment court’s contempt and disciplinary powers.

Sony and Warner say Anthropic pirated hundreds of song lyrics and sheet music from The Beatles, Taylor Swift, Michael Jackson, and hundreds of other artists to train Claude to respond to human prompts

items: Sony Music and Warner Music have filed a lawsuit against Anthropic for allegedly misusing copyrighted song compositions to train its Claude AI models.
The complaint claims Anthropic pirated lyrics and sheet music from numerous artists, including The Beatles and Taylor Swift, and seeks damages of up to $150,000 for each infringement.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
The music publishing branches of Sony Music and Warner Music have sued Anthropic in California federal court for allegedly misusing their copyrighted song compositions to train its Claude AI models.

Sony and Warner said in the complaint, filed on Friday, August 28, that Anthropic pirated hundreds of song lyrics and sheet music from The Beatles, Taylor Swift, Michael Jackson, and hundreds of other artists to train Claude to respond to human prompts.

The lawsuit is the latest in a wave of cases brought against tech companies by copyright owners including authors, publishers, music labels and news outlets over the use of their work to train AI systems. Universal Music Group sued Anthropic in 2023 and earlier this year over the alleged use of copyrighted song lyrics in AI training, in lawsuits that are still ongoing.
Anthropic became the first AI company to settle one of the disputes last year, when it paid $1.5 billion to resolve a class action from a group of authors.

“Anthropic clearly considers that to be just the cost of doing business given that its entire business model continues to be built on copyright theft,” Sony and Warner said in their complaint. “And $1.5 billion is obviously not a large enough settlement to deter infringing conduct by a company that has parlayed such mass infringement into a staggering 2-trillion-dollar valuation.”

“This is the third lawsuit from the same lawyers, recycling allegations from cases already before the courts,” an Anthropic spokesperson said on Monday. The spokesperson also said that the company will defend itself “robustly” and that AI training makes fair use of copyrighted material, citing the judge in the authors’ case against it.
Spokespeople and an attorney for Sony Music and Warner Music did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the case on Monday.

The complaint alleges Anthropic illegally obtained the publishers’ lyrics and sheet music through torrent downloads to train Claude, and that Claude can reproduce copyrighted lyrics “verbatim” when prompted.

Sony and Warner also said Anthropic used their lyrics to teach Claude to “generate vast quantities of purportedly ‘new’ AI-generated song lyrics, which compete with Music Publishers’ legitimate copyrighted works as harmful market substitutes.”
The labels are seeking damages of up to $150,000 for each infringed copyright and a court order barring Anthropic from using their works. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Agri damage due to Habagat, Luis, Maymay, Neneng at P2.84-B
articles.summary: Agri damage due to habagat, Luis, Maymay, Neneng tops P2.84-B

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 12:10pm

The agricultural sector has incurred P2.84 billion damage and losses due to the onslaught of the enhanced Southwest Monsoon or Habagat and tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng, the Department of Agriculture (DA) said on Tuesday.

Latest assessments by regional offices showed that the agricultural damages were recorded in Cordillera Administrative Region, Ilocos Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, Bicol Region, and Western Visayas.
There were 72,803 farmers affected and 64,234 hectares of agricultural areas destroyed.
The weather disturbances have also caused 63,921 metric tons of volume of production losses in agricultural commodities.
Of the total damage and losses recorded, rice accounted for the biggest share at P1.42 billion.

It was followed by high-value crops with P761.43 million in losses. Among the affected crops are upland and lowland vegetables, spices, legumes, avocado, calamansi, citrus, durian, guyabano, honeydew, lanzones, mangosteen, melon, papaya, passion fruit, pineapple, rambutan, strawberry, watermelon, banana, mango, rootcrops, commercial crops, and ornamental crops.
Corn also suffered P103.04 million in losses. Cassava production also sustained P24.74 million in losses.
Livestock, including chickens, fighting cock, swine, cattle, carabaos, goats, sheeps, ducks, rabbits, horses, quails, and turkeys, suffered P18.94 million in losses.
Irrigation facilities and farm structures also sustained damage amounting to P68.65 million and P27.45 million, respectively. Machineries and equipment also posted damage amounting to P3.64 million.

Meanwhile, fisheries and aquatic resources sustained P412.84 million in losses. Among the affected fish produce are milkfish, tilapia, mangrove, crab, oyster, giant freshwater prawn, catfish, sugpo, and fingerlings.
Affected farmers may avail themselves of P609.79 million worth of agricultural inputs like rice, corn, and vegetable seeds.
They may also avail themselves of loans of up to P25,000 under the Survival and Recovery (SURE) Loan Program of the Agricultural Credit Policy Council (ACPC).

The DA also said the National Food Authority will also distribute 9,260 bags of palay-milled rice to affected local government units in Ilocos Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, and Mimaropa. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: House panel OKs Office of the President's proposed 2027 budget
articles.summary: The House Committee on Appropriations on Tuesday quickly approved the proposed P10.15 billion budget of the Office of the President (OP) for fiscal year 2027.

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 12:01pm
The House Committee on Appropriations on Tuesday quickly approved the proposed P10.15 billion budget of the Office of the President (OP) for fiscal year 2027.

This came after the panel, voting 37 in the affirmative and 5 negative, "extended institutional and inter-branch courtesy" to the OP and terminated further discussions and interpellations on its proposed 2027 budget. Approval was granted in less than 20 minutes.
The ruling was announced by House appropriations committee Senior Vice Chairperson Representative Albert Garcia.

House Minority Leader Representative Marcelino Libanan of 4Ps party-list initially made the motion to extend interparliamentary courtesy to the office of President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr., subject to the manifestations of some House members.
This was echoed by House Senior Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez of South Cotabato.

ACT Teachers Party-list Rep Antonio Tinio, however, objected to the motions, as he argued that the OP should answer questions regarding the flood control mess and its confidential and intelligence funds.

"Ang gusto ng taumbayan ay transparency. Kailangan patas, dapat patas ang Kongresong ito sa application ng prinsipyo ng transparency. Lakas maka-demand ng Kongresong ito ng transparency para sa Office of the Vice President, dapat ganoon din para sa Office of the President," Tinio said.

(The people want transparency. We should be fair. This Congress must be fair in applying the principle of transparency. This Congress is quick to demand transparency from the Office of the Vice President, it should do the same for the Office of the President.)
Under the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP), the OP is seeking a total of P10,155,758,000 budget, about 64% lower than the 2026 budget.

Executive Secretary Ralph Recto said the substantial reduction reflected the "lower operational requirements of [the OP's] delivery units and the completion of activities related to the Philippines' hosting of the ASEAN Summit for which no additional funding will be required next year."

"In short, we're asking for less while remaining fully prepared to do more. We believe this amount is sufficient for the Presidency to meet the exacting demands of leading the nation at a time of overlapping domestic and external challenges," Recto said in his presentation.
The OP's proposed 2027 budget is now deemed submitted for plenary consideration of the House of Representatives.

Prior to the voting, Garcia explained that House members' questions, clarifications, and suggestions regarding the OP's proposed budget will be answered "either here or at the plenary where we will have a wider platform for everyone to witness." — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Madrid residents brace for noise and disruption from new F1 circuit
articles.summary:
City council emphasises economic case for Madring amid local outrage over disruption and environmental impact

Opponents of Madrid’s newly constructed Formula One circuit have accused the…

blocks.text: Opponents of Madrid’s newly constructed Formula One circuit have accused the regional authorities of putting profit before people’s wellbeing after tests for the inaugural Spanish Grand Prix at the track later this month yielded noise levels that were almost twice the legal decibel limit.

The regional government of Madrid and the city council are hoping that the 5.4km-long (3.3 miles) Madring circuit – which has been built in the north-east of the Spanish capital at a cost of €83m (£71m) – will attract visitors, boost the local economy and put the city firmly on the motor racing map. The Madring bills itself as “a perfectly connected circuit: just 20 minutes from the city centre”.

But recent track tests using Formula Three cars have worried local people who are taking legal action over the construction of the circuit and the noise it is expected to generate. The Stop F1 Madrid platform, which was formed a year ago, said neighbours had recorded average noise levels of 102.7 decibels during the tests, with peaks of between 107.7 and 109.1 decibels. The maximum noise level permitted in residential areas is 55 decibels.

blocks.caption: Those opposed to the Madring being built say its construction will add to the urban heat island effect during the summer. Photograph: Aaron Heredia/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

blocks.text: “It’s not just about the dust and the noise,” said Antonio Ibáñez, a spokesperson. He said there had been complaints from people who argued it was impossible for them to work remotely during the tests, adding: “We’ve also spoken to people who have children with autism and they had to get them out of the area because of [all the distress].”

One of the group’s biggest worries is the huge numbers of people expected to descend on the area for the grand prix itself, putting an enormous strain on public transport and the local area. “An urban Formula One circuit is just a bad idea,” he said. “It’s a nonsense idea.”

Regional and city authorities have sought to reassure residents and are attempting to stress the economic benefits of the track. Borja Carabante, Madrid’s city councillor for urban planning, mobility and the environment, said measures, such as acoustic panels, would be put in place to minimise noise during the grand prix on 11-13 September.
He also said that the Formula Three cars used to test the track “make and emit more noise than Formula One cars, so there’ll be less noise on 13 September than there was during the tests”.

Carabante said the city council would work to ensure traffic disruption was kept to a minimum. But he called on the people of Madrid to celebrate the arrival of Formula One in the city: “We should be congratulating ourselves that Madrid is hosting such an important and significant event that will put us at the epicentre of great sporting events. It’s amazing news for all the people of Madrid and it’s putting Madrid on the map.”

The regional minister for housing, transport, and infrastructure, Jorge Rodrigo, said the event would be of huge economic benefit for Madrid, and well worth one weekend’s disruption. “It’s worth a little bit of sacrifice from all of us … given the profitability of this event for the Madrid region and the city of Madrid, and, above all, given how it’ll position us internationally.”

blocks.caption: The Spanish Grand Prix will take place at the Madring for the first time later this month. Photograph: Aaron Heredia/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

blocks.text: A spokesperson for the Madring said it was taking “all measures within our reach to minimise the disruption caused by the construction work and the event”, adding: “Protecting the wellbeing of local residents and reducing the environmental impact are a priority for the organisers, and we are therefore working continuously with the relevant authorities and various stakeholders to implement mitigation and improvement measures.”
after newsletter promotion

But environmental groups have questioned the wisdom of building a grand prix circuit in a city where summer temperatures can exceed 40C (104F). According to Stop F1 Madrid , more than 700 trees have been felled or moved to make way for the track, while María Ángeles Nieto, a spokesperson for the Madrid Environmentalist platform, said a seasonal wetland that was home to amphibian species had been destroyed.

“Madrid is a city with significant temperature increases during the summer months – the entire city is a heat island,” said Nieto. “We’ve pointed out that this just exacerbates that heat island effect.”
Nieto said was “no justification whatsoever” for a track that would subject residents to “a living hell” for the duration of the grand prix and other possible events there.
“The people in charge of the city are prioritising the economic interests of Formula One over the wellbeing of the citizens in such an absolutely absurd and unnecessary way,” she said.
