articles.title: Thirty years of waiting, a memoir and a trial: conviction in Tupac Shakur killing brings closure
articles.summary: A Las Vegas jury on Monday found Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis guilty in the 1996 murder of the hip-hop icon

blocks.text: Thirty years after the killing of Tupac Shakur, conspiracy theories and rumors about the perpetrator’s identity, one man has now been held criminally responsible for the rap icon’s death.

A Las Vegas jury convicted Duane “Keffe D” Davis, a 63-year-old former South Side Compton Crips gang leader, of murder for his role in the drive-by shooting. During the two-week long trial, prosecutors argued Davis was the “on-the-ground, on-site commander of the effort to kill Tupac” and had sought revenge after the musician was involved in a fight with his nephew, Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson.
The conviction brings long-awaited resolution to the case, which has captured public attention and dominated headlines for decades.
“We’ve been waiting 30 years to grieve properly,” Zayd Akinyela, Shakur’s cousin, told reporters outside the courtroom when the trial was under way.

Shakur, the son of members of the Black Panther party was at the height of his career in 1996. The rapper had released the hit album All Eyez on Me, which sold millions of copies, and had become a global superstar.

In September 1996, he was in Las Vegas attending a Mike Tyson fight at the MGM Grand hotel. While heading to an afterparty that evening, he was attacked just off the Las Vegas strip alongside Marion “Suge” Knight, the founder of Death Row Records. As they waited at a red light, a Cadillac pulled up next to Shakur’s vehicle and shot him multiple times. Shakur died days later, at age 25.

Shakur’s death, at a young age and an ascendant point in his cultural power, turned him into an almost saint-like figure within hip-hop. A flood of posthumous songs, music videos and albums were released after the murder, eulogizing his legacy as one of the most prolific and talented artists of his generation.
Diss tracks, gang rivalries and a shooting

There were no arrests made in his killing and Las Vegas police faced criticism that the department had bungled the investigation and failed to pursue crucial leads. Questions and conspiracy theories persisted for decades, but few official answers.

The killing was for years viewed as connected to the east coast-west coast rivalry between different hip-hop groups and record labels. Shakur had a longstanding feud with Christopher Wallace, a Brooklyn rapper, better known as Biggie Smalls or The Notorious B.I.G., that had involved numerous diss tracks and threats between their camps. Wallace was murdered in Los Angeles less than six months after Shakur’s killing, adding to the lore around the feud.

Both Shakur and Biggie quickly became pop culture icons representing a golden era of 90s hip-hop. The unsolved nature of their deaths also created a cottage industry of books and documentaries claiming to uncover the real story of their deaths, many of which involved conspiracy theories and allegations of cover-ups.
Authorities say a clearer picture of what unfolded that September evening emerged in recent years thanks to Davis himself.

blocks.caption: Biggie and Tupac. Photograph: Film Four/Lafayette/Kobal/REX/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Davis, a former leader of the South Side Compton Crips gang, had long been known to investigators. He was the only living witness from the car that fired shots at Shakur. Detectives had also Davis to talk about the fatal shooting of the Notorious B.I.G. Though Davis was briefly a suspect, he was later ruled out by investigators.

During the weeks-long trial, jurors heard a 2008 interview where Davis told detectives that Anderson, who died in an unrelated 1998 shooting, fired the shots that killed Shakur. But prosecutors never gathered enough evidence to press charges.
The case took a turn when Davis published his memoir in 2019. In it, he described his involvement in the hit.

blocks.caption: Duane Davis and his attorney Michael Sanft in the courtroom in Las Vegas. Photograph: Bizuayehu Tesfaye/Pool Las Vegas Review-Journal/AP

blocks.text: According to Davis’s account, he was angry about the attack on his nephew and obtained a gun with the intent to “hunt down” Shakur and confront Knight. He and others, including his nephew Anderson, went searching for the group, and once they found them the incident unfolded quickly.

“No words were exchanged, the time for talking had passed, the shit was on! Tupac made an erratic move and began to reach down beneath his seat. It was the first and only time in my life that I could relate to the police command to, ‘Keep your hands where I can see them.’ Instead, Pac pulled out a strap, and that’s when the fireworks started. One of my guys from the back seat grabbed the Glock and started bustin’ back,” he wrote.
It was Davis decision to write the book that ultimately led to the trial, prosecutors said.
“Had he decided to never write the book, he would not, probably, have ever been prosecuted for the crime,” prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo said.
Davis’ defense unsuccessfully sought to have the memoir excluded from the trial, and said that it had been exaggerated to “falsely place [Davis] at the center of it all for personal gain”.

Over the course of the trial, defense attorney Michael Sanft argued that investigators had very little evidence to prove their case. He said that authorities, including the FBI, did not follow up with Davis because they did not believe what he said was credible.
“What they are telling you, they are representing as fact, when it’s really fiction,” said Sanft.
On Monday, a Las Vegas jury disagreed. The judge has set sentencing for 13 October.

articles.title: Remote Grand Canyon lodge hit by deadly flash flood boasts fabled history
articles.summary: Phantom Ranch, set up by Teddy Roosevelt, has welcomed exhausted hikers to its famed cabins for over a century

blocks.text: Phantom Ranch has been a solitary refuge visited by some of the most famous names of history. More typically, it’s been a beacon for the half-collapsed, exhausted and overheated hikers trudging down the Grand Canyon for more than a century.

The sole lodge at the very bottom of the Grand Canyon, the cabins long had a near mythical reputation. Located along the Bright Angel Creek, which tumbles into the mighty Colorado River at the base of the canyon, they served as a reminder of the long history of one of America’s most spectacular but savage environments.
It’s unclear yet how much damage the lodge has sustained after Saturday’s lethal flash flood.

On Saturday afternoon, more than 60 people had to be evacuated by air from the ranch and the bottom of the adjacent North Kaibab Trail, which winds 14 miles down from the lesser-trodden North Rim of the canyon. Two people were confirmed dead, nearly 80 people were rescued and one person remained unaccounted for.

Native Americans have made their home in various parts of the canyon for thousands of years and were driven out of much – though not all – of it before US president Theodore Roosevelt declared the canyon a national monument in 1908. It was Roosevelt who set up a camp on the site where the little visitor lodge now stands, while he was on a hunting trip in 1913. The area became a national park in 1919 and the ranch, named after one of the many side canyons within the Grand Canyon, opened in 1922.
Boaters floating and paddling down the Colorado River stay there, as do people riding mules. The future King Gustaf VI Adolf of Sweden was a prominent early guest, arriving via mule, in 1926.

In 1967, then senator Robert F Kennedy stayed at Phantom Ranch beneath the towering canyon walls after rafting down the Colorado with family and friends, bouncing and gliding 90 miles on the east-west flow of the river from Lake Powell.

Today, more than a vertical mile above, the hundreds of thousands of visitors who just peep over the South Rim, where lodges, tourist information spots, shops and restaurants buzz, cannot see the river, let alone the tiny ranch so far below.

But hikers who trek down the seven or eight zig-zag miles of the nearby dusty South Kaibab or Bright Angel trails to the bottom and cross footbridges over the Colorado to reach the ranch descend steadily from tourist hullabaloo into an ever more rugged and tranquil wilderness. Here, heat, thirst or flood are the biggest dangers, not the resident mountain lions, rattlesnakes or scorpions.

Having pounded the hard rock paths and rough steps all the way down, the few who get to stay at the ranch or snag a campsite along the creek are mostly thinking of the relief of not having to climb back up to the rim yet and the magic of cooling their throbbing feet in a stream before a simple canteen meal at communal tables and a rudimentary bed for a night or two.

But that sense of safety can be as elusively spectral as the name of the refuge. A fast and fierce deluge, such as occurred at the weekend, can quickly form a roaring flash flood when the rain swells creeks that drop steeply into the canyon as tributaries to the Colorado, which is what just happened in the Bright Angel Creek.

The National Park Service describes flash flooding as an inherent risk in the canyon but had additionally warned in February of “the elevated potential for flash flooding and debris flows in the Bright Angel Creek watershed” following the Dragon Bravo wildfire that decimated parts of the North Rim last year and forced the closure of the North Kaibab trail from July to March of this year.

articles.title: How intense rains in the Grand Canyon turned into a deadly disaster
articles.summary: Flash flooding in Arizona tourist destination was likely triggered by compounding climate factors, such as drought and warming in Pacific Ocean

blocks.text: A deadly flash flood in the Grand Canyon over the weekend was likely driven by a confluence of climate factors, including drought, wildfire scarring and warming temperatures in the Pacific Ocean that can supercharge storms.

At least two people have died, nearly 80 people were rescued and one remained unaccounted for after a surge of water and debris swept through the immensely popular tourist destination on Saturday, fueled by torrents of rain that hit the national park’s Bright Angel Creek area.

Flash floods are not uncommon in the region, especially during the monsoon season from June to September, when strong rains pummel the arid landscapes and can quickly fill narrow rock formations. Visiting the Grand Canyon – a crown jewel of the US national park system – can be particularly dangerous in the summer because of the risk of flash flooding, when clear days can give way quickly to thunderstorms and downpours.
The steep, rocky nature of the canyon itself funnels water rapidly, transforming downpours into a charging wall of water.

blocks.caption: This handout image released by the National Park Service shows a storm system moving across the North Rim of Grand Canyon national park on 29 August. Photograph: J Baird/National Park Service/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: But Saturday’s strong storm also hit part of the burn scar of the Dragon Bravo wildfire, a destructive and fast-moving blaze that swept across nearly 150,000 acres (60,700 hectares) and consumed the historic Grand Canyon Lodge in July 2025.
Runoff tends to flow more quickly in the aftermath of a fire, especially in hotter burns where slopes are left barren of vegetation.

While it’s still unclear how directly long-term damage to the landscape from that fire played a role in last weekend’s disaster, federal models indicated a rise in the risks of debris flows in Bright Angel Creek.

blocks.caption: Floods sweeping through Grand Canyon national park

blocks.text: Teams with the Department of Interior charged to assess post-fire threats to “life, property, and critical natural and cultural resources”, found runoff risks would be between two and eight times greater upstream of Phantom Creek. “Hikers on the trails within or downslope from the burned area will experience frequent stabilization issues, especially hazardous rockfall for at least the first year,” the team wrote in a report on conditions.

Park officials were reportedly concerned at the start of this summer that stronger storms could create dangerous conditions near the burned areas. Hikers that had to be evacuated by helicopter after the rushing waters swallowed bridges and other infrastructure told the Arizona Republic that the creek turned black as it filled with runoff.

blocks.caption: This handout image released by the Grand Canyon National Park Service shows remnants of stone bridge pylons along Bright Angel Creek following a flash flood. Photograph: J Thompson, handout/National Park Service/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Scientists have long warned that the climate crisis will create stronger extremes and destructive shifts between wet and dry conditions. As temperatures continue to climb, extreme events will not just increase – they are more likely to overlap, causing more calamity and testing the limits of the nation’s resilience and recovery.
So-called “compound extremes”, where a combination of contributing factors come together, are on the rise, according to researchers.

blocks.caption: The sudden, heavy rainstorm that fueled this catastrophic flood may have been been supercharged by the historic El Niño. Photograph: J Thompson, handout/National Park Service/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Along with the potential impact from a previous fire, a severe drought that continues to affect the Grand Canyon region – and the Colorado River basin that runs through it – could have contributed to the disaster. The deluge unleashed torrents of rain on hardened and sparsely vegetated steep terrain that is less able to absorb and contain abrupt increases in moisture.
The sudden and strong rainstorm that fueled this catastrophic flood may have been been supercharged by the historic El Niño that has sharply increased sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean.

blocks.caption: The Grand Canyon national park in northern Arizona on Sunday, a day after it was hit by heavy flooding. Photograph: Craig Sanderson via AP

blocks.text: The climate phenomenon has the ability to affect weather systems around the world. But in the south-west, the higher amount of water vapor in the atmosphere due to El Niño is wrung out in the form of rainfall, Park Williams, a hydroclimatologist at the University of California, Los Angeles, told the Associated Press.

El Niño is part of a natural cycle, but models show there is a strong likelihood this will become one of the strongest on record. It layers on top of spikes in temperature fueled by the climate crisis. Together, the possibility of severe and extreme weather is expected to dramatically increase.

blocks.caption: Bright Angel Canyon, the scene of flash floods, runs into the Colorado River in the Grand Canyon on Monday. Photograph: John Locher/AP

blocks.text: The link to human-caused climate change and the heavy Arizona rain is moderately strong, said Daniel Swain, a climate scientist at the California Institute for Water Resources.

Swain and colleagues recently published a study in the journal Weather and Climate Extremes finding that during the summer, short-term intense downpours in the US west – akin to the one that hit the Grand Canyon – have become 10% stronger since 2000.
The Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title: AFP: Chinese vessels spotted in West Philippine Sea increased to 56 in August 2026
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday said a total of 56 Chinese vessels have been monitored in some West Philippine Sea (WPS) features in August 2026.

blocks.text: Published September 1, 2026 9:52am
The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday said a total of 56 Chinese vessels have been monitored in some West Philippine Sea (WPS) features in August 2026.
This was higher compared to the 48 Chinese ships seen in the disputed area in July 2026.

In an update, AFP spokesperson for the WPS Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad said People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) and China Coast Guard (CCG) vessels were seen in WPS features from August 1 to 31:
• Ayungin Shoal – 18 Chinese vessels (17 CCGs, one PLAN)
• Bajo de Masinloc – 23 (14 CCGs, nine PLANs)
• Escoda Shoal – nine (five CCGs, four PLANs)
• Pag-asa Islands – six (five CCGs, one PLAN)

Tensions continue as Beijing claims almost all of the South China Sea, a conduit for more than $3 trillion of annual shipborne commerce, including parts claimed by the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei.
Parts of the South China Sea that fall within Philippine territory have been renamed by the government as West Philippine Sea to reinforce the country’s claim.

The West Philippine Sea refers to the maritime areas on the western side of the Philippine archipelago, including the Luzon Sea and the waters around, within, and adjacent to the Kalayaan Island Group and Bajo de Masinloc.
In 2016, the Permanent Court of Arbitration in the Hague ruled in favor of the Philippines over China's claims in the South China Sea, saying that it had "no legal basis."
China has refused to recognize the decision. — RSJ, GMA News

The public was urged to avoid prolonged outdoor exposure, particularly in areas where smoke or haze is noticeable.
Those who need to go outside were advised to wear face masks to help reduce the inhalation of smoke and fine particulate matter.
Children, older adults and people with sensitive respiratory systems were advised to take extra precautions and, if possible, remain indoors while the haze persists.

articles.title: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis found guilty of orchestrating 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur
articles.summary: A jury has found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, marking the first conviction in a case that has gripped hip-hop fans for decades.

image.caption: Duane Davis is the first person convicted in the 30-year-old murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur. (Steve Marcus/Pool/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
A jury has found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, marking the first conviction in a case that has gripped hip-hop fans for decades.
Jury delivered its verdict after 3 hours of deliberations

The 63-year-old Davis was convicted Monday of murder with the use of a deadly weapon and could be sentenced to life in prison. The jury deliberated for three hours after a weeks-long trial in Las Vegas.
After the verdict was read, Shakur's sister, Sekyiwa "Set" Shakur, cried and reached back to a person behind her. Also in the courtroom was Davis's son, who covered his face with one hand.

Chief Deputy District Attorney Binu Palal told jurors in closing arguments that Davis acquired a gun and "went hunting" for Shakur and Death Row Records co-founder Marion "Suge" Knight after they beat up Davis's nephew earlier that night.

Palal acknowledged that Davis's accounts of the killing evolved over the years but argued those differences reflected Davis's changing motivations and efforts to protect himself. One critical detail, he said, remained consistent: Davis repeatedly placed himself inside a white Cadillac from which the shots were fired.
"The core facts remain. The material facts remain," Palal said.

Davis's defence attorney, Michael Sanft, challenged jurors to identify evidence outside Davis's own statements that placed him in Las Vegas or inside the Cadillac on the night Shakur was shot. He pointed to the absence of surveillance footage, phone records and other evidence putting Davis there.
"They have nothing in this case that says that man was here in Las Vegas on Sept. 7, 1996," Sanft said, pointing toward Davis.
Justice in murder of Tupac 'foregone years ago': cousin
The decades-old case has drawn the attention of hip-hop fans and crime experts alike.

Shakur, who was considered one of the most influential rappers of all time, was in Las Vegas on Sept. 7, 1996, and stopped at a red light when a white Cadillac pulled up beside him, and shots were fired. He died six days later from his wounds. Knight was also wounded but survived.

For years, nobody had been charged in the rapper's death until Davis began making public statements, saying he was in the Cadillac and gave the gun to others in the backseat. Davis described the shooting as an act of retaliation after Knight and Shakur's entourage beat up Davis's nephew hours before the shooting.

items: Accused in Tupac Shakur murder trial says nephew fired the fatal shots in 1996 drive-by shooting
Former gang leader directed Tupac's drive-by killing, prosecutor tells jury
Man charged with arranging Tupac Shakur's murder heads to trial 30 years after hip-hop legend's death

blocks.text: Under Nevada law, someone who helps another person commit murder can be convicted of the crime. Davis is the only person still alive among the four men prosecutors say were in the Cadillac. The man prosecutors say originally gave the gun to Davis is also dead.
Palal told jurors that if they believe Davis's statements, they do not have to be independently corroborated with additional evidence.
"Who fired is not the question," Palal said. Prosecutors didn't argue that Davis pulled the trigger, but instead that he was criminally responsible because he provided the gun and ordered the attack.
Palal also argued the shooting was premeditated, pointing to testimony and Davis's accounts that the group searched for Shakur before spotting him on the road and making a U-turn.
"It's a plan, not an impulse," Palal said.
Davis's own words

Palal held up Davis's 2019 memoir, Compton Street Legend, and played an interview in which Davis encouraged people to buy it to get the "real truth." Although the book contains a disclaimer saying some facts were changed, Palal argued that names, hotels and other details changed while the central account did not.

Palal also rejected the defence's contention that Davis fabricated his accounts to make money. "It is an entirely different proposition to be profiting from a murder," Palal said. "And that is what Mr. Davis is doing."

Sanft also turned to his client's memoir during his closing argument. While reading an excerpt, he said the N-word aloud, prompting people watching in an overflow courtroom to recoil and shake their heads.
In multiple interviews, Davis said he handed the gun to the back seat, but in others as well as in his book, Davis wouldn't say who pulled the trigger.
In a rebuttal argument, prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo pointed to a scrapbook Davis kept containing articles about Shakur.
"This guy's scrapbooking his murder, for God's sake," DiGiacomo told jurors.

articles.summary: Dan Driscoll, the youngest-ever army secretary, was about 18 months into his post.

blocks.text: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll has submitted his resignation after about 18 months in the role.
His departure was confirmed by CBS, the BBC's US media partner, which reported it came after months of conflict between him and Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The youngest-ever army secretary has often been referred to as President Donald Trump's "drone guy".

Driscoll, 41, has been "highly effective" in advancing Trump's agenda "to Make America Strong Again" and provided "outstanding leadership" during military operations, the White House said in a statement given to CBS.
The BBC has contacted the White House, Pentagon and Army for comment.
Driscoll is the latest in a string of recent high-profile military leaders to depart, including Navy Secretary John Phelan who abruptly quit in April.
Other notable departures include Army Chief of Staff Randy George, Army Gen David Hodne and Maj Gen William Green.
Since entering the Pentagon, Hegseth has fired more than a dozen senior military officers, including the chief of naval operations and the Air Force's vice-chief of staff.

The details of the behind-the-scenes friction between Driscoll and Hegseth are unclear but CBS notes that the army secretary is good friends with George, who was reportedly asked by Hegseth to resign.
The post of army secretary is the top civilian leader of the US Army, directing active duty troops, along with the National Guard and reserve soldiers.
Driscoll previously served in the Army and was an officer in 2007 before leading a cavalry platoon and deploying to Iraq for several months in 2009.
As army secretary, Driscoll became known as Trump's "drone guy" due to his embrace of emerging battlefield technologies.
He took on a leading role last year in talks aimed at ending the Russia-Ukraine war, taking on foreign trips and meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
He's also a close ally and friend of Vice-President JD Vance, whom he met at Yale Law School.
During his tenure as head of the US Army, he was a key figure in Trump's deployment of the National Guard to US cities.
He also took over the role of acting director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.

articles.title: Putin, Xi hold talks in Kyrgyzstan as regional summit begins
articles.summary: BISHKEK — Russia’s Vladimir Putin and China’s Xi Jinping began talks Monday in Kyrgyzstan, where a dozen other heads of state also gathered for a two-day summit of the Shanghai…

blocks.text: BISHKEK — Russia’s Vladimir Putin and China’s Xi Jinping began talks Monday in Kyrgyzstan, where a dozen other heads of state also gathered for a two-day summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), which seeks to be a counterbalance to the West.

Iran’s leader Masoud Pezeshkian, Turkey’s Recep Tayyip Erdogan, India’s Narendra Modi and Pakistan’s Shehbaz Sharif were also among those in Bishkek to attend the summit of the regional SCO bloc, which celebrates its 25-year anniversary.
The summit takes place four-and-a-half years into Moscow’s Ukraine invasion and six months into the war between Washington and Tehran.
Putin and Xi have previously used SCO summits to promote their vision of a multipolar world and present a united front against the West.
Xi told Putin he was “happy” to see him, saying Russia-Chinese ties have become “more solid” and that their “prospects will be even brighter”.
“The amount of uncertainty and unpredictability in the international order has obviously increased,” the Chinese leader said.
Putin told Xi: “Cooperation is successfully developing on all fronts.” The pair last met in May.
Russia’s economy has become increasingly dependent on China during its invasion of Ukraine. Western countries have called on Beijing to pressure Moscow to end its offensive.
The Kremlin’s spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian media the pair only discussed the Ukraine war “in passing”.
Putin also met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with both leaders arriving in the same car for the talks.
The Russian leader said Moscow was “following the path” towards resolution of the conflict in Ukraine, without elaborating.
The peace talks, brokered by the United States, remain stalled.
Putin is also expected to hold separate talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.
Russia and Iran — among the most sanctioned states in the world — have massively deepened their military and economic ties since Moscow invaded Ukraine.
War not ‘in our interest’
US President Donald Trump has warned Moscow and Beijing against arming Iran.

Putin’s meeting with Pezeshkian will come days after the CIA’s director John Ratcliffe made a rare trip to Moscow, with US media speculating he could have discussed Ukraine and Iran with his Russian counterparts.
Speaking in Bishkek after the first exchange of fire between the United States and Iran in a month, Iran’s Pezeshkian said continuing the war was not in Tehran’s interests.
“We continue to strive for a path of agreement and understanding, and we believe that continuing the war is neither in our interest, nor in the interest of the region,” he told India’s Modi.
Putin, Xi, Pezeshkian, Modi and Sharif are due to take part in a plenary session chaired by Kyrgyz leader Sadyr Japarov.
The SCO has historically focused on economic issues but has gained momentum in recent years under Moscow’s and Beijing’s leadership.
On top of its 10 members, it now has 15 “dialogue partners”, including Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
It also has two observer countries: Afghanistan and Mongolia.
Real and trade wars

The Bishkek summit takes place at a time when some SCO members are in the midst of real wars — the Ukraine and Iran conflicts — or trade wars, with the imposition of US tariffs on Chinese and Indian goods.
This month, the US slapped secondary sanctions on Iran’s trading partners in the sectors of gold, technology, digital assets, aviation and maritime transport, aiming to cripple Tehran’s economy.
Washington has also threatened Iran’s allies with sanctions.
China, a major importer of Iranian oil, responded by saying it would “firmly defend” its interests.
Iran, living under sanctions since its 1979 revolution ended with Islamic authorities taking charge, has regularly said it will not cave to economic pressure.
But Pezeshkian has acknowledged his country faces “economic difficulties”.
Iran only joined the bloc in 2023.

Mohammad Hassan Najmi, an international relations expert, told AFP that Tehran “believes its membership and active participation in these alliances can enable it to circumvent US and European sanctions”.
But concrete benefits of the group are uncertain, he said, as “in times of crisis, these alliances have rarely allowed Iran to resolve its difficulties”.
While the bloc claims to represent some 40 percent of the world’s population and 25 percent of global GDP, it remains diverse, with disagreements among members. /dl

articles.title: 'Pilandok' keeps strength as habagat brings heavy rain over Luzon, Visayas
articles.summary: Tropical Depression Pilandok maintained its strength Tuesday as the southwest monsoon or habagat is expected to bring heavy rainfall over parts of Luzon and the western section of the Visayas, PAGASA…

blocks.text: September 1, 2026 | 8:52am
Satellite rendering shows Typhoon Depression Pilandok taken on Sept. 1, 2026.
PAGASA via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Pilandok maintained its strength Tuesday as the southwest monsoon or habagat is expected to bring heavy rainfall over parts of Luzon and the western section of the Visayas, PAGASA said.
In its 5 a.m. bulletin on Tuesday, September 1, the state weather bureau said Pilandok was located 1,050 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon.
Pilandok was carrying maximum sustained winds of 55 kilometers per hour near the center, with gustiness of up to 70 kph.
It was moving west-northwestward at 10 kph.
Pilandok is not directly affecting the country's land areas, while the southwest monsoon continues to bring rains over Luzon and the western section of the Visayas.
No tropical cyclone wind signal is currently raised over any part of the country.
Strong winds

PAGASA said the southwest monsoon will bring strong to gale-force gusts over most of Luzon and Visayas, as well as Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Dinagat Islands, Davao Occidental and Davao Oriental until Thursday, September 3.
PAGASA said strong to gale-force gusts are particularly possible in coastal and upland areas exposed to the winds.
Heavy rainfall
The state weather bureau said the southwest monsoon or habagat will continue to bring heavy rainfall over parts of Luzon through Thursday, September 3.
Tuesday, September 1

items: 50-100 mm: Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Batanes, Abra, Benguet, Zambales and Bataan

blocks.text: Wednesday, September 2

items: 50-100 mm: Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Batanes, Abra, Benguet, Zambales, Bataan and Occidental Mindoro

blocks.text: Thursday, September 3

items: 100-200 mm: Benguet, Zambales, Bataan and Occidental Mindoro
50-100 mm: Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, Abra, La Union, Pangasinan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Cavite and Batangas

blocks.text: PAGASA said forecast rainfall may be higher in mountainous and elevated areas. The impacts in some areas may also be worsened by significant antecedent rainfall.
Sea conditions
A gale warning is in effect over the northern and western seaboards of Northern Luzon.
Very rough seas with waves reaching up to 5 meters are expected over the western seaboard of the Babuyan Islands and the seaboards of Ilocos Norte.
Waves of up to 4.5 meters are also forecast over the western seaboards of Batanes and Pangasinan, as well as the seaboards of Ilocos Sur and northern La Union.
PAGASA warned that sea travel is risky for all types and tonnage of vessels under these conditions.
Small seacraft operators, including those using motorbancas, are also advised not to venture out to sea in affected waters.
Track, intensity
PAGASA said Pilandok is forecast to slowly turn east-northeastward then northward over the next 24 hours.
It will then move generally north-northwestward for the remainder of the forecast period.
Pilandok is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility by Wednesday evening, September 2, or Thursday morning, September 3.
The tropical depression is less likely to make landfall over the Philippines and is expected to remain far from the country's landmass.
Pilandok is forecast to intensify into a tropical storm within the next 12 hours and may remain a tropical storm as it moves toward southern Japan.
PAGASA said that heavy rainfall and severe winds may still be experienced in areas outside Pilandok's forecast track and confidence cone.

articles.summary: Chuck Thompson, the head of public affairs at CBC, says the public broadcaster is reviewing the Republican National Committee's "disappointing" decision to revoke CBC/Radio-Canada press accreditation…

image.caption: Chuck Thompson, the head of public affairs at CBC, confirmed the Republican National Committee revoked CBC/Radio-Canada press accreditation for the GOP's midterm convention next month. (Nathan Denette/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: World·New

Chuck Thompson, the head of public affairs at CBC, says the public broadcaster is reviewing the Republican National Committee's "disappointing" decision to revoke CBC/Radio-Canada press accreditation for next month's event in Dallas, Texas.
CBC official says public broadcaster hopes 'disappointing' decision will be resconsidered
The Republican Party has revoked CBC/Radio-Canada's media accreditation for the party's upcoming midterm convention.

Chuck Thompson, the head of public affairs at CBC, confirmed on Monday that the Republican National Committee (RNC) would no longer provide accreditation for CBC/Radio-Canada journalists to cover the convention in Dallas, Texas, on Sept. 9 and 10.
Thompson said in a written statement that CBC was reviewing the RNC's decision.
"It is a disappointing development; we hope it will be reconsidered."

items: America 'not at war' with Canada, insists U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent
IN PHOTOS | In the crosshairs of a trade war

blocks.text: Convention organizers did not immediately respond to CBC News' emailed requests for comment on Monday evening.
The White House referred CBC's questions to the RNC. CBC News was not able to reach the committee by phone Monday evening.
The revocation comes as tensions between Canada and the United States have soared amid a new wave of tit-for-tat sanctions and heated rhetoric from politicians on both sides of the border.

Republican lawmakers and Trump administration officials also recently criticized CBC after a leaked internal memo from the public broadcaster regarding the use of the words "terrorism" and "terrorist" in relation to the 9/11 attacks drew international attention.
How is the Canada-U.S. trade war affecting Carney's approval ratings?

The memo referred to a longstanding policy that had instructed CBC journalists to "generally avoid labelling any specific bombing or other assault as a 'terrorist act' unless this term is attributed."
It drew widespread condemnation ahead of the 25-year anniversary of 9/11 next month.

items: How and why CBC News will adjust its 9/11 language guidance

blocks.text: "What possible motive could there be for sanitizing the worst terrorist attack on American soil? Care to explain, @Canada?" a group of Republican members of the U.S. House of Representatives wrote on social media on Thursday.

On Friday, Basem Boshra, CBC's senior director of journalistic standards and public trust, said that after reviewing the public broadcaster's current language guidance, "we have decided to adjust it to clarify that direct attribution is not required for describing the historic events of 9/11 as terrorism."
"We are doing so to remove what has unfortunately (and unintentionally) become an impediment to clarity and public understanding," Boshra said.

articles.title: Taal Volcano logs 6 quakes, lone tremor in past 24 hours
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — Taal Volcano in Batangas recorded six volcanic earthquakes and a single prolonged tremor in the past 24 hours, indicating a decline in seismic activity, the Philippine Institute of…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — Taal Volcano in Batangas recorded six volcanic earthquakes and a single prolonged tremor in the past 24 hours, indicating a decline in seismic activity, the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) reported Tuesday, Sept. 1.

In its latest bulletin, Phivolcs said the volcanic tremor lasted 420 minutes. Despite its duration, the agency said there was no immediate cause for alarm, noting that volcanic tremors are a normal occurrence at Taal.

The latest seismic activity marked a notable decline from the previous nine days, from Aug. 20 to 28, when Taal recorded double-digit numbers of volcanic earthquakes daily, for a total of 229 earthquakes and 12 tremor episodes.
On Aug. 29, Taal recorded eight volcanic earthquakes, another eight the following day, and 13 on Aug. 31.
Phivolcs defines volcanic earthquakes as those “generated by magmatic processes or magma-related processes beneath or near an active volcano.”

“Unlike tectonic earthquakes that are produced by faulting, volcanic earthquakes are directly produced by many processes and are, therefore, much more varied in characteristics,” the agency explained.
Volcanic tremors, meanwhile, are continuous seismic signals with regular or irregular oscillations and low frequencies, typically ranging from 0.5 to 5 hertz, that can last for more than a minute.
Despite the decline in seismic activity, Taal continued to emit sulfur dioxide. Phivolcs recorded 381 metric tons of SO₂, although the emission level remained classified as “weak.”
The agency also reported no observed upwelling of hot volcanic fluids in the Main Crater Lake and no volcanic smog, or “vog,” during the monitoring period.
On Saturday (August 29), Phivolcs warned of possible lahar flows and volcanic debris around Taal and Mount Pinatubo amid prolonged heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon, or “habagat.”
Heavy rainfall may trigger muddy streamflows and volcanic debris flows around Taal Volcano, particularly along the western and northern slopes of Taal Lake.
These hazards could affect parts of Batangas, particularly the municipalities of Agoncillo, Laurel, and Talisay.
Phivolcs advised communities in potentially affected areas to closely monitor weather conditions and take necessary precautionary measures.
Taal Volcano remains under Alert Level 1, indicating a low level of volcanic unrest. /dp

articles.title: Heavy rain at Grand Canyon after flood kills 2, dozen missing
articles.summary: GRAND CANYON VILLAGE, United States — Heavy rainstorms swept through the Grand Canyon on Monday, threatening efforts to find more than a dozen people missing after flash floods over the…

blocks.text: GRAND CANYON VILLAGE, United States — Heavy rainstorms swept through the Grand Canyon on Monday, threatening efforts to find more than a dozen people missing after flash floods over the weekend, the National Park Service (NPS) said, with two bodies already recovered.
The floods hit the iconic US park’s Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch area on Saturday afternoon, forcing dozens of people to evacuate and damaging the sole water pipeline serving the area.
The body of a 46-year-old man was recovered on Sunday evening, the park service said.
The NPS said on Monday that a second body had been recovered, while warning that “forecasted weather may affect the timing and pace” of further search operations.
On Monday afternoon, low cloud shrouded the deep ravine, and the National Weather Service warned of more flooding with rain and thunderstorms in the forecast.

“Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Raging killer currents will be possible in side canyons and narrow slot canyons. Low-water crossings may be flooded,” it said in a bulletin.

On Monday, a handful of visitors, many of them foreign tourists, huddled under umbrellas or wore rain ponchos as they stood on the South Rim snapping selfies and straining to make out the Colorado River far below.

Video footage taken over the weekend by hikers showed a torrent of muddy water rushing by trails and under footbridges as well as logs and other debris floating down swollen rivers, accompanied by a rumbling roar.
The park service said it was working with Arizona authorities to evacuate people and account for missing individuals.
As of Sunday morning, 62 people had been evacuated, with others scheduled for later, it said.
It said around 15 people were thought to be missing.
A press conference was expected later Monday, when first responders would be joined by local and park officials to give reporters an update on the search for those left unaccounted for.
Water pipeline damaged
The flooding damaged or destroyed 40 percent of the Transcanyon Waterline, a key water pipeline into Grand Canyon National Park, the park service said Monday.
It announced water restrictions in its most visited area and a ban on wood and charcoal fires.

The twelve-and-a-half-mile (20 kilometers) pipeline runs from the Roaring Springs source on the North Rim to the South Rim, providing drinking water and fire suppression, according to the park’s website.
The flooding also resulted in “significant impacts to infrastructure,” destroying footbridges and blocking hikers from crossing Bright Angel Creek, the park service said.

Trails down into the Canyon from the South Rim remained open on Monday, but staff were warning visitors of the potential dangers, with sudden squalls possible at any time during the Southwest monsoon season.
The hike down into the wild belly of the Canyon from one popular starting point takes many visitors around four hours, one staff member said, while the return journey would likely add another six.

Flash floods are common in Northern Arizona because the arid, sparsely vegetated environments there have little capacity to absorb rain, the park’s website said, urging visitors to be especially cautious from July to mid-September.

The Grand Canyon — considered one of the greatest wonders of the natural world — is the result of the Colorado River eating away at layers of red sandstone and other rock for millions of years, leaving a chasm up to 18 miles wide and more than a mile deep.
Last year almost five million people visited the site. /dl

articles.title: Tupac Shakur murder trial: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis guilty
articles.summary: The jury reached a verdict in less than three hours in a case that had been unsolved for nearly 30 years.

image.caption: Davis is 63 years oldImage: Steve Marcus/REUTERS

blocks.text: A Las Vegas jury on Monday found former gang leader, Duane "Keffe D" Davis, guilty of orchestrating the killing of hip hop artist Tupac Shakur, following nine days of testimony.
It took jurors less than three hours to reach a guilty verdict in a case that has up until now been unsolved for almost three decades.
Sixty three-year-old Davis was convicted of murder with the use of a deadly weapon and could be sentenced to life in prison.
Shakur was wounded in a drive-by shooting on September 7, 1996, and died in a hospital six days later at the age of 25.
He was an award-winning rap artist, activist and actor who sold over 75 million records worldwide, many posthumously.
Davis, a one-time leader of the South Side Compton Crips gang, is the only person ever to have been charged in Shakur’s murder.
He is the only person still alive among the four men prosecutors say were in the Cadillac from which shots were fired. The man who prosecutors say originally gave the gun to Davis is also dead.
In closing arguments, Chief Deputy District Attorney Binu Palal told jurors that Davis acquired a gun and “went hunting” for Shakur and Knight after they beat up Davis’ nephew earlier that night.
Palal said that Davis’ accounts of the killing evolved over the years but maintained that those differences showed Davis’ changing motivations and efforts to protect himself.
Palal argued that a key detail remained consistent throughout and that was that Davis repeatedly placed himself inside the white Cadillac from which the shots were fired.
More to follow…

articles.title: Two dead and at least 15 missing after flash flood in Grand Canyon
articles.summary:
National Park Service confirms second death from weekend flash flood as area braces for more storms

A second death was…

blocks.text: A second death was confirmed by National Park Service officials on Monday after a flash flood sent a surge of water and debris through an area of the Grand Canyon over the weekend.

Dozens of visitors had to be evacuated by helicopter during the deluge, which consumed trails and infrastructure. Fifteen people are still missing or unaccounted for, as more heavy rain and thunderstorms in the forecasts threaten additional debris flows, flash floods or rock falls, the NPS said in a statement.
“With deep monsoonal moisture in place and already saturated soils in some locations, an elevated risk of flash flooding will be in place through Monday,” the National Weather Service (NWS) said.

Park officials are calling on the public to provide any information on those who may have been hiking or backpacking in the inner canyon near Bright Angel Creek, or campers with a reservation in the area.

Flash floods are not uncommon in the region, especially during the monsoon season from June to September when strong rains pummel the arid landscapes and can quickly fill narrow rock formations. Visiting the Grand Canyon – a crown jewel of the US national park system – can be particularly dangerous in the summer because of the risk of flash flooding that accompanies the monsoon, when clear days can give way quickly to thunderstorms and downpours.

The deluge that unleashed torrents of rain on hardened and sparsely vegetated steep terrain came as the Grand Canyon region – and the Colorado River basin that runs through it – continue to be mired in a severe drought that has fueled a widespread water crisis.

Scientists have long warned that the climate crisis will create stronger extremes and destructive shifts between wet and dry conditions. The sudden and strong rainstorm that fueled this catastrophic flood may have been been supercharged by the historic El Niño that has sharply increased sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean, which has the ability to affect weather systems around the world.

The NWS has issued flood watches across a large part of the south-west, including in northern Arizona. Officials cautioned against visiting creeks, slot canyons, burn scars and low water crossings in the area, where flash floods can quickly develop.

Videos taken by hikers before they were airlifted to safety showed churning brown waters carrying large metal objects and other debris. Some crossed the bridges just shortly before they were consumed by the waterway.

blocks.caption: Bright Angel Canyon, the scene of flash floods, runs into the Colorado River in the Grand Canyon. Photograph: John Locher/AP

blocks.text: “It must have been, like, 10 minutes afterwards – we crossed the bridges to get to the evacuation zone,” hiker Gabriel Burgeman told a local news station. “We were just barely in time to cross them before they got wiped out.”

The body of a 46-year-old man was recovered on Sunday evening near Crystal Rapids along the Colorado River, the NPS said, without providing additional details. At least one other body has been recovered, according to a statement posted on Facebook by the Grand Canyon national park without details.

Early assessments also showed roughly 40% of a key pipeline that provides drinking water for tourists and residents had been damaged or destroyed. The 12.5-mile (20km) long Transcanyon Waterline has endured dozens of breaks in recent years. A more than $200m repair and replacement project was well under way when the floods hit.

The pipeline moves water from one side of the canyon, down to its base, across a bridge and back up the other side of the rough landscape. Any effort to fix a break from rock falls or flash floods is time-consuming, precarious and costly, so addressing the latest damage will be complicated.

Emergency water restrictions began on Monday, closing down all overnight stay lodges and hotels within Grand Canyon national park, and spigots at campgrounds on the South Rim were turned off. Year-round residents were asked to conserve water. The park had water conservation measures in place even before the latest bout of flooding and damage.

blocks.caption: People wait near a bridge as a helicopter flies nearby. Photograph: Wieke De Boer/Reuters

blocks.text: The flooding on Saturday in Bright Angel Creek, which flows into the river, led to more than 60 people being airlifted from the canyon’s depths.
Parth Desai was hiking through a narrow passage in Bright Angel Canyon with fellow physicians and a park ranger when heavy rain started falling on Saturday.
“We saw the creek flood, waterfalls coming up out of nowhere, boulders, mud, landslides happening everywhere,” he said.

Torrents of water wiped out footbridges over the creek and altered the landscape, widening the creek bed and extending an existing river rapid or creating a new one. The flood was a blow to an enduring effort to modernize the pipeline that serves 6 million visitors a year and roughly 1,600 residents of Grand Canyon Village.

“Heaven help us if the whole thing down there at the bottom has to be reconstructed,” said Jack Schmidt, director of the Center for Colorado River Studies at Utah State University. “Where are they going to get the money?”

blocks.caption: The campsite at Bright Angel Creek corridor is seen from Grand Canyon Village. Photograph: Ian Maule/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Halting overnight stays at the park because of a lack of water is rare, although the pipeline frequently has failed over the years. While the Grand Canyon has large storage tanks for potable water on the South Rim, they will not be refilled while the pipeline is out of service.

A $208m rehabilitation of the pipeline and upgrades to the associated water delivery system started in 2023, with the park service calling it a crucial investment to ensure the park can meet the needs of residents and visitors. The project was expected to be completed next year.
In unrelated flooding, officials in San Antonio, Texas, on Sunday reported a pair of deaths related to a severe storm there two days earlier.

blocks.caption: Flood debris lines Bright Angel Creek. Photograph: John Locher/AP

blocks.text: Police said a 46-year-old woman died after being caught in rushing water in San Pedro Creek north of downtown, Texas Public Radio reported. A person with that woman made it out the situation safely, police said.
Separately, police said a man in his 50s was found at Woodlawn Park on Sunday morning.
The woman’s death is being investigated as a drowning while the man’s death is considered a possible drowning, police said.
The Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title: Search begins for Canadian team to restore uninhabitable 24 Sussex Drive
articles.summary: The search is officially on for a Canadian team to renovate Canada's most famous fixer-upper — 24 Sussex Drive — so it's no longer uninhabitable and future prime ministers can once again live there.

image.caption: A new procurement document calls for Canadian companies to put their names forward to take part in a competition to redesign and rebuild the prime minister's official residence at 24 Sussex Drive that is currently uninhabitable. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics·New
The search is officially on for a Canadian team to renovate Canada's most famous fixer-upper — 24 Sussex Drive — so it's no longer uninhabitable and future prime ministers can once again live there.
Canadian materials, Indigenous participation required to restore prime minister's official residence
The federal government recently posted its first procurement notice for the long-awaited rehabilitation project, which opens the door for domestic companies to pitch themselves as contenders.

The document reveals that Ottawa will choose seven finalists during this first stage to move on to the national design competition, with the winning team awarded a design and construction contract by the fall of 2027.

Ottawa is looking for a "world-class design vision" that focuses on using Canadian products to transform the gutted official residence into a secure and modern home and place to work for future prime ministers, the document said.
"Given its national and historical significance, the rehabilitated residence must be completed by Canadians for Canadians," the Request for Qualification (RFQ) posted on Aug. 21 said.
"In that spirit, the use of Canadian materials and innovations must be considered and incorporated throughout the project."
Carney wants 24 Sussex fixed up for future prime ministers

The official residence has sat vacant for more than a decade. Successive prime ministers have been unwilling to take the political risk to spend millions of taxpayer dollars on renovations, allowing the building to deteriorate. In recent years, the heritage home had to be stripped down to the studs to remove asbestos, mould and dead rodents.

Prime Minister Mark Carney called the state of the official residence an "embarrassment" in an exclusive interview with CBC News earlier this year. He unveiled his long-awaited plans in June to restore the heritage home built for his successors through a national design competition and a fundraising campaign to help foot the bill.
Canadians have donated more than $735,000 as of late July — almost 1.5 per cent of the $50 million fundraising goal.
Details of competition
The government's new RFQ is the first stage of the procurement process. The nearly 100-page document provides the most detail in writing about the competition to date.

Teams pitching a design plan must show they can create a private living quarter for the prime minister and their family while balancing space for work, meetings, hosting receptions or ceremonial events, the request said.
The winning team, according to the document, will also be responsible for making the property universally accessible, handling landscaping elements and restoring heritage elements.
The main building has already been gutted to remove "hazardous materials," the document said, but there might be archaeological assessments, geotechnical studies and security-related modifications.

The Royal Architectural Institute of Canada will use a jury of experts to score the design concepts, and a separate technical evaluation board at Procurement Canada will judge the construction plans, budgets and schedule, the request said.
The RFQ is a way for the government to screen potential teams and weed out any that aren't qualified.
The teams who want to compete must show they have experience working on a series of projects including a complex building that cost at least $50 million to build.
Carney launches design competition to 'rehabilitate' 24 Sussex Drive
The procurement rules also make it mandatory that competing firms' plans include Indigenous people and businesses to carry out at least five per cent of the contract's total value.
It's still unclear how much it will cost to renovate the famous property.
The construction budget is expected to be included in the next phase of the procurement process, known as the Request for Proposal, expected to launch in the winter of 2027, the request said.

items: Carney confronts our national home reno nightmare at 24 Sussex

blocks.text: The top contenders will ultimately compete to showcase designs that "inspire pride" and "architectural excellence," according to the rules.
"The desired outcome is a renewed 24 Sussex [that] serves contemporary needs and remains a symbol of Canada for generations to come," the request said.
The Rideau Hall Foundation, which is leading the fundraising effort for the project, said it's planning on a more formal launch of its campaign in the coming weeks.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Ashley Burke is a senior reporter with the CBC's Parliamentary Bureau in Ottawa. She was recognized with the Charles Lynch Award and was a finalist for the Michener Award for her exclusive reporting on the toxic workplace at Rideau Hall. She has also uncovered allegations of sexual misconduct in the Canadian military. You can reach her confidentially by email: ashley.burke@cbc.ca

articles.title: Health-care groups call on Ottawa to stop Alberta’s dual medical practice model
articles.summary: Canadian and provincial health-care groups are calling on the federal government to stop Alberta from allowing physicians to practise in both the public and private system.

image.caption: Jason MacLean, chair of the Canadian Health Coalition, called on federal Health Minister Marjorie Michel to stop Alberta from allowing physicians to practise in both the public and private systems. (CBC)

blocks.text: Edmonton·New
Canadian and provincial health-care groups are calling on the federal government to stop Alberta from allowing physicians to practise in both the public and private system.
Alberta gets nearly 400 expressions of interest from physicians
· CBC News
· Posted: Aug 31, 2026 7:09 PM EDT | Last Updated: 21 minutes ago
The change is enabled by the Health Statutes Amendment Act, 2025 (No. 2), commonly called Bill 11, which takes effect on Tuesday.

“[Bill 11 is] the biggest threat against health care since the Canada Health Act was passed in 1984,” Jason MacLean, chair of the Canadian Health Coalition, said at a news conference in Ottawa Monday.

The group is planning rallies in 30 locations across Canada on its so-called Day of Action on Tuesday. The rallies will be followed by 50 town halls this fall as part of its national campaign against the bill.

MacLean said he believes changes enabled by the bill will make access to health care unequal. He said when physicians are able to practise in both systems, resources tend to migrate towards the private pay system, creating long waitlists in the public system.
MacLean called on federal Health Minister Marjorie Michel to take action before other provinces follow suit.
“We don't understand why the federal government is mute on this. This is an issue of national consequence,” he said.
“We all know what happens in Alberta won't just stay in Alberta.”

items: Federal health minister voices concern as Alberta implements dual-practice health-care model

blocks.text: Bill 11 was introduced and passed in Alberta’s legislature in the fall 2025 sitting, allowing doctors to apply to be able to practise in both the public and private spheres.

In order to be eligible to apply for dual practice in Alberta, physicians need to work a prescribed number of hours in the public system. Family physicians are not allowed to practise in both systems at this time.

According to the province, surgeries under the dual-practice model likely won’t start until later in the fall because physicians must get approved by the government first. They can start applying in mid-September.

Maddison McKee, press secretary for Alberta’s Hospital and Surgical Health Services Minister Adriana LaGrange, told CBC News that the province is reviewing nearly 400 expressions of interest received from physicians about the new dual-practice option over the summer.
“This will help us gauge interest, understand what specialists are contemplating dual practice and prepare for the formal application process,” she wrote.
“Applications will be reviewed to ensure eligibility criteria and government requirements are met, including public surgery hour requirements, monitoring and new reporting requirements.”
Province insists dual practice is allowed

McKee dismissed concerns raised by the Canadian Health Coalition about what it sees as Alberta moving to a U.S.-style health-care system as “fearmongering.” She said dual practice doesn’t violate the Canada Health Act.

“Our priority is a strong public system and ensuring Albertans never have to pay out of pocket for medically necessary care — which is a commitment we have made under our Public Health Care Guarantee,” she wrote.
“Expanding access through dual practice does not take away from that. It adds to it. This is not an either/or debate. It is about giving Albertans more choice.”

Earlier this month, Michel told the Toronto Star she was concerned about Bill 11. On Monday, her spokesperson, Alexandre Bergeron, said the federal government was collaborating with Alberta on any changes “that respects their jurisdiction to explore innovative ways to improve access and care while strengthening the public, universal health-care system.”
“Minister Michel is advancing targeted discussions with her counterpart focused on ensuring access to medically necessary care and the core principles of the public system are protected,” he wrote.
“A collaborative approach between our governments has always produced strong results for all Albertans and we will continue to work in that direction.”

items: Eligible doctors in Alberta can work in both public, private systems starting this fall

blocks.text: The federal government sent a letter to the province on July 24 confirming it had reviewed the regulations and the June 18 ministerial order, and that both levels of government should continue their collaboration.

Bergeron said Ottawa is in close contact with the province to ensure possible adverse impacts on the public system are mitigated and that changes are in compliance with the principles of the Canada Health Act.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Michelle Bellefontaine covers the Alberta legislature for CBC News in Edmonton. She has also worked as a reporter in the Maritimes and in northern Canada.

articles.title: Pilandok won’t directly affect PH but habagat to prevail
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Pilandok will not directly affect the country, while the southwest monsoon, or habagat, will continue to prevail over Luzon and the western part of Visayas…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Pilandok will not directly affect the country, while the southwest monsoon, or habagat, will continue to prevail over Luzon and the western part of Visayas on Tuesday, according to the state weather bureau.

In the 5 a.m. weather forecast of the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration, weather specialist Veronica Torres said that Pilandok was last estimated 1,050 kilometers east of Extreme Northern Luzon. It maintained its strength as it was carrying a maximum wind speed of 55 kilometers per hour (kph) and gustiness of 70 kph.
“Walang direktang epekto sa ating bansa at napakababa naman ng tyansang maglandfall sa anumang parte ng bansa,” Torres said.
(This does not have a direct effect over the country and it has a low chance of making landfall in any part of the country.)

Torres also said that Pilandok will move east-northeastward and then northeastward in the next 24 hours. It may also traverse northwestward and exit the Philippine area of responsibility by Wednesday evening or Thursday morning.
It is forecast to intensify into a tropical storm in the next 12 hours.

Meanwhile, Torres noted that the habagat will bring heavy rains in the western portion of Luzon. She added that Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Batanes, Abra, Benguet, Zambales, and Bataan will experience 50 to 100 millimeters of rainfall on Tuesday due to habagat.
Weather disturbances outside the country
Torres also shared that there are currently three weather disturbances being monitored outside the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR.

Tropical Storm Saudel, formerly locally named Obet, was last located 965 kilometers west of Extreme Northern Luzon as of 3 a.m. Torres said that because of its east-southeast movement, its chance of re-entering the PAR is not ruled out.
A tropical depression seen 645 kilometers west-northwest of Itbayat, Batanes is not forecast to enter the PAR.

Lastly, a low pressure area 3,000 kilometers east of Southern Luzon has a medium chance of developing into a tropical depression in the next 24 hours. Its possibility of entering the PAR is not ruled out. /jpv

articles.title: Cardinal David: Resilience not acceptance of corruption, incompetence
articles.summary: "There comes a point when resilience becomes dangerous because it teaches us merely to endure."

blocks.text: September 1, 2026 | 7:00am
Motorists commute through a flooded street due to rains brought by the southwest monsoon in Pampanga on August 31, 2026.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa

MANILA, Philippines — Filipino resilience should not mean passive acceptance of corruption, incompetence and neglect, Kalookan Bishop Pablo Virgilio Cardinal David said Monday as floods continued to disrupt communities across Luzon.
In a social media post on Monday, August 31, David urged Filipinos to go beyond enduring disasters and instead demand accountability for preventable suffering.
"There comes a point when resilience becomes dangerous because it teaches us merely to endure," David said.

"After every disaster, we are told to be resilient. This time, let us also be defiant... Let us refuse to normalize preventable suffering. Let us demand answers. Let us demand accountability. And where the law allows it, let us act together as citizens to hold accountable those who fail in their duty to protect the public," he added.
David said such defiance should take the form of organized, legal civic action rather than simply anger on social media.

He encouraged motorists to file complaints before regulatory agencies, communities to demand disclosure of flood-control projects and budgets, and citizens to seek legal remedies when negligence results in injury or loss.

"Defiance asks questions: Who designed this? Who built it? Who inspected it? Who maintained it? How much did taxpayers pay for it? Why does the same place flood every year? Where did the flood-control money go?" David said.
"And when negligence is established, who will be held accountable?"
David cited recurring flooding along the North Luzon Expressway in San Simon, Pampanga, where he said he was recently trapped in traffic for almost five hours.
Flooding continued to disrupt traffic in the San Simon area Monday, with some NLEX lanes impassable to smaller vehicles.

Parts of Bulacan also remained flooded after days of southwest monsoon, or habagat, rains. Floodwaters remained inside historic Barasoain Church in Malolos earlier Monday before receding later in the afternoon.
"Filipino resilience is a beautiful virtue. But resilience should never mean passive acceptance of incompetence, corruption or neglect," David said.

articles.title: Q&A: Canadian man held in ICE detention centres for 9 months shares challenges while detained
articles.summary: An Edmonton-born man who spent months in ICE detention is back in Canada, where he is now sharing his story about the conditions and hurdles he faced while detained. Curtis Wright, 40, who spent most…

image.caption: Curtis Wright, centre, his fiancée Kayla Thomsen and their daughter are pictured in this undated handout photo. Wright was recently returned back to Canada from the U.S. on a removal order after being detained by ICE for the past nine months. (Kayla Thomsen/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: An Edmonton-born man who spent months in ICE detention is back in Canada, where he is now sharing his story about the conditions and hurdles he faced while detained.

Curtis Wright, 40, who spent most of his life living in the United States, was held by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Texas for nine months after returning from a business trip to Mexico in November.
Wright said the reason he was detained stems from a misdemeanor drug possession charge from when he was 17 years old.
Wright said he was motivated to fight to remain in the U.S to try to be with his two young sons from a previous marriage, aged 8 and 11, who are in Texas.
Wright said he was returned to Canada in mid-August, and is temporarily staying at his parents’ house in Kelowna, B.C., with his fiancée, Kayla Thomsen, and their two-year-old daughter.
In an interview with Edmonton AM on Monday, Wright detailed the challenges he faced while struggling to remain south of the border.
This interview has been edited for length and clarity.
LISTEN | Curtis Wright ends up back in Canada after months in ICE detention:
Edmonton AM10:57Edmonton born Curtis Wright is back in Canada after nine months in ICE detention centres in the U.S.
What happened when you returned to Texas after a work trip to Mexico?
When I was going through Immigration and Customs, they asked me to go into secondary screening, which isn't uncommon. I've been through that before, but this began pretty differently.
He right away asked me, “Were you charged with misdemeanor possession back in 2004?”
I said “Yes, I was.”
He said, “OK, make a text to one of your family members. Let them know that this is going to be a while because we're going to have to investigate this further.”
Once I did that, they brought me into a back interview room where I was interrogated almost as if I were on trial, like I had done something wrong at that moment.

Then once the interview was over, he said, “As of this moment, you're now being detained. You'll be taken to a federal facility, and you won't have a court date until Dec. 3rd.” And this was on Nov. 6.

From that point, they moved me to a separate room and then from there they shackled me, put the waist chains around me, handcuffed me to my waist, put on ankle shackles, as if I was some kind of murder convict, and had me wait in a cell then took me to the facility.

items: 12 international students at Calgary protest referred to CBSA office after status check
On America's northern border, the threats are not unidirectional

blocks.text: Has anything like this ever happened to you previous to this encounter?

Never. I've gone in and out of the U.S. probably over 100 times since this has happened. I came to Kelowna to visit my parents at their home just this last summer just a few months before this detainment.
I was under the impression that they were focusing on the worst of the worst, like gang members, and people of that nature. I didn't realize that they were going to be detaining me.

items: Canadian man stuck in ICE detention centre for 4 months, awaiting deportation hearing

blocks.text: What options did they give you about what could happen next?
Really nothing. The guy informed me that because I was being federally detained there's no bond available to me because they marked me as a visiting alien reentering the country.
I was told later that if ICE had grabbed me in the country, I would have been able to get a bond potentially so I could fight my case outside.
But they purposely marked me as a visiting alien so that I couldn't get a bond. And then he said, “You're just going to have to go through the court case.” So that's essentially what I did.
Then that took this whole nine-month process to go through that court case?
They keep pushing your court case back because the whole idea behind it is they want you to give up. They don't want you to fight your case.

They put you in these horrible facilities and treat you very, very poorly, and they continue to push your court cases back. So you think you're going to court and then they say, “No, actually it's going to be in another three weeks. Oh wait, no, it's going to be in another two weeks.” Because they want you to give up and just go home.

items: Canadian who was held in ICE facility for months back in detention despite judge's ruling rights were violated

blocks.text: How many times did that happen to you where they pushed it?
For my first court date, it happened four times. I was originally scheduled to have it on Dec. 3 but didn't end up having it until Jan. 16.
After about five months, I finally went through the court case process and lost.

You’re supposed to get three dates and your third date is your trial date where a judge renders a decision. But I didn’t even get the opportunity to fight my case. On my second court date, they just said “Order of removal.”

Then I appealed after that and we tried to get a federal release through a writ of habeas corpus. The whole idea behind that was to get out so I could fight outside, and then we'd continue to do continuances and continuances and continuances waiting for the next political regime or hopefully winning my appeal. But I was never given the opportunity to do that.

items: How the U.S. secures its northern border
Canada's immigration 180: Part 1

blocks.text: You were fighting to be released back into Texas. That's where you called home. I understand that's where some of your family is as well?
The main reason that I was fighting to stay in Texas is because I have two sons with a previous wife.
I knew if I went to Canada they wouldn't be able to come with me. At the time I had 50/50 possession, so I got them half the year.
I fought because I wanted to stay in my children's lives as much as I possibly could, so that's why I stayed for nine months until we exhausted every option.

We had Republican senators write in asking for my release. We had Democrat senators write in asking for my release. We had Texas state representatives, even one individual who was on the board of commissions for Texas State prisons and detention centres, he wrote to ICE, the federal courts, the immigration courts. They all did.

Then I fought my case and we tried federal release. We went to the media. I exhausted every option because, to me, it was important to leave with no regrets, knowing that I did everything I could to stay with my boys. And that one day when I have to tell them why Dad had to leave, I can tell them with honesty that, “Your father did everything he possibly could.” But it just didn't work out.

items: How Trump’s mass deportation plan became big business

blocks.text: Can you tell us about what you experienced over those nine months in those centres?

It's the hygiene side of it. There's dirt, mould and grime everywhere. Everything's run down. I mean, you're sharing a small bathroom and showers with 100 men. There are a hundred men in the dorms. The food is just abysmal.

But more than that, it’s the officers that are there in place to be security for you. They yell at you. They curse at you. They threaten you. Solitary confinement is always one of their biggest threats, or moving you to different dorms or taking away privileges.

The lights are on 24 hours a day. You're sleeping in a steel bunk bed with no pillow. You're asked to be counted in your bed five times a day, and it's almost like a psychological and emotional beatdown.

Because, as I mentioned before, they want to make things as uncomfortable as they possibly can for you because they want you to give up and just go back to your home country. You feel like you're less than human.

items: How ICE detention is forcing immigrants out of the U.S.

blocks.text: When did you finally decide to be deported to Canada?
I finally made that decision about eight months in, and then it took about another month to get out.

Because my lawyer had informed me that in the federal courts there's an ongoing case right now pertaining to permanent residence and due process, and that the judge that had my habeas corpus for a federal release was waiting on the ruling of that case, and it had already been ongoing for several months.

The lawyer said the case “could go on for two more weeks or it could go on for two more years. So, you could wait another year, year and a half, let’s say, and then the ruling goes against permanent residents. And then you can’t get release on that anyways.”

items: Canada's immigration 180: Part 2

blocks.text: At that point, I realized it was just the best thing for my family because even though I'm the one locked up in there, my whole family's going through it. I feel like we were all stuck in this terrible, terrible nightmare.
I thought it was important for the whole family that we just kind of move on and find a way to just move forward with our lives the best way we can and accept what is, and so that's what we're doing.
But again, I love Canada and there was no concern about coming back here. It was simply trying to stay there for my sons.
What are your next steps from here?

My career has been in oil and gas and so, being from Edmonton, it's kind of a perfect spot to pick that right back up. Thankfully, my company that I was working for before in Houston, is going to be opening up a Canadian division just for me to run and try to grow here in Canada.

I've had a lot of wonderful people in my corner, including my employer, and they're going to continue to stick by me and most of my family is in Edmonton — all my aunts, uncles, cousins, my brother and his wife and children are there.
